docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast, per site, in points of capacity. BG2 at Primaries ranges from -3.01 (Primary K) to +0.09, with all but Primary K and Primary I (-1.96) within -0.9 to +0.1. The simplest candidate ranges from -3.99 to +0.46. manual_heuristic has the same shape (-3.11 at Primary K). At farms the gap is -1.4 to -2.2 at solar and -5.4 to -7.6 at wind for both BG2 and the lag-free forecast, so removing the lags shifts it by less than 0.6 points. The supply points range from -5.9 to +3.9 for BG2 and from -5.5 to +1.7 for manual_heuristic.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each score contrast. C1 +1.084 (0.648 to 1.717), C2 +0.241 (0.030 to 0.494), C3 +0.041 (-0.043 to +0.121), C4 -0.055 (-0.165 to +0.050), all 95%; the lag-only contrast with Primary M cut is +0.509 (0.333 to 0.713) weekly. The error of the median forecast agrees in sign with every score contrast except the spread-factor contrasts and the BG2 reproduction, whose median changes by under 0.001. For C5 at the offset Primaries at midday in summer, the median error changes by -0.246 (-0.362 to -0.148).
  • Triggers fired. An Opus audit and code review of this page are in the private folder data/ml-experiments/briefs/ (dp_pr1345_numbers_audit_result.md and dp_pr1345_code_review_result.md). They found no leakage, reproduced every number, and left the verdict unchanged. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction): the lag cost of 0.806 is above the predicted 0.05 to 0.30, and the explanation is Primary M's uncut commissioning months plus Primary K's level change, tested by the refits above. The farm lag costs (+0.010, -0.059) and the offset gain (-0.184) also fall outside their predicted ranges (0.10 to 0.50 and 0.05 to 0.15), in the direction of a smaller cost and a larger gain. Trigger 4 (leaving a site out flips a planned contrast): leaving out solar farm E turns C3 from not shown safe into safe. Trigger 5 (a nested arm beats the arm that contains it): wind farms without lags score below wind farms with lags, inside the interval. Trigger 7 (a later design depends on the result): the differentiable-physics series briefs quote the lag cost, so they should quote the lag-only cost with Primary M cut. Trigger 6 does not fire, because experiment 87 has no comparable contrast. Triggers 1 and 3 did not fire.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Other late-starting series are uncut. Only D18 was refitted with its start cut. The other late starters in data-processing.md have shorter cuts (0.8 to 5.6 months) and were not cut here.
  • The two Primary substations are named after the fact. Primary K and Primary M were identified by the per-substation table, so the leave-out intervals are exploratory.
  • The best pair and best triple are exploratory. Their numbers decide no verdict.
  • Blend weights differ between arms. The offset contrast C5 and the "without the 14-day correction" contrast compare blends that each choose their own monthly weights, so each includes a small weights effect.
  • The example weeks are not matched to the weather. The summer week has the highest mean power, not the sunniest sky.
  • Not run. The curtailment-cost metric (it needs the private node table), a no-lag blend, an offset on no-lag models, and a seed noise floor for the small farm contrasts C3 and C4. The reference arms are scored on fewer rows than BG2 (climatology lacks 4.7% of Primary rows), so the absolute table compares arms on slightly different rows; every contrast is paired.
  • Selection bias. The BG2 recipe was tuned on the same validation year, so every simplification is judged against an optimistic reference.
  • Next. Test whether a level term (the last observed daily mean, say) can replace the three lags; repeat the farm lag removal on a second year and more farms; and give the supply points a lag-free alternative only if a level input can replace the lags.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, part 1: which substations, rows, and dates the model can use
docs.text:
The data lets the differentiable-physics series go ahead, with three changes. Start 13 of the 16 Primary substations later than their first record, fix the lockdown window in advance, and count eligible long-history MW sites at each tuning year's first day (5 at 2024-07-01, because D9 holds only 9.0 months then). Verdict: supported, exactly at the minimum of 5 eligible sites, so Part 2's tuning contrast needs 4 of 5 sites to improve. A sharper timestamp check, on the sunrise and sunset ramps of metered photovoltaic (PV) series, finds no 30-minute error on either side of the fix.

This experiment fits no model. It looks at the power records that National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) supplied for 22 series (16 Primary substations, four grid or bulk supply points, and two metered generators), at ERA5 temperature (the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' fifth-generation reanalysis) and CAMS irradiance (the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service), both estimates of past weather, and at 66 hand-filtered switching events. It decides which substations, rows, and dates the later parts can use.

A Primary substation is the transformer site that feeds a town or district. A MW Primary reports net power in megawatts, and an MVA Primary reports apparent power in megavolt-amperes, which cannot show reverse flow. A dark row is a half-hour with CAMS irradiance below 1 W/m², and only dark rows show an MVA Primary's demand alone. A site-year is 17,532 half-hours. Power is shown as a percentage of each series' effective capacity.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: Figures 4, 12, and 13 carry the findings. Figures 1 and 2 show the raw data, figures 3 and 5 to 8 test the planned modelling choices, and figures 9 to 11 test the generator screen, the timestamp correlation, and the MVA dark rows. The two metered generators appear only in figure 9, as G-a and G-b, as aggregate statistics with no dates.

docs.title: Sites and dates
docs.text:
• Roles (sites.parquet): mw_long for D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16; mw_short for D18; generator_case for D15; mva_dark for D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22; excluded for D1, D6, D13, D17, G-a, and G-b.
  • First usable dates come from a per-series review of every series' start, made for the differentiable-physics series, which Part 1 may only move later: D4 2021-05-01, D14 2020-07-01, D12 2020-05-01, D5 2020-02-01, D3 2020-01-01, D10 and D21 2019-12-01, D22 2019-11-01, D19 2019-10-15, D16 2021-02-01, D9 2023-10-01, D18 and D15 2025-03-01, and 2019-09-17 at D2, D8, and D11.
  • D12 keeps the rule's later date. The review recommends no cut, and the 15-point rule cuts 7.4 months (figure 4), so D12 starts 2020-05-01.
  • Months before a tuning year's first day (2022-07-01, 2023-07-01, 2024-07-01, 2025-07-01): the six long-history sites hold 12 or more months before 2025-07-01 (D9 21.0). Five hold 12 or more before each of the other three days. D9 holds 9.0 months before 2024-07-01.
  • Dark site-years per MVA Primary: 2.43 to 3.27 over all history, 2.34 to 2.68 with the lockdown window removed (20.1 in total), and 0.88 to 0.95 in 2023-07 to 2025-06, Part 3's training window. The share at 16:00 to 21:59 local time is 27.3%, 27.9%, and 27.2% in those three windows.
  • Row sets: dp_mw_v1 holds 508,341 half-hours and dp_mva_dark_v1 holds 352,841 dark half-hours (rows.parquet; rows in the lockdown window or under a switching mask are flagged and left out of both).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Early-calibration rule. The rule drops leading months while the night band (00:00 to 04:59) or the weekday daytime band (09:00 to 16:59) differs by more than 15 percentage points from the same month a year later. It cuts D14 9, D12 8, D15 8, D4 3, D18 2, and 1 month at D9, D16, D21, and D22 (figure 4).
  • Generator screen (negative dark share above 1%, run after cuts and masks on MW series only). It flags D1 (73%), D6 (26%), D15 (82%), G-a (62%), and G-b (65%). It leaves the other 15 Primaries unflagged, among them D18 (0% after its cut, 1.8% before it with 201 of 202 negative rows in January 2025), and the bulk supply points D13 (0%) and D17 (0.09%). The MVA Primaries go unscreened.
  • Timestamp. The clear-sky-hours correlation with irradiance is most negative between 0 and +30 minutes (parabola vertex +10.6 minutes before the fix and +6.9 after), and the plan's summer-midday test is flat (about -0.18 and -0.06), so neither locates an offset; the follow-up below bounds it.
  • Clip (daytime power flattening above a ceiling): yes at D5 (4 of 7 summers) and D15 (2 of 2), and no at the other six MW Primaries; D14 meets the rule in 1 of 6 summers.
  • Heating-slope drift is not detectable. No long-history site has a last-minus-first winter difference whose 95% interval excludes zero (D9's runs from -0.06 to +0.26 points per °C). The test uses the interval of the difference, which is stricter than the plan's non-overlap test.
  • Lockdown window. The differentiable-physics series brief fixes it at 2020-03-23 to 2021-07-19. A window detected from the data would not work: in April 2020 D11 sits 26 percentage points below a no-lockdown fit and D10 7, but from August 2020 to September 2021 the four sites with 2019 history sit mostly 5 to 17 percentage points above it (figure 12). The fit leaves similar excursions in months it was fitted on, so the departures show a poor fit as much as drift.
  • Correlation of monthly levels across D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16: the mean pairwise correlation is 0.56 for the night band (60 months) and 0.46 for the evening band (17:00 to 20:59; 59 months), and the first principal component holds 66% and 58% of the variance (figure 8).
  • Switching masks. 28,543 half-hours on the full grid are masked on the 16 Primaries, 26,763 of them in rows with data, the most at D5 (5,202) and the least at D2 (113). Each mask runs from 24 hours before the onset to 24 hours after the end. The 66 events start in 2022-03, so no mask precedes then.

docs.title: Timestamp follow-up
docs.text:
• Method. On clear-sky days, the half-hour-to-half-hour change of net power while the sun is between -3 and 25 degrees above the horizon is matched to the change of a sun-height predictor shifted by a trial offset, from -120 to +120 minutes in 5-minute steps. The best offset comes from the smallest residual sum of squares, with a slope of the physically expected sign, and a 95% interval comes from resampling whole days 1,000 times.
  • Orientation effect removed. A fixed south-facing panel makes the morning ramp read late and the evening ramp early (at the PV series the morning ramp reads 80 to 140 minutes later than the evening ramp reads early, which is twice the half-difference of 40 to 70 minutes). A stamp error moves both the same way, so the stamp offset is the mean of the morning and evening offsets.
  • The ingest's 30-minute correction has the right direction and size, to within 3 minutes. At the 6 metered PV series (aggregate only, no names, identifiers, or dates), the stored stamps before 2026-03-26 08:30 UTC run +0.9 minutes late (series from -0.2 to +2.9; intervals within -2.7 to +5.0). The feed as NGED sent it ran 30 minutes later than the stored stamps, so the feed read about 31 minutes late.
  • After the fix. The PV series' median offset is +4.7 minutes (+1.5 to +13.3; intervals -5.3 to +20.0) on April to 10 September 2026 (34 to 47 clear days each). The like-for-like April to September rows before the fix give +2.0 (-3.3 to +5.4), so the two sides do not differ.
  • MW Primaries. Only D5 and D18 give a usable fit; at the other six a ramp hits the 100-minute search limit because demand ramps dominate. D5 gives +7.4 (3.1 to 11.3) minutes in April to September before the fix and +8.1 (1.9 to 15.5) after; D18 gives +17.6 (11.5 to 24.4) and +12.3 (4.4 to 20.0). D5 and D18 both run 5 to 15 minutes above the PV series, which the demand ramps can explain, and neither D5 nor D18 is near 30.
  • No 30-minute error is confirmed on either side. A residual of about 0 to +8 minutes is possible and agrees with the correlation vertex, but the method cannot separate it from panel and horizon effects, and offsets at the Primaries are not resolved beyond that range. The residual touches no Part 2 arm, because the CAMS and ERA5 joins work on the half-hour and hourly grid and are unchanged by a few minutes.
  • Limits. The PV series lie in one area, the after side holds under 50 clear days, and the only known-answer check is the 30-minute correction, which gives a sign test.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• Held: the six sites hold 12 months or more before 2025-07-01 and D18 fewer; about 27% of dark half-hours fall at 16:00 to 21:59; the screen flags D1, D6, D15, G-a, and G-b and none of the other 15 Primaries; heating-slope drift is not detectable.
  • Failed: the clear-sky-hours correlation peaks at zero per site at only 1 of 8 sites before the fix and 5 of 8 after (the ramp check below finds no offset near 30 minutes); D14 and D15 are cut, but 13 Primaries start later than their first record, not 2, and the early-calibration rule alone cuts 9 (D14, D12, D15, D4, D18, D9, D16, D21, and D22); the MVA Primaries hold 2.43 to 3.27 dark site-years with the lockdown kept (24.3 in total), and 6 of 8 are below 3.2; D15's winter night slope is +0.48 points per °C, not within ±0.1; clip is at D5 and D15, not D5 only.
  • Superseded: the lockdown prediction, now a fixed window.

docs.title: Data validation
docs.text:
• Keys and values: no duplicate (series, time) keys, no NaN power, no null irradiance or temperature to 2026-06-30, and no MVA value below zero.
  • Stuck runs of 12 or more identical half-hours, and zeros outside the substation_zero flag: found only at the two metered generators.
  • Month-mean steps over 3 monthly standard deviations: D11 (2020-04), D2, D4, D12, D18, D19, D21, and D6, a grid supply point whose monthly mean falls 218 MW in 2023-07.
  • Scarce days (mean per long-history MW site): 3.8, 5.0, and 3.5 cold days (daily-mean temperature below 0 °C) in 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26, and 12.0 in November 2022 to February
  • A full year holds 8 bank holidays, and the Christmas run (24 December to 1 January) holds 9 days.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• ERA5 and CAMS estimates of past weather flatter the PV term (experiment 46).
  • The switching masks and the early-calibration cuts are hindsight decisions: each cut compares months with a year later, and the masks come from labels written after the events.
  • Four sites decide the lockdown figure, and D14 enters only from July 2020.
  • The D9, D16, and D18 first-month cuts rest on very few readings.
  • Every printed number is in report.txt.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Part 2 should use the site list above and count eligible long-history sites at each tuning year's first day, as the maintainer decided; this gives 5 eligible sites at 2024-07-01 (4 of 5 needed), where counting at 2025-07-01 would give 6 (4 of 6). All 8 MVA Primaries clear the 0.5 dark site-year entry rule in Part 3's window. The shared slow factor in the differentiable-physics design is worth keeping, given the correlations above.

docs.title: Review triage
docs.text:
• Accepted and fixed: the switching mask now includes the onset half-hour and ends at end_utc; first usable dates follow the per-series review of series starts; default_rows leaves out the lockdown and masked rows (in_pool stays the pool membership); D15 and D17 no longer use data or cuts that conflict with the review; the generator tables and report no longer print dates, and figure 9 sets aria=False; Part 3's window is 2023-07 to 2025-06; the July 2026 half-hour no longer enters the monthly levels; the correlations and census use rows after the cuts (and, for the correlations, the masks); rows.parquet carries early_cut; sites.parquet carries the clip and generator flags; decisions.json carries the cut dates, screen flags, dark counts, and masks.
  • Accepted as caveats: the maintainer decided not to stop the series and to run the sharper timestamp check above, the summer-midday test is reported beside the clear-sky one, and the eligibility count is the maintainer's.
  • Not changed: the heating-drift test and the one-criterion generator screen differ from the plan, and both follow the differentiable-physics series brief or are stricter.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, part 2: a simple structural model of demand and solar
docs.text:
A simple model of demand minus solar forecasts better than lagless XGBoost on 12 months of history, but more years of history do not clearly help it. This is part 2 of a six-part series on models built from physical terms (a daily profile, holidays, heating, and solar output) and fitted by gradient-based optimisation; part 3 pools the model across substations. Trained on 12 months, the model scored 0.25 points better than lagless XGBoost with its default start (post hoc; a lower score is better). Only the contrasts C1 to C3 were pre-registered; the others below are exploratory. The arm names (G1, G-all, G-all+D1, X-12, and so on) are defined in the first Results bullet. Trained on all usable years with no drift, the model scored 0.25 points worse than on 12 months in the scored year (exploratory; +0.03 without D16, and the reverse in the tuning year), and a drift term recovered that. The planned comparison C1, all years with drift against 12 months, gave 0.04 points better, with an interval from 0.30 better to 0.21 worse, and 2 of the 5 decision substations improved.

The verdict is inconclusive. The interval of C1 spans zero, and four of the five pre-registered positive controls fail. The framework tests, which the plan names as the fifth control, pass. The four that fail are these: old years without drift hurt by less than predicted (+0.25 against +0.3 to +0.8); the solar offset gains nothing once irradiance is an input; the zero start scores worse than the default start; and the baselines are not worse than every arm. On C1 alone, the merged rule for the first scoring pass would give partly supported.

The result narrows the long-history question to "all years need a drift to be level with 12 months in the scored year, and the data cannot yet say whether they gain". In this page, "history-window contrasts" means all years against 12 months, and drift against no drift. By substation the planned comparison is mixed: D14 (-0.51) and D11 (-0.22) improve, and D10 (+0.41), D5 (+0.11), and D16 (+0.03) worsen.

The model was fitted once per Primary substation on data to 30 June 2025 and scored on the next 12 months. We fitted the model, one convex optimisation (a problem with a single best answer) per Primary substation, on data to 30 June 2025, held the fit fixed, and scored the model on every half-hour from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026. The score is twice the mean pinball loss (an error measure for quantile forecasts) over 11 quantile levels, in points of effective capacity (1% of the substation's effective capacity, the scale every experiment divides power by). The five decision substations are D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16; D9 has 9.0 months of history at 2024-07-01 (experiment 103's row table) and is reported beside them. ERA5 (a reanalysis) and CAMS (a satellite-based irradiance product) supply temperature and irradiance; both are estimates of past weather.

docs.title: Correction (2026-10-19)
docs.text:
The first version of this page reported the opposite sign for two history-window contrasts (all years against 12 months, and drift against no drift), because the forecast spread carried last year's mean bias into the scored year. An audit found no bug in the fits. The fault was in the design of the spread: each quantile was the fitted mean plus the raw quantiles of the residuals of a replica fitted 12 months earlier, and the raw quantiles carry that replica year's mean bias, which shifted every quantile of the scored year by the same amount. The shift of the median forecast from the mean forecast ranged from -21.3 points (D9, G-all+D1+steps) to +3.6 points (D11, G-all+D1), and fully explains D9's former scores of 6.39 and 15.67. The spread is now centred: each (hour band, calendar quarter) group's median is subtracted from its quantiles (ResidualSpread.fit(centre=True), with a test that fails if the quantiles are not centred). The fits, the penalties, and the XGBoost arms are unchanged. The first run's sets stay in the store under their original names (g1, g_all, and so on) as the uncentred arm; the corrected sets are g1_centred and so on. report_uncentred_first_run.txt holds the first run's report, and E104_SPREAD=uncentred makes e00104_report.py reproduce it.

Quantity (five decision substations) First run (uncentred) Corrected (centred) G-all minus G1 -0.40 (-0.66 to -0.15) +0.25 (+0.08 to +0.40) C1: G-all+D1 minus G1 (98.33%) -0.20 (-0.68 to +0.22) -0.04 (-0.30 to +0.21) G-all+D1 minus G-all +0.20 (-0.05 to +0.43) -0.29 (-0.37 to -0.21) C2: G1 minus X-12am (98.33%) -0.24 (-0.80 to +0.24) -0.55 (-1.13 to -0.11) C3: G-all+D1 minus X-allam (98.33%) -0.29 (-0.67 to +0.03) -0.43 (-0.75 to -0.15) G-all minus X-12 -0.34 (-0.66 to -0.07) +0.00 (-0.40 to +0.34) Absolute: G1, G-all, G-all+D1 3.13, 2.73, 2.92 2.82, 3.07, 2.78 D9, G-all+D1 and G-all+D1+steps 6.39, 15.67 2.31, 2.63
  • What changed in the conclusions. More years without drift now hurt, in the direction the positive control predicted but below its predicted size of +0.3 to +0.8, where the first run said they helped by 0.40. C1 kept its sign and shrank from -0.20 to -0.04. Drift now helps the score in every month of the scored year (-0.07 to -0.51), where the first run said it lost most in August to October. The convex model's lead over XGBoost with the zero-start benchmarks is larger (C2 -0.55, C3 -0.43), and G-all is level with X-12, not 0.34 better.
  • The bias as its own result. Uncentred minus centred, five-site score: G1 +0.30, G-all -0.35, G-all+D1 +0.14, G-all+D1+steps +0.13 (report section 12). The replica year's bias helped one arm and hurt three, and the sign differed between substations, so it was a shift by chance, not a usable correction. Whether the replica year's bias predicts the scored year's bias was not tested beyond these four arms.
  • What did not change. The zero-start result (+0.30), the solar offset with irradiance (+0.006), the lagged reference, the cold block, the capacities, and the GPU benchmark are unaffected, because they do not use the spread. The tails are not fixed by centring: G-all+D1 covers 2.5%, 6.9%, 89.5%, and 96.2% at the 1%, 5%, 95%, and 99% quantiles, and pooled coverage hides opposite errors between substations.
  • D10's unlabelled jumps. The audit reported 15 to 20 point jumps in D10's power from about 8 November 2024 and about 1 November 2025, probably unlabelled switching. We found the first on 8 November 2024 (the night-time floor rises from 25 to 45 points and stays high to about 1 December), inside the training data, which this correction does not remove from any fit. We found the second as a rise of 15 to 20 points in D10's residuals from 17 November to 14 December 2025, not on 1 November. With those 28 days dropped at D10 only (1,344 of 17,401 rows), D10's scores fall by 0.09 to 0.53 (G1 3.19 to 3.04, G-all+D1 3.60 to 3.44, X-12am 3.90 to 3.37), and the five-site contrasts move by under 0.08 (report section 13): G-all minus G1 +0.24, C1 -0.05, G-all+D1 minus G-all -0.29, C2 -0.47, C3 -0.41, G-all minus X-12 +0.05. No conclusion changes.

docs.title: What the model learns
docs.text: The mean forecast is the sum of seven pieces, each a block of the design matrix times its fitted coefficients. The figures split the fitted G-all+D1 model (final cut 2025-07-01, centred spread, which plays no part in a mean) at three decision substations, D10, D11, and D14, in points of effective capacity. The pieces add up to the model's mean forecast (checked in the script to 1e-6 points). The steps panel comes from the steps arm and is not zero: its cumulative steps reach +20 points at D10 and -10 points at D11 over the training years.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per site. Zero at every site in the centred sets. In the first run's uncentred sets the mean shift of the median forecast, on all rows, was G1 +1.8, +3.1, -1.7, +2.3, +2.2, and +1.2 points at D10, D11, D14, D16, D5, and D9 (report section 12).
  • Error of the mean or median forecast beside each contrast (report section 14; mean absolute error of the GAM mean and of the XGBoost median, five sites). G1 4.93, G-all 5.24, G-all+D1 4.85, steps 4.95; X-12 5.01. G-all minus G1 +0.31 (+0.01 to +0.56); C1 -0.08 (-0.46 to +0.28); G-all+D1 minus G-all -0.38 (-0.52 to -0.25); C3 -0.43 (-0.73 to -0.16). All four agree in sign with the quantile score.
  • C2's lead lies mostly in the tails and the spread, not the centre. C2, G1 minus X-12am, is -0.08 (-0.40 to +0.20) on the error of the mean forecast against -0.55 on the quantile score.
  • Leaving one decision site out (report section 14). C1 changes sign without D14: -0.04 with all five sites, +0.08 without D14 and +0.01 without D11, and between -0.16 and -0.06 without D5, D10, or D16. C2 and C3 stay between -0.65 and -0.24 whichever site is left out. G-all minus G1 stays positive, between +0.03 (without D16) and +0.42 (without D14). G-all+D1 minus G-all stays negative, between -0.38 and -0.09.
  • Audit triggers. The seven triggers are those of the "Audit before merge" rule in the ml-experiment skill, and each is defined below with whether it fired.
    • Trigger 1, a control fails: fired. Four positive controls fail. The audit of the spread (private brief e104_audit.md) found no code bug in the zero-start, solar-offset, or tail results. It found that zero start overfits (better in training; the 99% quantile covered 73% against 98% in the scored year, report section 5; experiment 80's -0.04 came from lagged, weekly-retrained models) and that the solar offset adds nothing once CAMS irradiance is an input.
    • Trigger 2, a result contradicts its prediction or an earlier finding without a tested explanation: fired, for the same two results, with the explanations above, and for the corrected history-window contrasts.
    • Trigger 3, the quantile score and the error of the mean forecast point in different directions: did not fire.
    • Trigger 4, leaving one site out flips a planned contrast: fired. C1 changes sign without D14, from D14's winter against D10's summer (see the section below; the second audit found no data or switching fault at D14).
    • Trigger 5, a nested arm beats the arm that contains it: fired. G1, trained on less data, beats G-all by 0.25 (the audit found no leak, and drift recovers the gap), and steps do not beat D1 (+0.08, interval spanning zero).
    • Trigger 6, a headline interval twice as wide or half as wide as in a sister experiment: did not fire. No sister experiment scores these rows.
    • Trigger 7, a later experiment depends on the unreplicated headline: fired. Later parts of the series use G-all+D1 as the reference and D1 plus steps as the default drift.

docs.title: The tuning year as a replicate
docs.text:
The tuning year reverses two of the three history-window contrasts, so a one-year contrast between history windows is not yet a finding. The three are G-all minus G1, C1, and the drift contrast. This replicate is post hoc: a second audit added it after the first results. The audit refitted the four convex arms at the 2024-07-01 cut with the same penalties and scored them on the tuning year, 2024-07 to 2025-06, on the mean absolute error of the mean forecast (five sites), so the spread plays no part. No intervals were computed for the tuning-year column, and the steps row is in-sample because the step penalty was chosen on that year.

Contrast (error of the mean forecast, points) Tuning year 2024-25 Scored year 2025-26 G-all minus G1 -0.25 (4 of 5 better) +0.31 C1: G-all+D1 minus G1 -0.20 (3 of 5 better) -0.08 G-all+D1 minus G-all (drift) +0.06 -0.38 G-all+D1+steps minus G-all+D1 -0.22 (in-sample) +0.10
  • Two contrasts reverse between years and only C1 keeps its sign. G-all minus G1 and the drift contrast reverse. C1 favours all years with drift in both years.
  • C1's sign rests on one site's winter against another site's summer. On the quantile score (not the error of the mean forecast), C1 is -0.40 in November to March and +0.19 in April to October (-0.19 and +0.25 without D14), and all years with drift beats G1 in winter at 4 of 5 sites in both years. D14's gain (-0.51) is all November to March (-1.17, against -0.04 in other months): G1 under-forecasts the cold weeks of January and February 2026 by 8 to 11 points, and D14's scored winter was 6.8 points higher than its training winter. D10's loss (+0.41) is a summer effect: all years with drift over-forecasts D10's falling summer level by 5 to 8 points (on the quantile score, +0.91 in April to October and -0.30 in winter).
  • G-all's scored-year loss to G1 is mostly D16. G-all is biased +3.5 points at D16, whose demand rose every year from 2022, and -1.6 at D10, whose demand fell. Without D16 G-all minus G1 is +0.03.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. Convex model (G): G1 (12 months, no drift), G-all (all years, no drift), G-all+D1 (all years, a drift level per hour band), G-all+D1+steps (D1 plus sparse steps). XGBoost (X) without power lags, same weather inputs, named by window (12 months or all years) and suffix: no suffix is XGBoost's default start, z a zero start, am a zero start plus experiment 64's solar offset, amq (post hoc) each quantile starting at its training quantile plus the offset, and ng (post hoc) no irradiance input. References: climatology and manual_heuristic. Penalties were tuned on 2024-07 to 2025-06 by mean absolute error (ridge 0.1, drift step 3,000, step penalty 300). Every fit is frozen at 30 June 2025 with no refits, and uses one seed (the screening tier of the series). The convex arms' quantiles are the fitted mean plus the centred residual quantiles of a replica fit (see Correction); every number below is from the centred sets unless it says "first run".
  • Absolute scores (points, five decision sites; figure 3 has every site). G1 2.82, G-all 3.07, G-all+D1 2.78, G-all+D1+steps 2.86; X-12 3.07, X-all 3.15, X-12amq 3.06; climatology 4.07, manual_heuristic 3.49. D9 scores 2.31 (G-all+D1) and 2.63 (steps); its former 6.39 and 15.67 were the uncentred spread's shift.
  • C1 (the verdict contrast): G-all+D1 minus G1 is -0.04 (98.33% interval, which corrects for three planned contrasts by the Bonferroni method: -0.30 to +0.21; 2 of 5 better). Per site: D14 -0.51, D11 -0.22, D16 +0.03, D5 +0.11, D10 +0.41. With D9 (six sites) it is 0.00 (-0.21 to +0.21).
  • C2 and C3 (labels under the merged rule, not a claim of a DP gain). C2, G1 minus X-12am: -0.55 (-1.13 to -0.11; 5 of 5 better; supported). C3, G-all+D1 minus X-allam: -0.43 (-0.75 to -0.15; 4 of 5 better, D5 worse; supported). Both compare against zero-start arms, which failed their own control and are the weaker XGBoost benchmark.
  • Against XGBoost's default start (post hoc, 95%, decision sites). G1 minus X-12: -0.25 (-0.53 to -0.01; 4 of 5 better). G-all minus X-12: +0.00 (-0.40 to +0.34; 3 of 5 better). G-all+D1 minus X-12: -0.28 (-0.74 to +0.09). G-all minus X-all: -0.08 (-0.21 to +0.06). G-all+D1 minus X-all: -0.37 (-0.54 to -0.20; 4 of 5 better). X-all is the weaker benchmark: it is 0.78 worse than X-12 at D16.
  • Exploratory (95%). G-all minus G1 +0.25 (+0.08 to +0.40; 2 of 5 better). G-all+D1 minus G-all -0.29 (-0.37 to -0.21; 4 of 5 better). Steps minus D1 +0.08 (-0.01 to +0.17). X-12z minus X-12 +0.30 (+0.16 to +0.47). X-12am minus X-12z +0.01 (-0.01 to +0.02): with irradiance as an input the offset adds nothing and the fitted weights w are -0.02 to -0.34, not -1. Without irradiance X-12am-ng minus X-12z-ng is -0.28 (-0.48 to -0.08), with w from -0.53 to -0.71. Coastal D5 and D9: C1 is +0.15 (+0.03 to +0.26, both worse).
  • Drift by month since the end of the training data. G-all+D1 minus G-all, July 2025 onward: -0.14, -0.09, -0.07, -0.40, -0.46, -0.51, -0.28, -0.44, -0.35, -0.13, -0.33, -0.32 (months 0 to 11). The drift arm is better in every month, and gains most from October to December. The drift step still sits at the edge of its grid (3,000), and D10's residuals rise at the end of the training data, so the last drift knot may still follow the final months of training.
  • Lagged reference (descriptive). XGBoost with three power lags minus the same model without: -0.58 (-0.97 to -0.28) at leads of 24.5 to 48 hours and -0.32 (-0.56 to -0.15) at 144.5 to 168 hours, 5 of 5 sites better in both. The lagged model scores 2.49 and 2.75 against 3.07, and so beats G1 (2.82) and G-all+D1 (2.78) at the shorter lead.
  • Tails (coverage at the 1%, 5%, 95%, 99% quantiles, five sites). G1 1.4/4.9/88.4/95.8%; G-all 2.9/6.7/83.4/92.8%; G-all+D1 2.5/6.9/89.5/96.2%; X-12 1.4/9.7/79.3/97.7%; X-12z 0.2/7.6/ 66.2/73.1%; manual_heuristic 4.2/6.1/90.6/93.3%. Pinball loss at the same levels: G1 0.177, 0.642, 0.819, 0.256; G-all+D1 0.195, 0.669, 0.772, 0.235; X-12 0.261, 0.716, 1.078, 0.338. The 95% quantile is too low for every arm from November to February, and pooled coverage hides opposite errors between substations (figure 7). No curtailment-cost saving is reported: that metric needs a node with generators, and this experiment scores Primary demand only.
  • Predictions that held: the plan's framework unit tests (1 to 6) pass; steps within 0.1 points of D1 (+0.08); run time (every arm under 10 minutes).
  • Predictions that failed: old years without drift hurt by +0.3 to +0.8 (+0.25: the direction and the interval above zero held, the size did not); solar offset with irradiance (no gain); zero start within -0.10 to +0.02 (+0.30); C1 in 0.0 to +0.4 (-0.04); C2 in 0.1 to 0.5 and C3 in 0.0 to 0.5 (-0.55 and -0.43, in the direction that favours the convex model); tails within 1 and 2 points of nominal (no arm); baselines worse than every arm at every site (14 arm-site pairs fail, listed in report.txt). The post-hoc no-irradiance offset gain is in range, but w is outside -1.3 to -0.6 at three sites. Capacities within 20% of the vintages: held at D10, mixed at D11 and D16, and D14 is not comparable.
  • Capacity. The real-time frozen vintage (the weekly capacity estimate of experiment 45 made with data to each origin date) is not its hindsight season-year constant; the two differ in every shared week. See data processing. No training row needed a growth-prior scaling, and the cold block has no real-time capacity before 2023-08, so it has no am arm.
  • Cold block (November 2022 to February 2023, a cold winter scored by fits trained to 31 October 2022; descriptive). Mean absolute error of the central forecast, five sites: G-all+D1 4.15, G-all 6.41, G1 7.66, X-12 7.31 points. The drift term helps most here, probably because it follows the 2022 fall in demand.
  • Scarce-data rows (no interval). Bank holidays (1,728 rows): G-all+D1 2.65, G-all 2.97, manual_heuristic 6.05. Days below 0 °C (576 rows): G-all+D1 3.37, G-all 3.40. Christmas run (1,009 rows): X-allam 2.46, G-all+D1 2.68.
  • GPU benchmark (private file work/benchmark.json). The pooled proxy ran 6.6 times faster on the GPU (221 s to 33.5 s); 20 stacked bootstrap fits 3.1 times (50.8 s to 16.4 s); one fit on six sites 2.1 times (3.3 s to 1.6 s). CPU and GPU predictions agree to 2e-9 points, and peak GPU memory was 0.87 GB. The two convex workloads run in float64, because the normal equations are too badly conditioned for float32. CPU timings ran while other jobs used the machine.
  • Handed on. The spread model is the centred replica residual quantiles. The strongest XGBoost benchmark is the default start (X-12, X-all), and X-12amq is the matching solar-offset arm. For Part 3, the references for pooling to beat are G-all+D1 (2.78), G1 (2.82), and G-all+D1+steps (2.86), and the tuning year should be scored as a second frozen replicate. For Part 4, the plan's rule gives D1 plus steps as the default drift, because steps lowered the tuning year's error by 0.22 points (over 0.1). That gain was measured on the year the step penalty was chosen on, and steps lost to D1 in the scored year (+0.08, mostly at D10). Part 4 should instead run D1 and D1 plus steps as paired arms, with D1 as the default, and choose the step penalty out of sample.

docs.title: Substation cards
docs.text:
Provisional: fitted to past weather on a screening run. Each card shows what the G-all+D1 fit says about one decision substation at the final cut 2025-07-01, and the steps panel comes from the steps arm. A card has nine panels. They show the unmetered PV capacity per season-year, the daily profile by day type, the drift held through the scored year, the heating response, the four smoothing-window slopes, the holiday and Christmas effects, the lighting effect, and the cumulative steps. The slope of the 6-hour window against the 168-hour window shows how quickly demand follows temperature. The capacity panels carry no interval, because the fit gives a point estimate only. Every axis is in points of effective capacity unless labelled.

  • What the cards show about the model's constraints. Each heating response is zero above 15.5 °C and rises as the temperature falls, the unmetered PV capacity never falls from one season-year to the next, and lighting is zero around midday. All three properties hold by construction (non-negative heating and capacity coefficients, and a lighting ramp that is zero at midday), so they check the plotting and not the fit.
  • What differs between substations (comparison figure). D10 has the steepest heating response (a slope of about 19 points per 10 °C, against 6 to 10 elsewhere) and the lowest weekday profile peak (about 60 points, against 65 to 76). Fitted capacity runs from about 2.3 MW (D10) to 3.6 MW (D14), and the evening-to-midday ratio of the weekday profile from about 0.73 (D10) to 0.90 (D5). These are fitted values from one frozen fit each.
  • Not shown. Capacity has no interval, the holiday panel averages the four hour bands, and the steps panel comes from a different fit (the steps arm).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• ERA5 and CAMS are estimates of past weather and flatter the solar term; a production forecast uses forecast weather.
  • The hand-filtered switching masks are hindsight labels shared by every arm. All-rows scores (report.txt) rank the arms the same way.
  • Each fit is held fixed for 12 months, so it is staler than a production model, which is refitted weekly. The spread is fitted on the year before the end of the training data, a year tuning also used, so it is slightly optimistic. The spread's centring assumes the replica year's mean bias does not carry into the scored year; the uncentred arm shows no systematic benefit from keeping it.
  • The decision set is five substations and 12 months, so intervals are wide.
  • The spread model changed after a first look at the results and an Opus code review (a replica fit instead of quarter-by-quarter fits), so C1 to C3 here use a different spread from the one pre-registered, and this experiment did not compute them under the pre-registered spread. The centring was added after an audit of the first results (see Correction). The post-hoc arms (amq, ng, X-all, X-12amq) were also added after that look. The verdict rule is unchanged.
  • Penalties were tuned on one year; the drift step sits at the edge of its grid.
  • Effective capacity is the project-wide constant per series used by every experiment.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Part 3 pools the model across substations on the GPU. A drift that re-estimates its level from recent data, for example by assimilating the latest observed demand, is one option for a later part. The corrected drift-by-month table says the existing drift helps in every scored month, but the tuning year reverses that, so the next question is whether drift and more years help in both years and in winter and summer alike. Part 3's pooling comparison should compare against G-all+D1, G1, and G-all+D1+steps, score the tuning year as a second frozen replicate, and split every contrast into November to March and April to October. Whether all years with drift beat 12 months remains open.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, part 3: one pooled demand model across substations
docs.text:
A pooled neural-network model of substation demand and solar output, fitted across 15 Primary substations, forecasts a brand-new substation well from 2 to 4 weeks of its own readings, and forecasts a substation with 2 years of history worse than a model fitted to that substation alone. By the series' pre-registered success rule (C2 or C3 supported, and C1 passing), pooling is not yet a success, because C1 is refuted. The practical finding beside it, chosen after seeing the results, is that the pooled model is much better than every per-site model fitted to the same 4 weeks or 3 months, a per-site convex model included, and worse at full history. Post hoc, a convex partially pooled model (experiment 109, whose own known-answer test is not yet passed) gets about the same onboarding gain on the six held-out substations (4.17 against 4.04 at 4 weeks, and 4.06 against 4.16 at 3 months) without the full-history loss (+0.03 against +0.385 here), which suggests the loss came largely from the neural fit. The page is provisional: it is a first screening run on past weather, and one of the four known-answer checks (gate test 2, the injected-farm recovery) failed, which caps the verdict at inconclusive.

We asked whether one model for many substations (the "pooled" model) forecasts a substation as well as a model fitted to that substation alone (the "per-site" model), and forecasts a new or short-history substation clearly better. Every model predicts a substation's demand minus its embedded solar output from the calendar, the temperature, and the sun, and is fitted by gradient descent (differentiable physics, "DP"). We scored each arm on the 12 months from 1 July 2025, with one frozen fit and no refits, on the five Primary substations with 2 years of history (D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16, the "decision substations") and on D9, which holds 21 months of that window. A lower quantile score is better. Pooling is judged by the forecast scores, not by the inferred solar capacity.

Terms used below.

  • C1 asks whether the pooled model is no worse than the per-site model, by more than 0.10 points, at the 5 decision substations with 2 years of history.
  • C2 asks whether the pooled model beats the per-site model for a substation with only 4 weeks of history, and C3 asks the same for 3 months. "Onboarding" a new substation means fitting only its own settings (its daily profile, heating slope, and PV capacity) to its first weeks of readings, with everything the other substations share held fixed.
  • Centred spread: the forecast interval is fitted from past forecast errors with their mean removed, so the interval sits around the mean forecast.
  • K is the number of shared daily shapes in the pooled model; nats are the unit of the training loss; the interaction network is the small neural network that lets the calendar and weather inputs interact; vintages are experiment 45's weekly estimates of each substation's PV capacity; coverage at a quantile is the share of readings below it.
  • Gate means four known-answer tests on synthetic or injected data whose right answer is known (section "Known-answer gate").

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Pooling is worse by 0.385 at full history and better by about 10 points at 4 weeks.

A per-site model fitted to only 4 weeks scores about 14 or worse; the pooled onboarding arm scores about 4. The five decision substations plus D9, in the order of the tables below.

Two to four weeks of history put a new substation within 0.8 points of full history.

The pooled model uses two shared daily shapes, and most substations sit wholly on one of them.

The pooled fit's capacities are lower than the convex model's at five of the six scored substations.

Each substation has its own daily profile and heating response.

The holiday effects and the mix of smoothed temperatures are shared by every substation.

Fixing the capacities near the convex values gives the lowest training loss.

  • C1, pooling on all rows (non-inferiority, margin +0.10): refuted. P minus S is +0.385 (98.33% interval +0.178 to +0.689); P is worse at 5 of 5 substations (D10 only +0.03), more in winter (+0.66) than in summer (+0.21). Leaving out any one substation leaves the estimate between +0.31 and +0.48, with the interval above zero. The error of the mean forecast says the same (+0.61).
  • C2, onboarding with 4 weeks: supported. The pre-registered contrast P-onb4w minus S-4w is −10.95 (98.33% interval −15.12 to −7.28) on the five decision substations, better at 5 of 5, and −10.34 (−14.57 to −6.65) with D9, better at 6 of 6. A per-site model fitted to only 4 weeks scores poorly everywhere, so S-4w is a weak comparator. The comparisons below are descriptive: X-4w is untuned and uses XGBoost's own quantiles, a departure from the plan, so it is a weak comparator too; P-onb4w minus X-4w is −7.10 (95% interval −10.98 to −3.38), better at 6 of 6. The onboarding curve on the six substations is 7.97 at 0 weeks, 4.06 at 2, 4.04 at 4, and 4.10 at 8; full-history P scores 3.27 on the same six, and P-onb4w minus P is +0.76 (0.32 to 1.20) on the five. P-onb4w only ties climatology fitted on the substation's full history (+0.12, −0.33 to +0.57) and is worse than the manual heuristic (+0.70, +0.23 to +1.19).
  • C3, short history of 3 months: supported. P-short3m minus S-3m is −1.09 (98.33% interval −2.01 to −0.34) on the five, better at 5 of 5, and −1.86 (−2.99 to −0.82) with D9, better at 6 of 6; D9 contributes −5.59 of the six-substation figure. Against X-3m it is −2.77 (−4.56 to −1.16), descriptive. P-short3m ties climatology on full history (+0.32, −0.46 to +1.21).
  • D18, with 4 months of history at the cut (descriptive, in no count): P 5.08, S 5.84, X-2y 8.44, P-all 5.32, S-all 5.93.
  • C4, the pooled model against lagless XGBoost (labelled, outside the verdict): P minus X-2y is +0.36 (+0.21 to +0.55), worse at 4 of 5 substations; the tuning-year winner among the XGBoost arms was not computed, so the contrast is shown against each (+0.36 for X-2y and X-2yq, +0.37 for X-2yamq). The per-site model S ties XGBoost (S minus X-2yq −0.02, −0.13 to +0.08).
  • C5, the pooled model on all years against Part 2's convex models (descriptive): P-all minus G-all+D1 +0.60 (+0.22 to +1.06), minus G1 +0.57 (+0.31 to +0.89), minus G-all +0.32 (−0.02 to +0.72). P-all minus S-all is +0.46 (+0.24 to +0.76), worse at 5 of 5. The pooled model does not clear Part 2's bar.
  • Ablations. P-map minus P +0.04 (+0.01 to +0.07); P-nonet minus P −0.03 (−0.14 to +0.07), so the interaction network adds nothing measurable. The solar offset adds nothing (X-2yamq minus X-2yq −0.01).
  • Tails (coverage at q01, q05, q95, q99; nominal 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, 0.99; five substations): P 0.015, 0.038, 0.798, 0.903; S 0.012, 0.035, 0.836, 0.927; P-onb4w 0.052, 0.104, 0.946, 0.982; P-short3m 0.031, 0.074, 0.891, 0.958; X-2y 0.015, 0.071, 0.788, 0.979; G1 0.014, 0.049, 0.884, 0.958; G-all+D1 0.025, 0.069, 0.895, 0.962. The pooled and per-site forecasts are too low in the upper tail (the 95% quantile covers 80% to 84%), which matters most for curtailment. Pinball losses at the four levels are in the stored report under data/ml-experiments/00105-*/.
  • Not run, for lack of time on a shared GPU: the cold block (a Nov 2022 to Feb 2023 test of heating extrapolation); the tuning-year replicate of the contrasts (the tuning year's mean scores point the same way for C1: P 3.197 against S 2.993 on 2024-25, without an interval); the scarce-data rows (bank holidays, the Christmas run, days below 0 °C); G-2y (the convex model on the same 2 years); X-pool-onb4w (one XGBoost fitted to the other substations plus the 4 weeks); a report of the lagged XGBoost arms; the coastal split; the score by month since the cut; the usable-row counts of each short history; the sunny-hour residual against temperature; a second-seed point of the capacity profile; the tuning-year winner of the XGBoost arms; the cards of the held-out onboarding substations; and the curtailment-cost metric.

docs.title: Predictions held and failed
docs.text:
• Held: P-map within ±0.1 of P (+0.04); P-nonet within ±0.15 of P (−0.03); the solar offset within ±0.05 (−0.01); P's q01 within 1 point of nominal (+0.5) and q05 within 2 points (−1.2); the signs of C2 and C3.
  • Failed: C1 within ±0.15 and spanning zero (+0.385); C2 of −0.5 to −2.0 (−10.95 on the five, −10.34 with D9; larger); C3 of −0.2 to −1.0 (−1.09 on the five, −1.86 with D9; larger); C4 of 0.0 to 0.4 better (0.36 worse); C5 within ±0.3 (+0.60 against G-all+D1) and P-all minus G1 of −0.3 to 0.0 (+0.57); onboarding within 0.5 of P (+0.76); P-all minus S-all within ±0.15 (+0.46); P's q95 and q99 within 2 and 1 points (0.798, 0.903); the onboarding and short-history tails; P's capacities within ±20% of the vintages' season-year mean at D10, D11, and D16 (season-year 2024: 30.6, 15.5, and 27.0 points against 43.2, 32.9, and 39.5: −29%, −53%, −32%); every arm under 10 minutes (S 10.6 minutes, S-all 17.4) and the whole screening under 2 hours (it took many hours on a shared GPU, with the gate re-run).

docs.title: Known-answer gate
docs.text:
Gate: failed (test 2). The plan made each test blocking and capped the verdict at inconclusive if one stayed failed, so the verdict carries the gate failure and no other number on the page is labelled. All gate tests ran with K = 4 shared shapes, before tuning chose K = 2, and test 1 runs P with the interaction network off.

  • Test 1, synthetic pooled recovery: passed, after four post hoc changes to the test (the model was not changed; the fitting settings were): 1200 optimiser steps at rate 0.15 (800 steps at rate 0.05 recovered the threshold within 7 degrees only), the true capacity placed in each substation's first trained season-year (the first version put it where no rows existed), the daily profile compared as the shape mix plus the per-site deviation after subtracting the mean profile (the plan said "loadings", which are not identified one by one), and D9 left out (its rows cover 9 months of the tuning window, giving a profile correlation of 0.85 against 0.91 to 0.99 for the others). The pass: threshold within 0.01 degrees, slopes within 0.3%, capacities within 1.2%, profile correlation at least 0.91, and the onboarded substation's slope within 1.2% where a per-site fit on the same 4 midsummer weeks missed it by 79%.
  • Test 2, injected-farm recovery: failed, narrowly. Real output of a solar farm is added to a substation's demand at the rows where the farm has a reading (about 30% of rows, night rows included), and the fit must recover it without moving other substations or the shared terms. The median recovered capacity ratio is 0.78 (limit 0.75 to 1.25); other substations' capacities move 2.0% to 5.2% (limit 5%; D10 breaches it); and the shared midday output moves 0.06, 0.07, 0.10, and 0.11 points at D10, D11, D14, and D16 (limit 0.1). The modules that move differ by substation (lighting at D10, the holiday effects at D14, the network at D16). A noise floor for this statistic was not measured. Refitting the base model with another seed changed the network, harmonic, and lighting outputs by 0.3 to 1.9 points (the holiday and tent outputs by 0.07 and 0.02), which suggests the 0.1 limit sits below the fit-to-fit noise, but that compares fits of different seeds, not the paired same-seed fits the test compares. The first version of the test, which filled missing farm rows with zeros, recovered 0.70 and moved the shared output 0.30 to 0.44 points. The weaker capacity prior planned for a retest was not run, because the prior does not bind (below).
  • Test 3, placebo twin: passed for three draws. The fit uses the same site's irradiance from 1, 2, and 3 years earlier in place of the real irradiance; the summer-midday error is worse and the fitted capacity falls at all 6 substations.
  • Test 4, shuffled capacity: passed, rebuilt as the series brief's Part 3 plan defines it (the plan page defined the prior-swap refit below; both definitions existed): swapping the fitted capacity paths in MW among the six substations worsens the summer-midday error at 6 of 6 (+0.8 to +11.4 points). The first version (swap the capacity prior and refit) was a different test and failed (2 of 4); it is kept as a diagnostic: the prior is a few nats against about 340,000 rows, so it cannot move a capacity that the data determine.
  • The free fit does not find the capacity that fits best. Capacity in points, season-year 2023, from the K = 4 diagnostic fit at the tuning cut (not the K = 2 decision arm), against Part 2's convex model and the vintage mean: D5 50.1, 58.9, 66.0; D10 34.6, 49.2, 39.5; D11 13.5, 31.3, 28.8; D14 24.7, 30.6, none; D16 24.1, 25.5, 32.9; D9 12.1, 30.4, none. A second seed moves a capacity by 0.2 to 2.7 points, starting at the convex capacities lands elsewhere (D5 29.7, D16 18.7, D9 22.9), with the network off D11 is 20.6 and D9 17.6, and a vintage-anchored prior with scale 5 changes nothing. The capacity profile (the last figure) fixes every substation's capacity at 0.5 to 1.3 times the convex capacity and refits the rest: the training loss is 774,009 nats at 0.5, 769,644 at 0.7, 767,187 at 0.85, 767,141 at 1.0, 771,197 at 1.15, and 776,076 at 1.3, a clear minimum near the convex capacity, flat within 46 nats between 0.85 and 1.0. The free fit's loss is 771,694 nats, 4,553 above the loss with the capacities pinned at the convex values (767,141). The data therefore carry information about capacity, between about −15% and +10% of the convex value (the profile is flat on the low side), and the free fit did not find the best capacity.
  • Why the free fit misses it is only partly tested. The pinned and free fits differ in their posterior sampling and in the Kullback-Leibler term. Three post hoc variants (screening tier, tuning cut, K = 4; the primary P is unchanged) were fitted: (a) hides the temperature from the interaction network by day, (c) starts the capacities at the convex path, and (a+c) does both. Training loss in nats: free fit 771,694, network off 777,200, (a) 768,292, (c) 777,050, (a+c) 774,771, against 767,141 with the capacities pinned. Variant (a) closed 3,402 of the 4,553 nats; the combined variant (a+c) did not, so the evidence is mixed. The variants' capacities are in work/diagnostics.json and the losses in work/variant_losses.json. None of the variants clears the leak test (gate test 2). (a) recovers 0.78 of the injected capacity and moves other substations' capacities by at most 3.2%, so it passes those two limits, and fails only the midday limit, with shared midday output moves of 0.07, 0.14, 0.16, and 0.18 points at D10, D11, D14, and D16. (c) recovers 0.53 (fails) and moves the midday output by 0.50, 0.20, 0.09, and 0.24 (fails), with other capacities moving by at most 3.5%. (a+c) recovers 0.54 (fails), moves other capacities by up to 6.7% (fails the 5% limit; the only variant to do so), and moves the midday output by 0.21, 0.22, 0.10, and 0.83 (fails), so it fails all three. Hiding temperature from the network therefore does not remove the leak, and starting at the convex capacities lowers the recovered capacity.

docs.title: Post hoc comparison with per-site convex and fleet-profile baselines on the same short history
docs.text:
• Mean absolute error of the mean forecast over the six scored substations (descriptive; the convex model's ridge tuned on the tuning year; no quantiles built): with 4 weeks, the pooled P-onb4w 6.88, a per-site convex model (Part 2's, no drift) 12.79, XGBoost's median 13.97, a fleet-profile baseline (the other substations' mean daily profile shifted to the substation's own 4-week level) 16.24, and the per-site neural model S-4w 20.06. With 3 months: P-short3m 7.07, per-site convex 8.46, XGBoost's median 8.99, S-3m 9.55, fleet profile 15.08.
  • Pooling therefore beats a per-site convex model fitted to the same history, not only the per-site neural model, by 5.9 points at 4 weeks and 1.4 at 3 months; the fleet-profile shift is worse than both. The neural pooled model is the only pooled model tested here; a pooled convex model, planned separately, would show whether the gain comes from pooling or from the neural form.

docs.title: Equivalence check
docs.text:
• The per-site neural model, configured like the convex model, does not reproduce its score. With no interaction network, no shared shapes, a weak penalty on the deviation, and the capacity pinned to the convex path, it scores 3.326 on all years against Part 2's G-all at 3.072 (+0.25, 0.12 to 0.41), worse at 5 of 5 substations, mostly D10 (+0.90; the others +0.05 to +0.12). The error of the mean forecast, which the spread does not touch, gives +0.60 (+0.43 to +0.78). The setup left the daily profile (48 half-hours by 4 day types) nearly unpenalised where G has a tuned ridge, so the gap is regularisation and optimisation, not a bug we found. S-all, with its shared shapes and network, scores 2.928, better than this setup.
  • Why P loses to S in C1 is therefore only partly explained: P-nonet minus P is −0.03, so the interaction network is not the cause, and the per-site model set up like G is 0.25 worse than G, mostly at D10.

docs.title: Tuning
docs.text: • Tuned on 2024-25 by quantile score (a fit before 2024-07-01 and a replica fit before 2023-07-01 for the spread): K = 2 shared shapes scored 3.197 against 3.255 for K = 4 and 3.207 for K = 6; the maximum a posteriori model's deviation scale 1.0 (3.235 against 3.319 and 3.280); the per-site model's 1.0 (2.993, 3.001, 2.993); the short-history per-site model's 1.0, by the error of the mean forecast. The short-history per-site models score about 14 points on the tuning year whatever the penalty.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• No leakage in the onboarding arms, by construction. Every fit (the final leave-one-out fits, the replica fits, the short-history fits) is trained only on rows ending at or before its cut, for every substation in the pool, and the pooled batch builder raises if a row ends after the cut. The final fits cut at 2025-07-01 and score from that instant; the replica fits cut at 2024-07-01 and their residuals cover only 2024-07-01 to 2025-07-01, so a held-out substation's scored rows never reach any fit's training rows. The caveat on the spread stays: the replica fits contain the other held-out substations' own rows before 2024-07-01.
  • Median forecast minus mean forecast, per site (points; P): D5 0.01, D9 −0.38, D10 −1.70, D11 0.81, D14 0.24, D16 0.16, D18 0.95. Every arm's spread is centred on the mean, so these gaps are skew, not shift (P-onb4w shows −0.42 to +0.14). D10's gap (−1.7) comes from its unlabelled switching windows.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside every contrast: C1 +0.61 (same direction), C2 −13.18 on the six (−13.86 on the five), C3 −2.48 on the six (−1.74 on the five), C4 worse, C5 worse. No contrast points the other way.
  • Audit triggers (the ml-experiment skill's list): fired for a failed control (gate test 2), for a result that contradicts its prediction (C1, whose explanation is only partly tested above), and for later designs that depend on this result (Part 4 and the pooled convex experiment). Not fired for a quantile-score contrast that disagrees with its mean-error contrast, for a contrast that flips sign when one substation is left out (P-all minus G1 is +0.33 without D16), for a nested arm beating the arm that contains it, or for an interval much wider or narrower than a sister experiment's.
  • Leave-one-out and season splits for every contrast, D10 with its 2025-11-17 to 2025-12-14 jump masked, and the error of the mean forecast are in the stored report; none flips C1, C2, or C3.

docs.title: Substation cards
docs.text: Provisional: fitted to past weather on a screening run. Figures 5 to 7 are the cards of the decision arm P: capacity per season-year (pooled fit with 80% posterior intervals, next to Part 2's convex model), the mix of shared shapes and the resulting daily profile per day type, the heating response (slope and threshold), and the holiday and thermal-inertia effects. Drift is absent from P. The vintage capacities of season-year 2024 are D5 62.1, D10 43.2, D11 32.9, and D16 39.5 points, against the pooled fit's 49.3, 30.6, 15.5, and 27.0. Three reading notes: the pooled neural fit's capacity follows its start (the loss has a minimum near the convex value, so the data pin it to between about −15% and +10%) and is not a measurement; the posterior intervals are far too narrow (the variational posterior stayed near its starting spread of 0.05, so they do not show the real uncertainty); and the shape mixes are close to 0 or 1 (K = 2 acts as two clusters: D4 and D8, two substations of the pool of 15, sit wholly on the second shape, D18 mostly, and D5 and D11 partly). The cards of the held-out onboarding substations were not drawn in this run.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
• Use the pooled model for onboarding and a per-site model for mature substations (a post hoc design reading, untested): the pooled neural model beats the per-site models fitted to the same 4 weeks or 3 months (mean absolute error 6.88 against 12.79 for a per-site convex model at 4 weeks, 7.07 against 8.46 at 3 months), and is worse at full history (C1 +0.385).
  • Fit the optimiser properly before drawing more from the equivalence gap (+0.25) and the capacity profile (4,553 nats above the pinned fit). A variable-projection fit, which solves all linear coefficients exactly with the bounded convex solver at each step and takes gradient steps only for the heating threshold, the thermal-inertia mix, the shape loadings, and the network weights, is planned separately and is the recommended next step.
  • Where does the pooled model lose at full history? C1 and P-nonet say the interaction network is not the cause. Test whether per-site heating and calendar terms on top of a shared fleet mean (the pooled convex model, planned separately) keep the onboarding gain without the full-history loss.
  • Can a new substation start from a pooled model and move to a per-site model as history grows? On the five decision substations, the onboarding curve is flat from 2 to 8 weeks at 4.1 to 4.3, against 3.0 for a per-site model with 2 years.
  • Fix the capacity fit before Part 5: the data pin the capacity to between about −15% and +10% and the free fit misses it, so profile the capacity out or fit it by a second-order method.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• ERA5 temperature and CAMS irradiance (the weather and sunshine estimates of past weather) flatter the solar term; the switching masks are hindsight labels; a frozen fit is staler than a production model, which is refitted weekly; five decision substations and one year give wide intervals.
  • The spread for a new substation uses the other substations' replica residuals, from fits that saw the new substation's rows before the replica cut (a new substation would not have them). The hyperparameters were tuned on a year that includes the held-out substation's history.
  • Both onboarding histories (April to June) are summer histories; a winter onboarding is untested.
  • Run time and memory: P 256 s (0.44 GB) including its replica fit; S 636 s; P-all 463 s (0.86 GB); S-all 1,045 s. The GPU was shared throughout.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, part 4: all years with drift, and recent-level assimilation
docs.text:
Correcting each day-ahead forecast with the demand errors the model made up to 3.5 hours earlier lowered the quantile score by 0.61 points in the scored year and by 1.02 points in the year before, at all five long-history Primary substations in both years. Scores are quantile scores in points of the substation's effective capacity (lower is better), and a negative difference means the first-named arm scored better. The scored year is 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026. With the filter running, a drift term added nothing measurable, and refitting every 4 weeks made the score slightly worse (0.06 points). The filter beat a 14-day weighted average of recent errors by 0.20 points. The filter's estimated gain depends on ERA5 reanalysis temperature and Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) irradiance, which are estimates of past weather that a live service would not have at the time of the forecast. Part 6 of the series tests the filter on ensemble weather forecasts. More years of history helped in the scored year (-0.22 points, 3 of 5 substations) and hurt in the year before (+0.32 points), so the series' long-history criterion (a gain from old years at 4 of 5 substations, confirmed in a second year) is not met on this evidence.

We asked two questions about a physical model of Primary substation demand: demand minus the output of the solar panels behind the meter, fitted by least squares, whose daily profile, heating response, and solar term are separate pieces. First, does training on every usable year since 2019, with a slowly varying correction called drift, forecast better than the same model on its best shorter window? Second, does a Kalman filter (a method that updates an estimate of the current demand level each time a new error arrives) that corrects each forecast with the errors observed up to 3.5 hours before the forecast, the model's counterpart of the lagged-power inputs of XGBoost, add to drift, replace drift, or replace refitting the model?

We fitted the model at 1 July 2024 and at 1 July 2025, froze each fit for the following year, and scored the 5 decision substations (the Primaries D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16, which have history from 2019 to 2021) on every half-hour outside the hand-filtered switching events. The 2025-26 year is the scored year, and 2024-25 is the replicate year, whose estimates decide nothing alone but must agree in sign. Every arm uses the convex model, which is Part 2's model with the solar capacity pinned to a real-time estimate. We did not use Part 3's pooled model, because Part 3 scored it 0.385 points worse than the per-site model in its scored year and gave it the verdict refuted (capped at inconclusive by a failed known-answer gate).

Contrasts. C1 to C6 are the six planned contrasts of this experiment: C1 more years against the best window, C2 the filter on drift, C3 the Kalman filter against the weighted mean, C4 drift once the filter runs, C5 the filter on a frozen fit against weekly refits, and C6 the model against lagless XGBoost. Every other contrast is exploratory, as the plan listed them, unless it is labelled post hoc. The numbers come from e00106_report.py, saved as report.txt, and the known-answer gate is gate.txt.

docs.title: Arms, rows, and settings
docs.text:
• Model. Net power in points of effective capacity is a daily profile by day type, holiday periods, a Christmas tent, heating slopes on ERA5 temperature averaged over 6, 24, 72, and 168 hours, lighting ramps, and minus a solar term, with a drift level per hour band on monthly knots. The solar capacity is pinned to the capacity estimate that was available in real time (the frozen vintage of experiment 45), not fitted.
  • Arms. The labels are used throughout the page:
Label Meaning A0 no drift A1 drift (monthly knots, drift step 30, chosen on 2023-24) A2 A0 plus the Kalman filter A3 A1 plus the Kalman filter A4 A1 plus a 14-day weighted mean of recent residuals A4-0 A0 plus that mean W the best window: 24 months with drift, chosen on 2023-24 WK W plus the filter X-best lagless XGBoost on 12 months, chosen on 2023-24
  • Post hoc arms. A1 smooth, A1s smooth, and W smooth use Part 2's drift step of 3,000, and A1s smooth also has steps at a penalty of 100. They were added after the tuned drift step sat at a grid edge and the tuned steps switched off, so they are labelled post hoc wherever they appear.
  • The filter. Per site and hour band, a persistent level (a random walk) and a transient (an AR(1) decaying per half-hour) observed with noise. The filter sees only residuals whose half-hour ended at least 3.5 hours before the 09:00 UTC initialisation, and no switching mask. Its four hyperparameters per site were fitted by marginal likelihood on the out-of-sample 2023-24 residuals of each base arm.
  • Schedule. One frozen fit per cut. The 4-weekly and weekly refit arms refit from 2023-07-01. A frozen model is weaker than a refitted one, so a contrast against a frozen arm could depend on the refit schedule. The refit arms test whether it does.
  • Rows. Every half-hour with a reading in the scored year, outside the hand-filtered switching events, at the five decision substations. D9 is scored in the scored year only, because D9 has no history to fit a replicate-year spread on.
  • Spread. Each arm's quantiles are its mean plus the residual quantiles of a replica fitted 12 months earlier, centred on their median per hour band and calendar quarter. The filter arms use the replica run through the same filter, with its first 14 days left out.

docs.title: Decision rule and verdict
docs.text:
• The verdict is partly supported. C1 (A1 minus W) is -0.223 points in the scored year, so its estimate is below zero, but only 3 of 5 substations improve and the replicate year reverses the sign (+0.317, 2 of 5 improve). The rule needs 4 of 5 and an agreeing replicate year for supported.
  • The verdict covers the convex model only. Even a supported C1 would meet the series' long-history criterion only for the convex model.
  • Part 6 keeps the filter. C2 is below zero in both years at 5 of 5 substations.
  • Part 6 uses the Kalman filter, not the weighted mean. C3 is below zero in both years at 5 of 5.
  • C4 passes non-inferiority. The interval lies inside +-0.10 and the estimate is at most +0.10 in both years, so dropping drift is not shown to be worse.
  • C5 shows the filter on a frozen fit beating weekly refits. These are choices for Part 6 to confirm or reverse, not findings.

docs.title: Headline numbers
docs.text:
Scored year, five decision substations, quantile score in points (negative favours the first arm); the interval is 99.17% (Bonferroni across six contrasts), from resampling whole calendar months. The stored mean forecast equals the median forecast in every arm, so "median-forecast error" names the error of that one forecast throughout.

  • C1, A1 minus W (more years): -0.223 (-0.416 to -0.036), 3 of 5 substations better. The replicate year is +0.317, 2 of 5 better. Leaving out any one substation leaves the sign unchanged in both years. The median-forecast error is -0.415.
  • C1 holds up to most checks in the scored year. Without D16 it is -0.060, from November to March -0.377, and from April to October -0.124. With D10's two unlabelled switching windows dropped from scoring it is -0.213, and with all rows including the masked events -0.188.
  • C2, A3 minus A1 (filter on drift): -0.606 (-1.014 to -0.272), 5 of 5 better. The replicate year is -1.017, 5 of 5. Without D16 it is -0.628, from November to March -0.188, and from April to October -0.876. The median-forecast error is -0.980.
  • C3, A3 minus A4 (Kalman against weighted mean): -0.204 (-0.452 to -0.054), 5 of 5 better. The replicate year is -0.200, 5 of 5. The median-forecast error is -0.323.
  • C4, A2 minus A3 (drift once filtered): -0.015 (-0.053 to +0.003), 5 of 5 lower. The replicate year is -0.003 and the median-forecast error -0.024.
  • C5, A3 frozen minus A1 refitted weekly: -0.158 (-0.258 to -0.087), 5 of 5 better. The replicate year is -0.313, 4 of 5, and the median-forecast error -0.260.
  • C6, A1 minus lagless XGBoost (X-best): -0.172 (-1.068 to +0.618), 4 of 5 better, and the interval is wide, so the contrast is inconclusive. The replicate year is -0.169 in the quantile score but +0.122 in the median-forecast error, so the two scores disagree there.

docs.title: Absolute scores
docs.text:
Five-site quantile score, in points:

Arm Scored year Replicate year A0 3.046 3.060 A1 2.895 3.303 A2 2.275 2.284 A3 2.290 2.287 A4 2.493 2.486 A4-0 2.386 2.486 W 3.119 2.987 WK 2.267 2.260 X-best (lagless XGBoost) 3.068 3.473 X-best with the filter 2.496 2.432 Climatology 4.068 3.910 Manual heuristic 3.488 3.839

A1 scored 0.112 points above Part 2's best arm (G-all+D1; interval -0.125 to +0.367), which fitted its capacity and used a smoother drift.

docs.title: What the filter does
docs.text:
• Alone it is the larger part of the gain. A2 (no drift) minus A0 is -0.771 (-0.904 to -0.650), 5 of 5. The weighted mean alone (A4-0 minus A0) is -0.660, and A2 minus A4-0 is -0.110 (-0.205 to -0.044).
  • The level carries all of it at day-ahead. The level-only filter scores the same as A3 (difference 0.000), and the transient-only filter is 0.618 worse than A3. The fitted transient decays within hours.
  • The gain lasts a week. At day 7 A3 still scores 0.18 points below A1 in the scored year (29% of the day-1 gain) and 0.54 in the replicate year.
  • Delaying the readings by 24 hours instead of 3.5 raised the score by 0.099, so the delay assumption matters a little (exploratory). Readings 0 hours old lowered the score by 0.035 (95% interval -0.060 to -0.016). Readings 9 hours old raised it by 0.026 (0.000 to 0.046), and readings 24 hours old raised it by 0.099 (0.059 to 0.142), 5 of 5 substations worse.
  • The filter works on XGBoost too (exploratory). X-best with the filter minus X-best is -0.571 (-1.005 to -0.235), 5 of 5. A3 minus X-best with the filter is -0.207 (-0.347 to -0.055), 4 of 5.

docs.title: Against lagged XGBoost (exploratory)
docs.text:
• At the same lead, A3 beat lagged XGBoost by 0.138 points, which is not significant alone. The two arms are compared at the same initialisation (00:00 UTC on the day before, leads of 24.5 to 48 hours): A3 scores 2.349 and lagged XGBoost 2.487, and the difference is -0.138 (95% interval -0.363 to +0.059). The day-ahead 2.29 of A3 is at another lead (15.5 to 39 hours) and is not comparable with 2.487.
  • The difference is not uniform. A3 is better at 4 of 5 substations and worse at D5, in both years. The difference is -0.523 from November to March and +0.111 from April to October. The replicate year gives -0.245, 4 of 5.
  • At 144.5 to 168 hours the difference is -0.110 (-0.336 to +0.102), 3 of 5 better. The replicate year is -0.169, 5 of 5. A1 without the filter is 0.408 worse than lagged XGBoost at the 24.5 to 48 hour lead (-0.022 to +0.825).
  • The lagged XGBoost arm is a fair but untuned comparator. It has the same 3.5-hour lag, XGBoost's 12-month window (not a window tuned for it), the default start, and no solar offset, which changed nothing when CAMS irradiance is an input. The arm's spread is too narrow: q05 coverage is 9.6% to 12.0% and q95 coverage 86% to 88% (report.txt). A3 has the pinned-capacity solar term, and the XGBoost arms do not use it. Both arms read ERA5 and CAMS at the target time, so every number here is a ceiling, not a live score.

docs.title: What did not help
docs.text:
• Drift steps. The step penalty tuned on 2023-24 switched every step off (penalty 1,000 and above), so A1s equals A1 at the five decision substations (at D9 it scores 2.353 against 2.305). With Part 2's smoother drift and a penalty of 100 (post hoc), steps scored 0.288 worse (0.116 to 0.473) in the scored year and -0.055 in the replicate year.
  • The COVID flag. Keeping the lockdown rows with a flag scored 0.515 worse (0.337 to 0.690) in the scored year and 0.160 better in the replicate year (3 of 5).
  • Fitted against pinned capacity. The fitted-capacity arm scored -0.041 (-0.090 to +0.005) in the scored year and +0.155 in the replicate year, so no consistent difference.
  • D10's November 2024 jump. Masking it from training changed D10's score by +0.021 (-0.220 to +0.283).
  • XGBoost's zero start and offset. The zero start scored 0.295 worse (0.157 to 0.468). The offset changed nothing: +0.007 (-0.010 to +0.025) on the zero start, -0.004 (-0.016 to +0.008) on the default start.
  • Refits with the filter. A3 frozen minus A3 refitted every 4 weeks is -0.061 (-0.118 to -0.010), and minus weekly refits -0.040 (-0.070 to -0.002), so refitting made the filtered model slightly worse. Without the filter, weekly refits scored 0.241 better than 4-weekly refits (0.144 to 0.362).

docs.title: The drift step did not generalise
docs.text:
• The step chosen on 2023-24 sat at a grid edge twice. The planned grid (300 to 30,000) chose 300, and the extended grid chose 30, the lowest value tried. The tuning score changed by 0.04 points from 100 to 30, mostly at D16.
  • Out of sample the smooth step won (post hoc arms). A1 smooth scores 2.817 in the scored year and 2.854 in the replicate year. A1 minus A1 smooth is +0.078 (-0.157 to +0.332) in the scored year and +0.450 in the replicate year.
  • With the smooth step the years contrast is near zero (post hoc). A1 smooth minus W smooth is +0.022 (-0.101 to +0.133) in the scored year and -0.087 in the replicate year, 3 of 5 both times.
  • The final knot. The tuning year did not choose a shrunk final knot (it gained 0.012 to 0.027 against the required 0.05). Out of sample, shrinking the last knot by 0.5 towards the mean of the last 12 knots scored -0.164 (-0.326 to -0.003) in the scored year and -0.167 in the replicate year, 3 and 4 of 5 better. Tying the last knot to the one before it scored +0.065 and -0.292. These contrasts are exploratory.
