docs.title: Differentiable physics, VP: fitting the pooled model's linear coefficients exactly
docs.text:
Fitting the pooled demand model's linear coefficients exactly did not improve its forecasts, so the optimiser is not what made the pooled model lose to a per-substation model. The pooled model is one differentiable-physics demand model fitted to many Primary substations at once. Variable projection (VP) is a fitting method that solves the coefficients entering the forecast linearly exactly at each step and moves the other parameters by gradient steps. VP reached a training objective (the negative log-likelihood of the training rows, in nats) 16,000 to 27,000 nats lower than the gradient fit of the same objective, which uses the Adam optimiser. The decision substations are the five Primary substations that carry the experiment's planned contrasts. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points (percent) of effective capacity. With the interaction neural network on, the scored year's quantile score, averaged over the five decision substations, was 5.49 for VP against 3.27 for the gradient fit. The excess comes from four days: on 28 and 29 March 2026 (the weekend of the spring clock change), Good Friday (3 April), and Easter Monday (6 April), VP forecast 20 to 280 points too high (75 to 280 on three of them), because the exact solve had made the network's last layer and the seasonal and holiday coefficients very large. Without those four days (a post hoc check) VP is still 0.70 points worse than the gradient fit, at all five substations. With the network off, VP is stable and within 0.03 points of the gradient fit. The known-answer test failed on its pre-registered definition, so the verdict cannot exceed inconclusive.

We asked whether the pooled model lost to a per-substation model in experiment 105 because gradient descent stopped short of the optimum. We fitted the pooled model, and a model per substation, by VP at three training cuts, scored 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30 with 2024-07-01 to 2025-06-30 as a replicate year, and compared with the gradient fit on one objective. The objective is under-regularised: its penalties on the network's last layer and on the calendar terms only make the solution unique, so the exact solve finds large weights that cancel on the training rows and diverge on rare inputs. The gradient fit's early stop had been acting as the regulariser. Exact optimisation is not the bottleneck for a simple model (L1 below), and the pooled model with its network cannot recover heating even from noise-free data.

Figure 1. The VP fits are no better than the gradient fits, and the onboarding contrasts compare against per-substation VP fits that score 71 and 48 points. Dot plot of the four planned contrasts with 98.75% intervals; the first two are positive (worse) at all five substations.

Figure 2. VP reaches a far lower objective than the gradient fit (P-map-same), and its two starts differ by up to 3,000 nats.

Figure 3. With the network on, the exact fit scores worst; with it off, the fit matches the gradient fit, and no pooled fit beats the per-substation convex model.

Figure 4. In one winter week and one spring week, the median forecasts of VP-P differ visibly from the others at some substations. The weeks were fixed in advance, not chosen by error, and both end before the four blow-up days; the days table in Results lists those.

Figure 5. The free fits sit 1,400 to 8,600 nats above the lowest capacity-profile point.

Figure 6. Only the network-off fit recovers a synthetic fleet, and only without noise. The network-on fit fails even on noise-free data.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text: Name What is fitted VP-P the pooled model (K = 2 shared daily shapes, interaction network of two hidden layers of 64 units, fitted capacity), maximum a posteriori (MAP), fitted by VP VP-S the same model, one MW substation at a time, fitted by VP P-map-same experiment 105's Adam fit (steps and schedule) on VP's objective P-map-polish P-map-same's non-linear parameters with the linear coefficients solved exactly VP-P-nonet VP-P without the interaction network (exploratory arm in the plan) G-2y, G-all Part 2's convex per-substation model on the 2-year window, and on all years L1 the equivalence configuration (see the ladder bullet) fitted by VP V1, C1v, C2v, C3v planned contrasts 1 to 4 under VP: fitting method, pooling, onboarding, short history

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms and references. The arm VP-P is the lower-objective start of two (start 0: seed 0; start 1: seed 1 with every heating threshold at 17 degrees), which is start 0 at the 2024-07-01 and 2025-07-01 cuts and start 1 at 2023-07-01. References: experiment 105's P, P-map, S, and equivalence arm (s_equiv_all); climatology; the manual heuristic. Row set, window, pool, and masks are as in experiment 105.
  • Fitting schedule. Every VP fit used 600 Adam warm-start steps, L-BFGS for up to 300 evaluations, and an Adam fallback of 1,200 steps (VP-P) or 400 (other arms) when L-BFGS missed its convergence test. Start 0 of VP-P was optimised in two rounds (the second at the second round's noise scale, with 300 more L-BFGS evaluations and 400 more Adam steps), so it received about twice the optimisation of start 1. Four VP-P-nonet fits (both starts at the 2023-07-01 and 2024-07-01 cuts) met the convergence test; no other fit did.
  • Scores (five decision sites, scored year; replicate year in brackets). VP-P 5.49 (4.26); VP-P start 1 3.89 (3.64); VP-P-nonet 3.30 (3.21); VP-S 4.09 (3.70); P-map-same 3.27 (3.11); P-map-polish 3.29 (3.18); experiment 105's P 3.42, P-map 3.46, S 3.04; G-2y 2.94 (3.02); G-all 3.07; climatology 4.07; manual heuristic 3.49.
  • V1 (planned): VP-P minus P-map-same is +2.215 points (98.75% interval +0.398 to +5.041), better at 0 of 5 substations; replicate year +1.154 (+0.527 to +1.849), 0 of 5 better.
  • The exact fit's objective is 16,000 to 27,000 nats lower at every cut. VP-P minus P-map-same is -16,747 nats at the 2025-07-01 cut (172,257 against 189,005), -16,014 at 2024-07-01, and -27,257 at 2023-07-01. Experiment 105's own P-map is 239,053 on this objective (it was fitted on a different objective, so this is a reference only).
  • Four days carry the headline (post hoc). The first two, 28 and 29 March 2026, are the Saturday and the Sunday of the spring clock change (a 23-hour local day); the other two are Good Friday and Easter Monday. A separate check of the clock-change handling in the differentiable-physics features and the ensemble weather join is under way; this page claims no bug in either. A per-day check of the mean median forecast error over the five decision sites finds the days below (a day is listed when any listed arm is over 30 points off), plus Good Friday (3 April), which the numbers audit flagged although its VP-P error is smaller. VP-P is also 47 points too high on 5 and 6 January; those two days are in the table but outside the four-day exclusion below, so the "without" numbers still contain them.
Day (2026) VP-P VP-P start 1 VP-onb4w VP-P-nonet P-map-same G-2y 5 January +47.1 -18.4 -5.0 -3.6 +0.4 -7.8 6 January +47.9 -16.8 -5.1 -5.3 -2.2 -9.5 28 March +75.2 +9.4 +91.8 -1.6 +3.3 -2.5 29 March +199.2 +12.3 +70.8 -5.2 -2.9 -6.4 3 April +19.5 0.0 +5.3 -1.4 -1.6 -3.5 6 April +278.2 +8.6 +17.6 +1.9 +3.3 +0.3
  • Without the four days (28 and 29 March, 3 and 6 April; post hoc). V1 falls to +0.696 (+0.317 to +1.264), still 0 of 5 better; C1v falls from +1.394 to -0.132 (-1.107 to +0.896); the VP-P five-site score falls from 5.49 to 3.97 (P-map-same 3.28); and the spread between the two VP-P starts falls from 1.599 to 0.104 points. In the replicate year the only day over 30 points is 27 December 2024 (VP-P-nonet +42.1, VP-P +29.0); without it V1 is +1.089 (+0.504 to +1.773) and the start spread is 0.636, so start dependence remains in the replicate year.
  • Mechanism: the exact solve found very large weights (saved models, 2025-07-01 cut). The network's last layer has an L2 norm of 270 in VP-P start 0 and 197 in start 1, against 7.6 for P-map-same. The largest harmonic coefficient is 37 (start 0) against 2.0, and the largest holiday coefficient is 54 against 6.9. The penalties are NETWORK_DECAY (1e-5) and CALENDAR_RIDGE (1e-6), sized only to make the solution unique. The same mechanism explains the per-substation fits on 4 weeks and 3 months below. That the large weights cause the four blow-up days is a hypothesis consistent with these numbers, not a tested result.
  • Solving the linear coefficients exactly after the gradient fit changes the score by only +0.013 (-0.001 to +0.025; P-map-polish minus P-map-same), while lowering the objective by 1,005 nats, so the linear coefficients do not limit skill.
  • C1v (planned): VP-P minus VP-S is +1.394 (-0.896 to +4.508), 0 of 5 better; replicate year +0.561 (-0.095 to +1.289). Non-inferiority (upper end at most +0.10) fails.
  • VP-S minus S is +1.059 points (95% interval +0.579 to +1.734), better at 1 of 5 substations; replicate year +0.716, 0 of 5 better. VP-S minus G-2y is +1.158 (+0.648 to +1.829). The per-substation VP model keeps the network, so exact optimisation made the per-substation model worse too.
  • VP-P-nonet (exploratory arm in the plan). VP-P-nonet minus P-map-same is +0.031 points (95% interval -0.174 to +0.192), so the network-off exact fit is within noise of the gradient fit with the network on. That comparison changes the network and the optimiser together. VP-P-nonet minus VP-P is -2.183 (-4.257 to -0.412), better at 5 of 5. The two VP-P-nonet starts differ by 0.004 points.
  • C2v and C3v (planned) compare against broken comparators. On the five decision sites, VP-onb4w minus VP-S-4w is -64.951 (-87.248 to -40.993) and VP-short3m minus VP-S-3m is -44.105 (-75.674 to -16.684), 5 of 5 better each (on all six scored sites: -60.8 and -49.4). The per-site VP fits on 4 weeks and 3 months score 70.6 and 48.4, because the exact solve fits the lightly penalised seasonal terms to a short window and extrapolates them. Against experiment 105's gradient arms, VP-onb4w minus P-onb4w is +1.460 (+0.439 to +2.522; VP-onb4w shares VP-P's network and blows up on 28 and 29 March too) and VP-short3m minus P-short3m is -0.122 (-0.554 to +0.182).
  • Ladder (L1, exploratory). L1 is experiment 105's equivalence configuration (one substation at a time, no network, no shared shapes, capacity pinned to the convex path, all years), fitted by VP from five threshold starts (12 to 20 degrees in steps of 2). It scores 2.877, against s_equiv_all's 3.326 (-0.449, -0.537 to -0.373, 5 of 5 better) and G-all's 3.072 (-0.195, -0.298 to -0.075). That lead over G-all depends on D16, whose replica fit was singular (so its spread is borrowed from other substations): without D16, L1 minus G-all is -0.116 (-0.277 to +0.072), so L1 matches G-all rather than beating it. The contrast L1 minus s_equiv_all combines the optimiser with a changed objective (natural-scale slope prior, fixed noise scale) and a threshold search; the share of the 0.25-point gap that comes from the heating form cannot be separated from them. L2, the plan's heating-basis step, was dropped. At D9 and D16 the replica fit was numerically singular; the cause at D16, a long-history substation, was not investigated. The objectives of the five threshold starts were not stored, so this page does not claim they agree.
  • Capacity profile (labelled). Criterion 1, capacities agree across the three starts within 3 points at every substation, passes at both configurations (largest spread 1.6 points for K = 2 and 1.3 for K = 4). Criterion 2, each free objective within 1 nat per 10,000 rows of the lowest profile point, fails: the free fits are 1,400 to 8,600 nats above it (tolerance 31 to 34 nats). Criterion 3, each free capacity where the profile is within that tolerance of its minimum, fails: the minimum is at 0.85 times the convex capacity path and the free capacities lie between 0.5 and 1.05 times it. The three starts reach objectives up to 7,000 nats apart, and none converged, so the interaction network's loss surface has many local optima. The pinned fits did not converge either.
  • Gate, test 2 (synthetic fleet at the pre-registered noise, sd 5.0 points; failed). Worst-case errors over eight synthetic substations and three starts:
Quantity Worst-case error Limit Heating threshold 5.1 to 5.7 degrees 1 Heating slope 70 to 76% 15% Season-year capacity 39 to 44% 10% Growth increment 2.0 to 2.5 points 1.5 Network summer-midday output 2.1 to 6.1 points 0.1
  • Gate, tests 3 and 4 (failed). Test 3: no start converged, and the objectives spread by 32 nats per 10,000 rows (limit 1). Test 4: the recovered capacity over the injected capacity was 0.77 to 0.90 (median 0.82; limit 0.9 to 1.1; experiment 105 had 0.78); other substations' capacities moved 1.1 to 4.8% (limit 5%).
  • Gate diagnostics (post hoc). Continuing the fit for 1,500 more evaluations lowers the objective by 4,200 nats and leaves the errors unchanged, so the failure is not under-training. Without noise the network-off fit recovers the fleet exactly (all errors 0.000), so the module is correct, but the network-on fit does not: its threshold is 6.9 degrees off, its slope 99% off, and the network adds 1.8 points in summer, because the network absorbs the heating term. The pre-registered gate has the network on and a truth without a network, so it could not pass by design. At noise sd 1.0 the network-off fit recovers thresholds to 0.02 degrees, slopes to 1%, and capacities to 1.3%; the network-on fit has slopes 17% off and a network output of 0.40 points; hiding temperature from the network by day fixes the slope (0.8%) but not the output (0.30). At the pre-registered noise every variant fails: network off 2.7 degrees, 30%, and 33%; temperature hidden by day 3.1 degrees, 37%, and 37%. The sd-1 runs use Gaussian noise and the sd-5 gate uses week blocks of another substation's convex residuals, so the step from sd 1 to sd 5 changes the noise structure as well as its size.
  • The harmonics hypothesis is not confirmed. Generating and fitting the fleet without the day-of-year harmonics improves the network-off thresholds and slopes (1.7 degrees and 21%) but not the capacities (34%), and worsens the network-on fit (5.9 degrees and 79%).
  • Hypothesis, not a result: the seasonal terms absorb the seasonal cycle. The harmonics, the per-band profile, and the calendar terms may absorb most of the seasonal cycle of temperature and sun. Only day-to-day weather anomalies would then identify the slope, threshold, and capacity, which makes the effective sample far smaller than the row count. Identification should then improve with more years of history.
  • Tails (five sites). Coverage is the share of actuals at or below each quantile. The worst 1% of rows carry 32% of VP-P's score; those are the four blow-up days.
Arm Coverage q01 q05 q95 q99 Pinball q01 q05 q95 q99 VP-P 0.023 0.052 0.910 0.983 1.929 2.548 1.057 0.272 VP-P-nonet 0.016 0.047 0.829 0.922 0.277 0.735 0.996 0.352 P-map-same 0.015 0.043 0.834 0.920 0.198 0.731 0.987 0.365 G-2y 0.015 0.043 0.846 0.940 0.186 0.666 0.851 0.282
  • Descriptive: D18, a young substation. In the scored year VP-P scores 5.86 and P-map-same 4.19, but VP-S scores 24.4 and G-2y 12.1. In the replicate year VP-P scores 180.5 against 13.6 for P-map-same.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site (scored year, points). VP-P: D10 -1.11, D11 0.58, D14 0.27, D16 0.43, D5 0.01, D9 -0.27, D18 0.93. VP-P-nonet: D10 -1.80, D11 0.94, D14 0.21, D16 0.20, D5 0.32. P-map-same: D10 -1.72, D11 0.73. D10's gap of about -1 to -1.8 points appears in every arm, including S (-1.74), so it is not a VP effect.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each contrast. V1 +2.676 (+0.847 to +4.840); C1v +1.460 (-0.665 to +3.950); C2v -69.7 and C3v -47.6 (five decision sites, as the contrasts above). The quantile-score and mean-error contrasts agree in sign.
  • Leave one site out. V1 stays +2.1 to +2.3 with any site dropped (0 of 4 better); C1v stays +1.2 to +1.7. Dropping D10's unlabelled jump (2025-11-17 to 2025-12-14), the winter or the summer half, or masked rows changes no sign.
  • Control. G-all scores 3.072 at the five sites, as in Part 2. P-map-polish is never above P-map-same on the VP objective, at all three cuts.
  • The plan stopped scoring after a failed gate; the experiment manager ruled to score anyway. The pre-registered gate stays as written and failed. The VP-P and P-map-same fits were scored and labelled "gate failed", and the verdict is capped at inconclusive.
  • Handoff. C1v's interval does not lie wholly above +0.10, so by the plan the pooled neural model continues and a later experiment compares VP-P against the per-substation model. The fitter option fitter="vp" stays off by default. The advice to compare fitting methods with the network off departs from that handoff and is advice only. It departs because, with the network on, the exact fit could not recover heating even from noise-free data, and the network-off fit matched the gradient fit.
  • Audit triggers that fired, and their triage. Trigger 1 (a control failed): the gate failed. Trigger 2 (the result contradicts its prediction): V1 is positive where -0.15 to -0.45 was predicted. Trigger 5 (a nested model beats the larger one): VP-P-nonet beats VP-P by 2.183. Trigger 6 (an interval far wider than a comparable one): V1's interval is 4.64 points wide, nine times Part 3's C1 on the same rows. Trigger 7 (the result decides the pooled route). A numbers audit by a fresh Opus reviewer traced triggers 2, 5, and 6 to the four blow-up days; its other findings are in this page.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• Held: the VP-P objective is over 2,000 nats below P-map-same (it is 16,747 below); criterion 1 of the capacity profile; P-map-polish does not exceed P-map-same; VP-P's coverage at q01, q05, and q99 is inside the predicted bands; peak GPU memory under 1 GB.
  • Failed: the predicted VP-P minus P-map-same difference of -0.15 to -0.45 points at all five substations (the result is +2.215, at none); C1v within +/-0.10 (+1.394); dropping D16 moves C1v by under 0.10 (it moves to +1.216); a start spread under 0.05 (1.599); VP-S minus S of -0.05 to -0.30 (+1.059); onboarding and short-history differences of -0.5 to -2.0 and -0.2 to -1.0 (-64.951 and -44.105, from broken comparators); the capacity profile passing (criteria 2 and 3 fail); VP-P's q95 coverage (0.910, 4 points below nominal; limit 3); every VP fit under 10 minutes of GPU time before its fallback (the longest, vp_p_s1 at 2023-07-01, took 664 s including the fallback).
  • Not evaluated: that VP-P's capacities lie within 15% of G-2y's at 4 of 5 substations. As a proxy, the capacity-profile free fits imply multipliers on the G-all capacity path of 0.99 (D5), 0.78 (D10), 0.58 (D11), 0.82 (D14), and 1.02 (D16), which is 2 of 5 within 15%; those fits are not VP-P itself. The ladder prediction (L1 against G-all by the 0.25-point gap) is also not evaluated cleanly, because L1 changes the objective.
  • Not built: VP-P-pin, the equivalence ladder's L2, batching of copies, the ladder, threshold profile, and tails figures, and the substation cards. The series rule asks for cards that let the maintainer check each fit is sane. The fit's weights are blown up (last-layer norm 270, largest harmonic coefficient 37, largest holiday coefficient 54), so a card would show unreliable values, and the manager waived the cards for this page once. Cards for the repaired fit are owed. A card, when built, will carry the line "weakly identified at real noise levels (experiment 112); compare across substations with care".
  • Figure 4 shows VP-P-nonet and G-2y in place of the plan's VP-S.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• No VP-P or VP-S fit met its convergence test, so the comparison is between fits that are lower in objective but not at the optimum.
  • The pooled VP result depends on the penalties on the network's last layer and the calendar terms; a stronger penalty was not tried.
  • The four blow-up days were found after the run, so every number "without" them is post hoc.
  • ERA5 and CAMS flatter the solar term; the hand-filtered masks are hindsight labels; the MVA tan(phi) and q0 are zero in VP, unlike P-map's; the replicate year is in sample for K and the deviation scale; fits are maximum a posteriori only.
  • The gate used the plan's noise (residuals of the per-substation convex model, sd 5.0 points). A parameter-recovery gate should test calibrated intervals (an 80% interval covering the truth 70 to 90% of the time over at least 20 synthetic substations, with the interval widths reported), not point tolerances.
  • The per-site VP fits on 4 weeks and 3 months are broken comparators (see C2v and C3v); the leave-one-out and short-history VP refits start cold and use L-BFGS only. The fits at the 2023-07-01 and 2024-07-01 training cuts exist only to give the spread of the later cut.
  • GPU time used: 5.77 of the 10 hours cap, tallied by e00112_budget.py (it includes about 0.26 hours of gate diagnostics; the L1 fits are not recorded).

docs.title: What the next experiment could answer
docs.text: Two questions are open, and the maintainer chooses between them. Does the exact fit work once the network's last layer and the calendar terms are penalised enough? A rerun of VP-P with stronger penalties would show whether the four blow-up days disappear. Does the pooled demand model need its interaction network at all? The network-off model is the candidate to compare with the per-substation convex model, on more years of history, where identification should improve with more weather anomalies.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, N5: does the convex model identify heating slopes and PV capacity at realistic noise?
docs.text:
At the noise the real fits have, the convex model's 80% month-block bootstrap intervals contain the true heating slope and the true PV capacity 84% of the time each, but a heating slope is only known to within about 38% of its size. N5 is the fifth step of the differentiable-physics series.

The pre-registered verdict is refuted, because the capacity interval covers the truth only 52% of the time when the noise is independent. The shortfall is a bias of about 0.24 points of capacity that comes mainly from the drift penalty at its tuned step of 3,000. The bias falls to 0.02 points at Part 4's step of 30, where coverage is 78% (a post hoc check). With independent noise, the same intervals cover the noise-free fit's own value 85% of the time, so the bias, not the interval width, accounts for the shortfall.

The test cannot show the bias that a wrong PV shape causes. The truth has the model's own form (experiment 112's gate test 1 found that bias). The posterior interval of the same fit covers only 20% at real noise and must not go on a card.

Absorption by the seasonal terms is a hypothesis for experiment 112's weak slopes, not a result. The day-of-year harmonics and the drift term can reproduce the seasonal cycles of temperature and of clear-sky PV. In N5 the harmonics absorb about 80% of a heating slope's variance. N5 does not test that hypothesis on experiment 112's pooled model, and N5's own capacity intervals are narrow.

We built 100 synthetic substations on the real calendar, weather, and PV shape of 5 Primary substations (20 each), put a known heating slope per hour band and a known PV capacity into each, added either real residuals borrowed from other substations (the decision noise, standard deviation 4.97 points, autocorrelation 0.83 at one half-hour) or independent noise (standard deviation 5.0, no autocorrelation), and asked how often each 80% interval contains the truth. Both noise cells gate the verdict. No forecast is scored. The first commit of this branch (ef25882da) is the pre-registration, written before any fit.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• Points: percentage points of a substation's effective capacity. A heating slope is in points per 10 °C of cold.
  • Month-block bootstrap: resample whole calendar months with replacement, refit the convex model, and take the 10th and 90th percentiles of the refitted values as an 80% interval. I1 keeps each calendar quarter's number of months in every resample and widens the interval about its median by sqrt(m / (m - 1)), where m is the months per quarter (6 for capacity). I1u resamples months freely. I2 is the posterior interval of the penalised fit.
  • Arms (the convex model's variants): G-full has day-of-year harmonics and the monthly drift path (D1) beside the heating, capacity, and calendar terms. G-H has the harmonics and no drift. G-D has the drift and no harmonics. G-0 has neither. G-full-30 is G-full with experiment 106's ("Part 4") drift step of 30 in place of 3,000.
  • Truths: T-HD keeps the real fit's harmonics and drift. T-0 sets both to zero.
  • r: the variance of a quantity's estimate with the harmonics and drift removed, as a share of its variance in the full fit. A small r means the seasonal terms absorb most of the information.
  • tau: the inflated bootstrap variance divided by the sandwich variance, the variance of a penalised fit under independent noise. A tau of 27 means the autocorrelated noise makes the estimate 27 times as uncertain as independent noise would.
  • rho: a descriptive collinearity share of a quantity's column with the other columns.
  • Effective sample size: the number of independent half-hours that carry the same information as the autocorrelated rows, which is the row count times rho over tau.
  • Identified means the data fix a quantity within a narrow range. A calibrated interval contains the truth as often as its nominal 80%.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1 shows the month-block bootstrap (I1) covering the truth 84% of the time at real noise for both families, and the posterior interval (I2) 20%. With independent noise the posterior interval is fine for heating slopes (80%). The capacity row shows the bias: I1 covers the truth 52% of the time and the noise-free fit's value 85%. The step-30 row is a post hoc rerun at Part 4's drift step of 30, which covers 83% and 80% at real noise and 80% and 78% with independent noise.

Figure 2 shows the estimates scattering around the truth. The median signed relative error, the median of (estimate minus truth) divided by truth, is -1.4% for band slopes and -1.3% for capacity at real noise.

Figure 3 shows the seasonal terms widening the heating-slope intervals. Where the truth has no harmonics or drift, the fit that omits both has an I1 interval about 0.55 times as wide (relative width 0.21 against 0.38; real noise, band slopes). The harmonics alone account for the widening.

Figure 4 shows which term absorbs the information. At the drift step of 3,000, the harmonics carry the heating slopes (removing them leaves 26 to 32% of the variance) and the drift carries part of the capacity (removing it leaves 73%). At the step of 30 the drift absorbs more of the heating slopes (removing it leaves 89 to 92%, against 97 to 98%), and the harmonics' unique share falls (removing them leaves 86 to 90%).

Figure 5 shows the real fits at the 2025-07-01 cut. The fitted latest capacity is 5.8%, 19.8%, and 19.4% below the season-year mean of experiment 45's weekly capacity vintage at D5, D11, and D16, and 0.5% above it at D10; D14's vintage stops in 2023. At the replicate cut (2024-07-01) D16 is 24.7% below the vintage, outside experiment 40's 20% band.

docs.title: Design and numbers
docs.text:
• Design: convex model of studies.dp_gam with fitted capacity and D1 drift (ridge 0.1, drift step 3,000), one design per substation, cut 2024-07-01, all years, lockdown out (experiment 103's rows). Every fit is a column subset of that design. Each of D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16 gets 20 draws.
  • Truths and noise: truth heating totals are U(0.7, 1.3) times the real fit's (floor 2 points per 10 °C); capacity is U(5, 25) points then U(1, 5) increments. Real noise is whole months of other decision substations' residuals, from other years, with a random sign; 4.7% of slots were empty and set to zero, and one draw can reuse a donor month for several of its months.
  • Decision rule, per family: I1's coverage of the truth in the real-noise cell and the independent-noise cell. Band slopes are calibrated (84% with a site-clustered 95% interval of 76.0 to 90.8%, and 83%, 78.5 to 88.0%). Capacity is overconfident (84%, 76 to 91%, and 52%, 32 to 74%). The verdict is refuted. The independent-noise cell is a gate cell with the same standard deviation as the real noise but no autocorrelation.
  • Width, real-noise cell: band slopes 3.3 points per 10 °C, 38% of the truth, so weak; capacity 2.8 points, 12% of the truth, so precise. With independent noise the widths are 8% and 3%.
  • Posterior interval (I2) at real noise: 20% (bands) and 19% (capacity). The inflated bootstrap variance is 27 (bands) and 25 (capacity) times the sandwich variance (tau). The effective sample size is rho over tau of the rows, with rho 0.06 for bands and 0.17 for capacity, which is 0.23% (bands) and 0.70% (capacity). I1 is 5.0 and 4.5 times as wide as I2 in the simulation. On the real data I1 is 4.6 times as wide (2.5 to 6.0) for slopes and 6.4 times as wide (2.8 to 31) for capacity.
  • Penalty bias on capacity (analytic, full fit): median -0.24 points (median absolute 0.35; the sign varies by site, 40% of draws positive) at drift step 3,000, of which -0.23 comes from the drift penalty and -0.01 from the ridge. At step 30 it is -0.02 points. The bias is 0.51 of the interval width with independent noise and 0.13 at real noise. For band slopes the median absolute bias is 0.07 points at step 3,000 and 0.004 at step 30.
  • Seasonal misfit in the donor residuals: fitting the full model to the real noise alone, unbounded, returns -0.4 to -1.5% of the true slope and -1.0% of the true capacity on average. The bounded fit's 5 to 6% measures the zero bound (every fit sits on a bound), not misfit.
  • Absorption (G-0 against G-full): r is 0.18 to 0.22 for band slopes and 0.67 for capacity at drift step 3,000, and 0.16 to 0.20 and 0.60 at step 30. The capacity ratio is above the 0.56 limit, so the label is absorption partial at both penalties, though the heating slopes alone would be absorption large. The I2 width ratios (0.44 and 0.83 at real noise) equal the square roots of r (0.44 and 0.82) by construction. The I1 width ratios agree with them with independent noise (0.43 and 0.82) and at real noise for band slopes (0.53, 0.09 above, inside the 0.1 tolerance) but not for capacity (1.08 against 0.82).
  • Noise: autocorrelation 0.83, 0.44, and 0.21 at lags of 1, 48, and 336 half-hours; standard deviation 4.97 points.

Other arms (I1 coverage of the truth, real noise):

docs.title: Predictions against outcome
docs.text:
• Held: I1 coverage 70 to 90% in the decision cell for both families; band slopes weak; capacity width under 25%; I2 under 60% at real noise; tau between 3 and 30; I1 and I2 both 70 to 90% for band slopes with independent noise; r at most 0.36 for every band slope; the I1 width ratio within 0.1 of the square root of r for band slopes; G-0 on T-HD under 50%; the pinned-0.8 arm within 10%; an active bound in over 30% of fits; unbounded coverage within 5 points (exactly 5 for capacity); spectral share over 70% in G-full; I1 2 to 5 times I2 in the simulation; the night-band slope excluding zero at all 5 real substations; the penalty bias under a quarter of the width at real noise (0.13); the noise-only bias under 5% (unbounded).
  • Failed: I1 and I2 both 70 to 90% for capacity with independent noise (52% and 39%); r at most 0.56 for capacity (0.67); harmonics giving the smaller r for capacity (the drift does, 0.73 against 0.95); drift giving the smaller r for the night band (the harmonics do, 0.26 against 0.97); independent-noise widths at 30 to 60% of the real-noise widths (23% and 25%); G-0's spectral share under 50% (70 to 83%); 2-year widths 1.3 to 2 times the all-years widths (1.2 and 0.93); the I1 width ratio within 0.1 of the square root of r for capacity at real noise; I1 2 to 5 times I2 on the real capacity (6.4 times).
  • Not pre-registered: with independent noise the penalty bias is 0.51 of the interval width.
  • Real data (2025-07-01 cut): I1 capacity intervals are 2.7 to 5.9 points wide. They overlap the vintage's 20% band at the 4 substations with a vintage.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast, and the mean-forecast error beside the quantile score: not applicable; no forecast is made. The estimates' own bias is the median signed relative error, -1.4% (bands) and -1.3% (capacity).
  • Audit triggers that fired: the trigger for a result that contradicts a prediction or an earlier finding fired, because the convex model's capacity is precise at real noise where experiment 112's pooled fit failed, several predictions failed without a tested explanation, and the fitted capacity is more than 20% below the vintage at the replicate cut's D16 (24.7%); the explanation recorded here is the seasonal terms and the in-family truth. The trigger for a later experiment's design depending on the result fired, because the cards, Part 5's capacity reading, and the next pooled test depend on it.
  • Audit triggers that did not fire: a failed control (all five controls pass: the largest relative difference from fit_gam is 4.6e-11, and from a dense bounded least-squares fit 4.9e-10; noise-free recovery is exact to 1.6e-12 over 235 checks; I2 covers 79.5% of the noise-free value over 500 independent-noise draws; I1's coverage on the cell's 100 draws is 78% and 81%; every resample keeps every quarter's size; no row is past its cut); a quantile-score contrast and a mean-forecast contrast pointing in different directions (coverage and bias point the same way: the capacity bias lowers coverage); a leave-one-site-out result that changes a label (leaving any one site out leaves the labels unchanged, the capacity row stays overconfident and the band row calibrated, absorption stays partial, and leaving D16 out moves the capacity independent-noise interval to 28 to 60%, wholly below 70%); a nested arm beating the arm that contains it (G-full never beats the true smaller G-0 on T-0 in error, and the pinned-truth arm's slope error, 14.65% root mean square, matches G-full's, 14.62%). The trigger for a headline interval more than twice or less than half as wide as a sister experiment's cannot be checked, because Part 5 has not run.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Caveats: ECMWF Reanalysis v5 and Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service estimates flatter the solar term by an amount this experiment did not measure. In-family truths cannot show PV-shape bias. The donors are the other decision substations. The inflation is an approximation (uninflated I1 covers 83% and 80%). The noise is not experiment 112's (whole months of the same season from another year, not weeks from any season). Capacity rests on 11 months of data, not the 6 the plan assumed, so the inflation with m = 6 is slightly too large. Season-years with under 1,000 training rows get no capacity column (see the data-processing page). The 2024-07-01 replicate cut is reported only for the capacity-against-vintage comparison, not for the intervals.
  • Next: a gate of the step-30 convex model in both noise cells would be needed before a capacity interval is printed, and Part 5's capacity rule depends on that outcome. A test of the pooled model with the same real-residual noise would show whether pooled slopes are as weak. Part 5's bootstrap ranges and dp_pinned_capacity can go beside the real intervals once Part 5 has run.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, N3 and N4: interaction terms and a per-site heating threshold
docs.text:
Splitting each heating term of the convex model between the first and second half of each hour band (for example 00:00 to 03:00 against 03:00 to 06:00) lowered its day-ahead error by about 0.04 percentage points of substation capacity (97.5% interval 0.014 to 0.070), at all 5 substations in both years. The error is measured after a Kalman filter that corrects the forecast using its recent errors. The convex model is the demand model of each Primary substation (a substation that steps the voltage down for the local distribution network). Experiment 111, the sixth part of the differentiable-physics (DP) series, chose it as the series' candidate and called it GAM-K. Every number here uses observed past temperature, not weather forecasts.

The gain is a temperature-dependent shape of the day more than a heating effect, and the gain label rests on D5. Two placebo splits of the same size gain nothing, but about 38% of the gain appears on warm rows where every heating term is zero. Without D5 the estimate is -0.0296, which is small gain (see Checks). Letting heating or lighting differ between weekdays and weekends adds nothing: the interval of the weekday split excludes a gain larger than 0.006 points.

Choosing the heating threshold separately for each substation did not clearly help (-0.012 points, interval spanning zero). The heating threshold is the temperature below which heating demand starts; the model uses 15.5 degrees C. The profile minimum lies below 15.5 degrees C at 4 of 5 substations, but only D10 passes the rule that allows a threshold to be printed, and D10's reads "12 degrees C or lower" because its minimum sits at the edge of the 12 to 19 degree grid.

The verdict is partly supported (N3 gain, N4 tie). Audit triggers 2, 4, and 7 fired. An Opus audit has run, and its findings are triaged under Checks.

We fitted GAM-K's convex model per substation at 4 yearly cuts, froze each fit for the year after its cut, and corrected its day-ahead forecast with the Kalman filter. The base model (B0) was compared with variants of it, called arms, that add interaction terms (N3) or a per-site threshold (N4). The tuning year chose the penalty weights and filter settings, the replicate year checked the sign, and the scored year decided. A third planned change, N13 (a mix of PV panel orientations), was dropped because experiment 73 and experiment 77 found the mix unidentified or immaterial.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• Points: percentage points of a substation's effective capacity. A heating slope is in points per 10 degrees C below the threshold.
  • B0 and B0-K: GAM-K's convex model (24-month window, no drift, pinned PV capacity, ridge 0.1) without and with the Kalman filter of recent errors. The suffix -K always means "after the filter".
  • T1, T2, T3, T-all: B0 with each heating column split by day type (T1: weekday against Saturday, Sunday, and bank holiday), each heating column split by half of its hour band (T2: 00 to 03 against 03 to 06 local time, 06 to 08:30 against 08:30 to 11, 11 to 13:30 against 13:30 to 16, 16 to 20 against 20 to 24), each lighting ramp split by day type (T3), or all three together (T-all, where each heating column splits four ways). A difference penalty ties the pieces towards each other, and a weight lambda sets its strength.
  • H-site: B0 with the heating hinge at the threshold, from 12 to 19 degrees C in 0.5 degree steps, that minimises the training loss at each substation and cut.
  • Effective nats: a loss difference over 2 times the noise variance times tau, where tau (21.4 here) is the factor by which autocorrelated noise inflates the variance of a heating slope.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1 shows T-all-K ahead of B0-K by 0.039 points, with the interval wholly below zero and the replicate year matching. The gain survives B0's filter settings (the control row) and is about three times larger after the filter than before. The per-site threshold's interval spans zero. T2 (the half-band split alone) carries the whole gain, but see Checks for what that gain is.

Figure 2 shows every arm's score beside the references. The filtered convex models score between 2.22 and 2.26 pooled over the 5 substations. Lagless XGBoost with the filter scores 2.50, the manual heuristic 3.49, and climatology 4.07.

Figure 3 shows the gain sitting in the morning and evening bands, and in winter. T-all-K gains 0.066 points in the morning and 0.061 in the evening, 0.022 at night, and loses 0.004 at midday. T2-K (the half-band split alone) carries the pattern, and T1-K and T3-K are near zero.

Figure 4 shows each substation's loss over the heating thresholds at the scored cut. D5 and D10 bottom out at the 12 degree edge, D11 at 12.5, D16 at 13.5, D9 at 14.5, and D14 at 15.5. The loss at 15.5 degrees is 39 effective nats above the minimum at D10, 15 at D11, 8 at D5, 6 at D16, and 0 at D14.

Figure 5 shows gate 3, the synthetic test of the threshold rule. The 80% interval covered the true threshold in 88 of 100 synthetic substations, and the median interval width was 3.0 degrees C. The arg-min sat at a grid edge in 32 of 100 draws, although every true threshold lay between 12.5 and 18.5 degrees C, so the gate never tested recovery at the 12 degree edge where D10 sits.

Figure 6 shows gate 2, the synthetic test of the interaction terms. With a real interaction sized to a 0.03 point gain, T-all beat B0 in 80 of 100 draws. Without one, T-all lost 0.006 points on average. The real interaction in this gate is weekday against weekend only, so the half-band split that carries C1 had no positive control, and the pass test counts the draws where T-all wins (91 of 100 pass at lambda 10,000 on a mean gain of 0.0019). It passed at exactly 80 of 100.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per site: 0.000 points at every site for every arm, by construction, because the spread of each arm is centred on its median.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each contrast: C1's mean absolute error of the mean forecast changed by -0.076 points (replicate -0.069), the same sign as its quantile score. C2's changed by -0.023 (replicate -0.034).
  • Triggers fired: 2, 4, and 7 of the seven in the ml-experiment skill; 1, 3, 5, and 6 did not fire. The Opus numbers review and audit (two independent runs) reproduced every number and changed no label, and its findings are triaged here.
    • Trigger 4 fired. Without D5, C1 is -0.0296 (97.5% interval -0.0537 to -0.0106), above the -0.03 that a gain needs, so C1 would read small gain and the verdict small gain. The gain label therefore rests on D5, the substation with the largest gain (-0.080 against a median of -0.036), and on an estimate that clears the threshold by 0.009 points. The 97.5% interval's upper end is -0.014, under half the threshold. Without any other substation, C1 stays a gain. The report script now recomputes the label for each leave-one-out set.
    • Trigger 2 fired four times. The plan predicted the opposite of each of these: gate 3 passed; D10 passed the printing rule; T2's unfiltered gain was a third of its filtered gain (-0.013 against -0.040) where at least twice was predicted; and C2's replicate year is negative at 5 of 5 sites where at most 3 was predicted. The third has the tested explanation in the next bullet.
    • Trigger 7 fired because a gain would change GAM-K's base on one year plus a replicate at the screening tier.
  • What the T2 gain is. Two placebo splits with T2's column count, penalty, and lambda (even against odd local half-hours, and even against odd days; every arm through B0's filter settings, e00114_placebo.py) give -0.0008 and +0.0024 against T2's -0.0370 in the scored year, and -0.0007 and +0.0011 against -0.0348 in the tuning year. So extra columns do not explain the gain. Splitting the scored year by temperature, T2-K minus B0-K is -0.069 on warm rows (20% of rows, all four smoothed temperatures at or above 15.5 degrees C, so every heating column is zero) and -0.029 on cold rows (all four below it). Unfiltered, T2 minus B0 is -0.065 on warm rows and +0.0075 (worse) on cold rows. About 38% of the filtered gain, and all of the unfiltered gain, therefore arrives through the refitted daily profile and not through a heating slope. A likely mechanism is that the profile no longer averages cold-day and warm-day shapes; the experiment did not test that. The unfiltered gain is also an April-to-October gain (T2 minus B0 is +0.017 from November to March), which is why the filtered gain was three times the unfiltered one.
  • Gate margins and limits. Gate 2 passed at exactly 80 of 100 draws, and its real interaction has no half-band component, so T2 had no positive control (the truth-0 run is its only null control). Gate 3 passed on the margin on three criteria: median width 3.0 against at most 3.0, placebo recovery 0.70 against at least 0.70, and recovery of far thresholds 0.64 against at least 0.60.

docs.title: Substation cards
docs.text:
Provisional: fitted to past weather on a screening run. One card per decision substation shows B0's daily profile by day type, holiday and Christmas effects, the loss against heating threshold, B0's heating slope by hour band, T-all's heating slope by half-band and day type, B0's thermal-inertia mix, the lighting terms, the solar capacity, and the filter's daily level and anomaly over the scored year. The transient anomaly is near zero at day-ahead leads, so its panel is flat. D9 has 9 months of history at the replicate cut.

Heating slopes are weakly identified at real noise levels (experiment 113); compare across substations with care. Do not rank substations by their heating slopes. The fitted capacities carry no interval and are not measurements.

A threshold is printed only for D10: 12 degrees C or lower (80% interval 11.75 to 12.75), because the grid starts at 12 degrees C and gate 3 never tested recovery at that edge. The other substations read "threshold not identified at this substation".

Sample weeks. Each figure shows one week per season of the scored year, chosen by one rule before any score was read: the week that starts on the second Monday of the season's middle month. B0-K sits beside T-all-K, with the median forecast, the 80% and 90% bands, and the observed power. The panels show whether the half-band gain is visible in a single week; at this scale it is not, because a gain of 0.04 points is under 2% of the score (2.255). Sample weeks are drawn for the 5 decision substations only; D9 has none.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
Every number on this page is printed by e00114_report.py into report.txt.

  • Arms and schedule: B0, T1, T2, T3, T-all, and H-site, each unfiltered and filtered, fitted at 2022-07-01 (the tuning year's replica), 2023-07-01 (tuning), 2024-07-01 (replicate), and 2025-07-01 (scored). One frozen fit per arm and cut, no refits, one seed, day-ahead (09:00 UTC origins). The screening tier's monthly refits would be a follow-up.
  • Chosen settings (tuning year, filtered score): lambda 1 for T1, T2, and T-all (the weakest of 1, 100, and 10,000) and 10,000 for T3. New columns at lambda 1: about 42 effective degrees of freedom for T-all (median over the 5 substations).
  • Absolute scores, scored year (points, 5 substations pooled): B0 2.884, B0-K 2.255, T-all 2.872, T-all-K 2.216, H-site 2.882, H-site-K 2.243. Replicate year: B0-K 2.261, T-all-K 2.223, H-site-K 2.240. Tuning year: B0-K 2.099, T-all-K 2.067, H-site-K 2.101.

docs.title: Predictions against outcome
docs.text:
• C1 between -0.06 and +0.01 in both years: held (-0.039 and -0.038).
  • T2-K carries most of any gain, in winter and in the morning and evening bands: held.
  • T2-K's unfiltered gain at least twice its filtered gain: failed. The unfiltered gain (-0.013) is a third of the filtered one (-0.040). Explained by the warm and cold split under Checks.
  • T1-K and T3-K within 0.02 points, filtered or not: held.
  • Gate 2 passes, and no capacity move is flagged: held.
  • N4 gate fails on width, B0's tau 10 to 40, no real substation passes the printing rule, the profile flat over 3 degrees C or more at 4 of 5 substations, arg-min at a grid edge at 1 or more: partly failed. The gate passed (median width exactly 3.0), tau was 21.4, and D10 passed the printing rule. No profile was flat over 3 degrees C, and the arg-min sat at the grid edge at D5 and D10.
  • C2 between -0.04 and +0.03, replicate negative at 3 of 5 sites at most: partly held. C2 was -0.012, inside the predicted range, but the replicate was negative at 5 of 5 sites against a prediction of at most 3.
  • B0-K within 0.06 of WK, run under 1.5 hours: held (-0.012). The stages together took about 20 minutes of wall clock on 6 cores (the work file times are in report.txt).

docs.title: Work this builds on
docs.text:
• Earlier experiments in the series: experiment 104 (Part 2) built the convex model and tuned its ridge; experiment 105 (Part 3) found that a neural-network interaction added nothing measurable, which is why N3 asks the question of the convex terms directly; experiment 106 (Part 4) built the Kalman filter and supplies the stored references (A2, WK, XGBoost, climatology, the manual heuristic); experiment 107 gave the 0.03-point sister contrast; experiment 103 chose the rows, cuts, and switching masks; experiment 45 supplies the pinned PV capacity; and experiment 87 fixed the 11 quantile levels of the score.
  • Heating response in the literature: additive models of electricity demand with smooth, data-fitted terms are the closest published relatives of the convex model's heating terms, which use a hinge at a fixed threshold. Fasiolo et al. (2021) fit additive quantile regressions with calibrated inference, motivated by load forecasting. Obst et al. (2021) correct additive load models with Kalman filters, the same pairing as GAM-K and its recent-error filter. Neither paper's page states how temperature enters its model, so this page makes no claim about their temperature terms.

docs.title: Caveats and choices made after the plan
docs.text:
• Past weather: both gains use ERA5 temperature at the target half-hour, an upper bound on skill with a live forecast. Part 6's calibration moved ENS temperature by -1.15 to +2.05 K and its filter gain on ENS was about two-thirds of Part 4's. Only an ENS confirmation with monthly refits tests transfer.
  • One scored year plus a replicate, frozen fits, hindsight switching masks shared by every arm.
  • Lambda sits at the weakest penalty tried for T1, T2, and T-all. A weaker penalty was not tried, and the tuning-year gain was still growing towards it.
  • Edits to the plan. Test 1's tolerance for the fitted-value gap at lambda 10^10 went from 1e-6 to 1e-5 points, because development runs on the penalised solve alone showed a float64 floor of 0.8e-6 to 2.6e-6 points (12 of the 40 checks exceed 1e-6, none exceeds 2.6e-6); the plan commit is amended in its own commit, before the experiment's arms were fitted. Gate 2's amplitude rule is a post-tuning clarification, recorded only in this write-up: it was set on the gain attributable to the interaction (the gap to the true-parameter forecast under truth I, less the gap under truth 0), because the estimation error alone is about 0.1 points and the plan's wording would have chosen an amplitude near zero. It came after the tuning fits and the pilot draws, and before any replicate-year or scored-year row was read. T-all splits each heating column four ways, and its two difference penalties share one lambda.
  • Placebo arms and the leave-one-out label check were added after the Opus audit, by e00114_placebo.py and e00114_report.py.
  • Leaks, none reaching a scored row: the 2022-07-01 replica, which supplies the tuning year's spread, reads the 2023-08-07 capacity vintage, 13 months late; the 2023-07-01 cut has the 5-week vintage leak; D9's 2024-07-01 fit reads the 2025-04-14 vintage; the replicate year's filter spread is in sample for the filter's hyperparameters. The first day of the scored year (288 of 104,897 rows) is forecast from an issue time of 2025-06-30 09:00, after the fit's 2025-07-01 cut, for every arm alike.
  • Run history: e00114_fit.py ran twice (the predictions date from the first run, the profiles and coefficients from the second), and the stored predictions' manifests record the commit as dirty. A refit of three arms agrees with the stored sets to 4e-6 points.
  • Synthetic substations share the model's own form, so gates 2 and 3 cannot show a wrong PV shape.
  • No new data-processing finding for docs/ml-experiments/data-processing.md.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• An ENS confirmation of T-all or of T2 alone as GAM-K's base, with Part 6's monthly refits. A gain on past weather becomes a candidate only after that run, which needs its own plan.
  • A threshold grid that reaches below 12 degrees C, to see where D5's and D10's minima lie before drawing any conclusion about the heating threshold.
  • Combining T2 with the shape state of the filter (a later follow-up, outside this plan).

docs.title: Differentiable physics, W1: a diurnal-shape state in the recent-error filter on ENS
docs.text: Take-home: a daily shape learned from recent readings lowers the physics-based forecast's day-ahead error by 0.075 points (about 3%) at five Primary substations, but a simple average of the last 14 days' errors gains as much, and the shape state failed its own speed check. The shape state cut the day-ahead score in two separate periods at 5 of 5 substations, and by 0.112 points in the scored winter (a post hoc breakdown). The 14-day average (recipe R) scored 0.014 points better than the shape state (interval -0.014 to +0.048, no difference), so the added machinery is not justified yet. The shape state recovered 0.35 of an injected change in two weeks against a pre-registered floor of 0.4, so the verdict is inconclusive. A faster shape state, tried afterwards, chosen from the gate's formula before any score of it was read, and labelled post hoc, passed that check and beat both K0 and R, and needs a pre-registered rerun to count.

docs.title: What was asked, and the answer in plain terms
docs.text:
The question was whether the part of a demand forecast's error that lies in the shape of the day can be removed by learning that shape from the last few days of readings. The forecast is for the electricity demand of five Primary substations (the stations that step power down from 33 kV to 11 kV) for the day after the forecast is made, up to 168 hours ahead. It comes from a physics-based demand model driven by ECMWF ensemble (ENS) weather forecasts, with a Kalman filter that estimates from recent readings how far the model has been off (experiment 111; Kalman (1960)). That arm is called K0 here. The shape state (arm KW) gives the filter 48 more numbers, one per half-hour of the day, which it adjusts from every reading and adds to the forecast.

Scores are in points of effective capacity, and lower is better. A point is 1% of a substation's effective capacity (the capacity its readings are scaled by). The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, as in experiment 87. Day D+1 is the UTC day after the forecast's 09:00 UTC origin (leads of 15.5 to 39 hours). Every setting was chosen on the odd months of July 2024 to June 2025 (the tuning months). The even months of the same year are the replicate months, which no setting had seen. The scored year is 2 July 2025 to 29 June 2026, the 292 runs of experiment 87's fold_a_daily_gap_v1. Rows inside the hand-filtered switching events are left out. Weather is ENS, and the demand model is fitted to estimates of past weather. The recent-error filter follows the design of experiment 106.

The scored year chose the idea's form, which is why the replicate months exist. A screening of the same data, run by the session that planned this experiment and recorded in the plan commit, had suggested the idea, so a gain in the scored year alone would not count. Both periods showed the same gain.

Gate failure: the verdict is capped at inconclusive. The pre-registered check that the shape state learns an injected change fast enough failed its floor, so all scoring below was run after a failed blocking test. The first gate run is kept in full (see "The gate"), and the faster shape state is a post hoc arm that never passed the pre-registered gate.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. K0 (GAM-K, reproduced exactly from experiment 111's stored output); KW (the decision arm: K0 plus a shape with zero mean inside each of the four hour bands); KW-lb and K0-lb (noise settings chosen per lead band); KW-day (no readings from the day of the forecast); R (K0 minus kappa times the 14-day mean D+1 error profile by local half-hour, kappa 0.75 chosen on the tuning months); R75 (the same as R, kappa fixed at 0.75, so identical); KS and KS1 (exploratory shape variants); KW-nomid (midday shape frozen at zero); KW-pl52 (the shape from 52 weeks earlier); delay arms at 0, 24, and 33 hours; and KW-fast (post hoc: the shape step 16 times larger). No arm refits the demand model, so the experiment reuses experiment 111's fits and member forecasts.
  • Rows and compute. Five decision substations (D5, D10, D11, D14, D16) with D9 beside them; 41,126 D+1 rows in the replicate months and 464,228 rows over all leads in the scored year on the rows every reference holds. Retraining schedule: none, because experiment 111's monthly refits are reused; the contrasts compare filters on one set of fits. Run time: about 13 minutes on 6 cores for all arms.
  • Headline: the shape state (C1, KW minus K0 at D+1, 98.75% intervals). Replicate months -0.0745 (-0.1449 to -0.0091, 5 of 5 substations better); scored year -0.0750 (-0.1188 to -0.0329, 5 of 5). Absolute scores in the scored year: K0 2.525, KW 2.450. Over all leads: -0.0661 and -0.0543. The gain at 48 to 144 hours is 0.049 (scored year), 66% of the D+1 gain, so more than half remains.
  • C2, lead-band tuning (KW-lb minus KW): 0.0000 in both periods. The tuned multipliers ([4, 4, 0.5, 0.25] for KW) barely change the filter, because the observation noise sits at 0.05 to 0.09 points at five of six substations, so the filter already trusts each reading.
  • C3, the newest readings (KW minus KW-day): -0.0564 (replicate) and -0.0546 (scored) at D+1, 5 of 5 substations. The gain is in the night and morning bands (-0.167 and -0.061 in the scored year) and none in the midday and evening bands, where the readings of the forecast day arrive too late to help.
  • C4, shape state against the recipe (KW minus R): +0.0170 (-0.0164 to +0.0401) and +0.0136 (-0.0138 to +0.0483); 1 of 5 and 0 of 5 substations favour KW. The plan's rule for choosing between them makes R the candidate, because C4 is not below zero.
  • Post hoc, KW-fast. Against K0: -0.109 (-0.190 to -0.047) and -0.113 (-0.143 to -0.086), 5 of 5 each. Against R: -0.0175 (-0.0405 to +0.0038) and -0.0244 (-0.0349 to -0.0141), 5 of 5 each. Intervals are 95%. The arm was chosen from the gate's analytic recovery (the smallest step factor on the grid 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 giving at least 0.6), before any score of it was read. Only the docstring of FAST_SHAPE_FACTOR in e00115_arms.py and the file times of the private work folder record that order (the recovery search finished at 10:31 UTC and the KW-fast forecasts were written at 10:39 UTC on 20 October 2026); no commit predates the choice.
  • Exploratory (95%, scored year, D+1). KS minus KW 0.0000: the whole-day zero-mean shape adds nothing over the band levels (KS and KW are different arms, whose corrections differ by 0.0002 to 0.002 points on average and by at most 0.023 at D5, which is why their scores agree to four decimals). KS1 (one level and one transient, no bands) minus KW -0.0492 (-0.0930 to -0.0158, 4 of 5): bands may not be needed. KW-nomid minus KW +0.0008: the midday shape does not hurt. KW-pl52 minus K0 -0.0337 and minus KW +0.0412: last year's shape gains about half as much as the current one, so the shape drifts. K0-lb minus K0 -0.0027.
  • Telemetry delay (assumed 3.5 hours, never measured). KW minus K0 is -0.0751 at 0 hours, -0.0632 at 24, and -0.0634 at 33. K0's own score rises from 2.524 at 3.5 hours to 2.612 at 24 and 2.644 at 33 (all on the rows the delay arms share; K0 is 2.525 on the rows it shares with the references).
  • References, scored year, on shared rows (D+1, all leads). K0 2.525 and 2.812; KW 2.450 and 2.757; R 2.436 and 2.743; KW-fast 2.412 and 2.725; BG2 2.535 and 2.780; Xlag-d 2.638 and 2.877; X-nl+K 2.693 and 2.934; GAM-0 2.830 and 2.951; climatology 3.826 and 3.804; manual heuristic 3.520 and 3.497. KW minus BG2: -0.0855 (-0.2255 to +0.0625) at D+1 and -0.0230 (-0.1621 to +0.1212) over all leads, not like for like. K0 rebuilt with a refitted spread is 0.011 worse than experiment 111's stored GAM-K over all leads (2.812 against 2.800).
  • D9 beside the decision substations. D+1 scored year: K0 2.194, KW 2.146; replicate months: 1.942 and 1.860.

docs.title: Winter (November to March; post hoc, because scores were already read)
docs.text:
KW does not lose to K0 in winter, but it loses to R, and KW-fast does not lose to either. The scored year holds one independent winter (2025-26). The replicate months hold two winter months of a second one (December 2024 and February 2025), so those rows say little. A cold-snap day is a local day from November to March whose mean ERA5 temperature at the substation is below 3 °C; the rule was fixed before cold-snap scores were read, a fact that only the docstring of cold_snap_mask in e00115_report.py records, because no commit predates the scores. The scored year has 25, 25, 18, 7, and 5 cold-snap days at D10, D11, D14, D16, and D5, so D16 and D5 have too few days to read alone. The replicate months have 6 to 8 per substation in one or two calendar months, so their cold-snap intervals are degenerate and are not quoted.

Scored year, D+1 Winter Winter evening Cold-snap days KW minus K0 -0.112 (-0.155 to -0.074), 5 of 5 -0.056 (-0.111 to -0.005), 4 of 5 -0.148 (-0.222 to -0.103), 5 of 5 R minus K0 -0.136 (-0.166 to -0.099), 5 of 5 -0.134 (-0.181 to -0.084), 4 of 5 -0.134 (-0.196 to -0.091), 4 of 5 KW minus R +0.024 (+0.004 to +0.055), 0 of 5 +0.078 (+0.019 to +0.150), 0 of 5 -0.014 (-0.043 to +0.023), 4 of 5 KW-fast minus K0 -0.155 (-0.192 to -0.115), 5 of 5 -0.125 (-0.177 to -0.073), 5 of 5 -0.201 (-0.275 to -0.176), 5 of 5 KW-fast minus R -0.020 (-0.031 to -0.010), 5 of 5 +0.009 (-0.019 to +0.038), 2 of 5 -0.067 (-0.092 to -0.052), 4 of 5 KW minus BG2 -0.330 (-0.426 to -0.255), 5 of 5 not covered -0.499 (-0.955 to -0.023), 4 of 5

Intervals are 95%, resampling whole months. The winter row for KW minus R is a winter loss for KW at the tuned step, particularly in the evening, so under the rule that a winter loss holds an arm back even when the annual mean improves, KW is held back in favour of R until a faster shape state is confirmed. Annual gains and winter gains point the same way for K0, KW, and KW-fast; the loss is only KW against R.

docs.title: The gate
docs.text:
The gate failed its blocking test 1 on the first run, and the first run is kept. All five tests ran on the tuning months. The forecasts of every period were built before tests 1 and 2 ran, but no replicate or scored score was read until the gate had run.

  • Test 1, an injected change is recovered: failed. Median share of the injected change that KW's day-ahead correction carries on days 8 to 14: 0.350 of a +3-point evening shift and 0.295 of a morning peak moved earlier, against a floor of 0.4. K0 recovers 0.196 and 0.000; R recovers 0.422 and 0.482. The tuned filter's own formula, evaluated on a complete stream, predicts 0.350 and 0.295, so the code is right and the tuned shape state is slow. The brief's 0.6 to 1.0 target was not reached either.
  • Post hoc reading of test 1 for KW-fast: 0.621 and 0.720, equal to its expected values. This is a labelled post hoc reading and never counts as passing the pre-registered gate.
  • Test 2, no false shape on clean data: passed. On permuted real streams and synthetic streams, the refitted shape step falls to between 4e-5 and 1e-4 points² per day (0.1% to 2% of the tuned values), the refitted shape's root mean square is at most 0.053 points, and KW's score is within +0.0000 and -0.0051 of K0's.
  • Tests 3 to 5: passed. K0 reproduces experiment 111's stored output exactly (worst difference 0 in the stored quantiles and 2e-14 against the code in float64); a change after the cut changes no forecast (0 maximum difference, including the ensemble runs and the recipe); the shape sums to zero in its blocks to 1e-14.

docs.title: Predictions against results
docs.text:
• Held: C1 between -0.03 and -0.10 in both periods at 5 of 5 substations; largest in winter (-0.112 against -0.051 from April to October); at least half of the gain at 48 to 144 hours; C2 between 0 and -0.04; C4 within 0.03 and kappa 0.75; KS minus KW within 0.02; KW-pl52 minus K0 above KW minus K0; tails within the limits (largest coverage gaps at q05, q95, q01, and q99: 1.60, 1.33, 1.46, and 1.12 points).
  • Failed: the gain was largest in the night band (-0.154), not the evening band (-0.059); KW was not worse than K0 at midday (-0.004 scored, -0.026 replicate) and KW-nomid did not beat KW; C3 at D+1 was -0.055, not under 0.02; R75 minus K0 on the median's error was -0.177, not within 0.02 of the screening's -0.14; the gate's test 1.
  • Not run: the past-weather check against experiment 106's A2 residual streams, which the plan listed among the first arms to cut.

docs.title: Decision rule and verdict
docs.text: The verdict is C1's label, capped by the gate. Without the cap, C1 meets supported: below zero in both periods with 5 of 5 substations better, the scored-year interval wholly below zero, and the estimate (0.075) above the 0.03 threshold. With the failed blocking test the plan's rule gives inconclusive. The plan's follow-on rules give three readings: KW-lb does not replace KW (C2 is zero); R, not KW, is the simpler candidate (C4 is not below zero); and a winter loss against R holds KW back.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast per site at D+1 (scored year, points). KW: D10 +0.002, D11 -0.031, D14 +0.022, D16 -0.010, D5 -0.114. K0: +0.003, -0.022, +0.014, -0.014, -0.097. R: D5 -0.037. The shift of the mean at D5 is the only one over 0.04, and KW-shift (K0's quantiles moved by KW's correction) has K0's values by construction.
  • Error of the mean and median forecast beside each contrast (scored year, D+1). C1: median -0.148, mean -0.150. C2: -0.0001 and -0.0001. C3: -0.089 and -0.089. C4: +0.029 and +0.029. The quantile score, the median's error, and the mean's error point the same way for every contrast.
  • Triggers that fired. (1) A control failed: gate test 1, and the screening's R75 reproduction (-0.177 against -0.14 within 0.02). (2) A result contradicted its prediction: C3 at D+1, the midday band, and KW-nomid, listed above, each with an explanation in this page that no test has confirmed. (6) C1's 98.75% interval (width 0.086, scored year) is under a third as wide as the sister interval GAM-K minus GAM-0 from experiment 111 (0.291), because the sister contrast is four times larger. Triggers 3, 4, 5, and 7 did not fire: no sign differs across the quantile score and the errors; no leave-one-substation-out run flips a sign (C1 stays between -0.066 and -0.085 in the scored year); no nested arm beats its container (K0, which is KW with the shape step set to zero, does not beat KW, and KW-day does not beat KW); no later design depends on C1. Trigger 5 is a near miss: KW-fast beats KW by 0.038 and KS1 beats KW by 0.049 at D+1, but neither arm is nested in KW (KW-fast is KW with a different shape step, and KS1 has one level instead of four), so the trigger's definition does not cover them; the result says the marginal-likelihood step is not the best step for the score, and the audit may read it otherwise. The Opus audit these triggers call for has not run: status done means the runs and this page are finished, and the audit and a prose review are conditions of the merge. Its findings and their triage are added to the pull request.
  • Tails (scored year, KW, D+1). Coverage minus nominal: q01 +1.41, q05 +1.53, q95 -1.13, and q99 -1.11 percentage points; pinball loss 0.190, 0.617, 0.656, and 0.210. No curtailment cost: experiment 87 found no event at the MW Primaries that could rank forecasts. Threshold-weighted CRPS is not computed, because studies.tail_calibration has no function for it.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The scored year chose the idea's form, the tuning and replicate months interleave, the 3.5-hour delay is assumed, the switching masks are hindsight, the analysis proxy is the control member of the latest run, and there are five substations and one independent winter.
  • Inherited from experiment 111: the calibration of ENS to past weather is fitted per hour band on the tuning months and applied in-sample there, which shrinks the daily error in the tuning stream and biases the shape step and kappa against this experiment; the pinned capacity reads hindsight weeks; the demand model's last training rows use past weather a live refit would not have; and the spread is fitted on the tuning months.
  • The tuned observation noise sits at the lower bound (0.05 points) at D9 and close to it at D16, D11, D10, and D5, so the filter nearly interpolates the readings. D14 alone has 0.57.
  • Generator series are not used. Two series with embedded generation are outside this experiment.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Rerun the shape state with its speed fixed in advance. Tune the shape step so the injected change is recovered at or above 0.6 within two weeks, state the floor before scoring, and score it against R in winter evenings, which is where KW lost.
  • If KW-fast holds its gain against R, test one level and transient with a shape (KS1), which scored 0.049 better than KW and has no hour bands to tune.
  • Measure the live telemetry delay. The shape state's gain and K0's score both depend on it.

docs.title: Substation cards
docs.text:
Provisional: fitted to past weather, forecast on ENS, screening run (KW, scored year). Each card shows the shape state by week and local half-hour, the working-day profile at D+1 with and without the shape, and the cold-snap panel (days counted by the rule above; "too few days to read" where fewer than 10). The forecast panels show eight fixed weeks, two per season, which were fixed by calendar before any score was read, plus the week with the largest mean absolute shape state (chosen from the shape alone). Each week panel shows the readings against the K0 and KW median and 5% to 95% bands.
