docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• Does a graph penalty on heating slopes alone, with a weight tuned for coverage and not for forecast skill, keep slope intervals calibrated? The heating-only arm worsened the real score by 0.006 and 0.001 points and spared scale and capacity, but still covered slopes only 68% of the time. Weights of 300 to 3,000 rows are untested for it.
  • A penalty on a single number such as PV capacity has to be scaled by the information that the data hold about that number. Here the capacity sum carries about 1,230 rows of information, and the per-interconnection weight of 510 rows at a setting of 10,000 is not small beside it.
  • The hierarchy work does not need a parameter graph. The real graph adds nothing over the three rewired graphs tried, and the penalty worsens the scored year's winter evening peak. A forecast-level hierarchy (a bulk supply point informed by its Primaries) is untouched by this result.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, KFE: a Kalman filter on the convex model's effects, on ENS
docs.text:
The 14-weight filter (KEZ) does not beat experiment 111's level-and-anomaly filter (GAM-K) at day D+1: it scored 0.015 points worse in the scored year (99% interval -0.013 to +0.048; 1 of 5 substations better), and it did no better in winter, on winter nights, or on cold days. A point is 1% of a substation's capacity, and a smaller score is better. The arm that switches the filter's correction off on holidays (KEZ-DT) is much worse on the 17 holiday days (+1.24 points), and the arm that halves it (KEZ-DTs) is not better either (+0.09), so the filter's correction still helps on holidays. The known-answer gate and control P4 both failed: the filter recovered an injected 30% rise in the weight on the solar panels (PV) and a 30% fall in the heating weights when the noise followed its own model, but not when the noise was resampled from real residuals, so the PV and heating weights are not interpretable, and P4 adds that the PV and holiday variances are not recovered (a holiday variance simulated at 0 was fitted between 9e-7 and 3e-2 per day in the first run). The verdict is inconclusive. The evidence supports keeping GAM-K's filter, and fitting a new filter's noise by a day-ahead likelihood with a wide bound on log q (the combined change improved KEZ by 0.127 points here; the two changes were made together). The scored-year interval excludes any gain over GAM-K above about 0.05, so the data answer "not worth porting"; inconclusive refers to what the weights mean.

This experiment re-implements the method of de Vilmarest et al. (2024) on our convex model and our data. They froze the fitted effects of an additive model of regional electricity load, put a random walk on one weight per effect, and fitted a diagonal noise matrix by likelihood. We applied the same idea to the convex model of the differentiable-physics series at 6 Primary substations, driven by ECMWF ensemble (ENS) weather forecasts (ECMWF is the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts), with the noise choices of de Vilmarest and Goude (2022) and the greedy likelihood search of the R package viking. Everything builds on experiment 111, whose monthly fits, calibration, and forecasts the experiment reuses, and the code is the module studies.dp_effects_filter in PR 1407.

The question was whether a filter that lets 14 weights drift beats a filter that lets one level per hour band drift. In the tables GK is GAM-K, KEZ is the 14-weight filter with an anomaly state, KE is the same without the anomaly, KEZ-Q0 moves only the level, and KEZ-QI shares one step variance between the weights. The weights multiply the fitted effects of the convex model (the level, the daily profile of each day type, the heating response, the PV capacity, and the holiday effects). A "point" is 1% of a substation's effective capacity, and a score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles (smaller is better). The experiment scored the day after the forecast is made (D+1, leads of 15 to 39 hours) over the five decision substations D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16, with D9 beside them, on the 292 daily runs of the scored year (2025-07-02 to 2026-06-29) and on the replicate months (the even months of 2024-07 to 2025-06). The noise matrix and the spread were fitted on the odd months of 2024-07 to 2025-06 only.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Verdict: inconclusive. The known-answer gate failed, which caps the verdict (decision rule below). The planned contrast C1 shows no gain either way: +0.015 in the scored year and +0.021 in the replicate months.
  • GAM-K is reproduced: 2.800 points over leads 0.5 to 168 hours in the scored year, as in experiment 111, and GK minus GAM-0 is -0.152 points (-0.264 to -0.039) there, against -0.151 in experiment 111. Controls P0 to P3 pass (see Controls).
  • Planned contrasts at D+1 (99% intervals from resampling whole calendar months, paired; "k of 5" counts decision substations where the first-named arm scores better):

| Contrast | Scored year | Replicate months | |---|---|---| | C1, KEZ minus GK | +0.015 (-0.013 to +0.048), 1 of 5 | +0.021 (-0.068 to +0.115), 1 of 5 | | C2, KE minus GK | +0.180 (+0.046 to +0.305), 0 of 5 | +0.166 (+0.041 to +0.318), 2 of 5 | | C3, KEZ minus KE | -0.164 (-0.267 to -0.048), 5 of 5 | -0.145 (-0.226 to -0.049), 4 of 5 | | C4, KEZ minus KEZ-Q0 (descriptive) | -0.006 (-0.035 to +0.023), 3 of 5 | -0.045 (-0.124 to +0.052), 3 of 5 | | C5, KEZ minus KEZ-QI | -0.010 (-0.066 to +0.032), 3 of 5 | -0.026 (-0.192 to +0.072), 3 of 5 |

  • Absolute scores, scored year, D+1 and over leads 0.5 to 168 hours (five decision substations, shared rows): GK 2.521 and 2.800; KEZ 2.536 and 2.848; KE 2.701 and 3.039; KE-infl 2.558 and 2.799; KEZ-Q0 2.543 and 2.805; KEZ-QI 2.546 and 2.828; KEZ-DT 2.577 and 2.887; KEZ-1s 2.663 and 2.955; KEZ without the PV weight 2.508 and 2.841; shift-only check (KEZ's correction with GK's spread) 2.540 and 2.844. Replicate months: GK 2.412 and 2.735; KEZ 2.433 and 2.836.
  • References on the rows they share with KEZ (scored year, D+1 and all leads): BG2 2.535 and 2.780, so KEZ minus BG2 is +0.015 (-0.111 to +0.142) at D+1 and +0.066 (-0.063 to +0.196) overall; lagged XGBoost (Xlag-d) 2.637 and 2.877; lagless XGBoost with the filter (X-nl+K) 2.692 and 2.934; GAM-0 2.830 and 2.951; the manual heuristic 3.520 and 3.497; climatology 3.826 and 3.804. KEZ minus X-nl+K is -0.127 (-0.239 to -0.018) at D+1; the other contrasts against references are in results_scored.json in the private data folder.
  • What each group of weights does (95% intervals, scored year, D+1, drop-one arms minus KEZ): without the profile weights +0.060 (+0.022 to +0.095), without the heating weights +0.032 (+0.015 to +0.047), without the holiday weight -0.001 (-0.011 to +0.011), without the PV weight -0.028 (-0.046 to -0.010; replicate months -0.013, -0.060 to +0.042). KEZ without the PV weight minus GK is -0.013 (-0.027 to +0.002) in the scored year and +0.008 (-0.070 to +0.073) in the replicate months.
  • The likelihood and bound change together were worth 0.127 points (KEZ-1s minus KEZ, scored year, +0.084 to +0.171; replicate months +0.083, +0.031 to +0.139). The first run fitted the noise by the one-step likelihood and the narrower bound on log q (a pre-fit clarification, below), and KEZ-1s is that run. The two changes were made together, so this experiment cannot say which one caused the gain. KEZ-Q0 (level only, day-ahead-fitted noise) scored worse than GK, whose hyperparameters come from the one-step likelihood, by +0.022 (scored year) and +0.066 (replicate months), which points the other way.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• P0, initial state and vintages: the five long-history substations use a real-time capacity vintage at every monthly cut (the vintage origin is 21 days before the cut); D9 uses a hindsight level scaled back at the growth prior for its cuts before 2025-04. The level and anomaly start at GAM-K's stationary values, and a non-level weight starts with a standard deviation of 0.1 of the effect.
  • P1, nesting: KEZ with only the level weights moving equals experiment 111's filter: the level and anomaly differ from studies.dp_assimilation's by at most 1.4e-14 in float64, and the quantiles of arm GK equal experiment 111's stored gamk_tuning files exactly on 13,440 rows per substation.
  • P2, decomposition: the regressors plus the remainder equal the fit's prediction to 1.4e-14 points for every member of every tuning run at every substation, and the PV regressor is exactly 0 at night.
  • P3, causality: changing every reading after the cutoff, or every ensemble run issued after the origin, leaves the filter's state and the members' forecasts unchanged; the noise fit's stream is empty after 2025-07-01, and the regressor scale uses the tuning months' readings only.
  • P4, known-q recovery: failed. A stream simulated from known weight variances (PV 1e-4, heating 1e-6, profile and holiday 0 per day, in weight units) on the real regressors and the filter's own noise was refitted at each decision substation. Heating was recovered within a factor of 3 at all 5 substations (fitted 0.4e-6 to 2.8e-6), but PV was recovered within the factor only at D5 (2.95e-4; the other four fitted 0.9e-5 to 2.7e-5, 4 to 11 times too small), and the holiday weight, simulated at 0, was fitted above the bar of 1e-7 at all 5 (0.9e-6 to 3.2e-2). A failed control is a trigger for the audit. A Sonnet diagnosis of the control found no plumbing fault: a naive dense Kalman filter matches the module's likelihoods, and the bounds, scale mapping, and starting covariance are right. A post hoc repeat over 10 seeds per substation (50 fits; no bar changed, and the first run's result stands) gave a median fitted PV variance of 7.4e-5 against the true 1e-4, with 58% of fits within a factor of 3 (10th to 90th percentile 6e-8 to 2.4e-4); a median heating variance of 6.8e-7 against 1e-6, 62% within the factor; and, for the holiday group simulated at 0, a median of 4.4e-6 with none of the 50 fits under the bar of 1e-7 (10th to 90th percentile 6e-7 to 6e-3). The median fit is slightly low (0.74 of the true PV variance, 0.68 of the heating variance), but the scatter runs over two to three orders of magnitude (10th to 90th percentile 6e-8 to 2.4e-4 for PV and 1.2e-7 to 5.7e-5 for heating), so the pre-registered bar of a factor of 3 asked for more than the fit delivers. One reading is that the variance of a rare effect is not identifiable from the likelihood (the holiday group is active at 480 half-hours in the tuning months).

docs.title: Winter, cold snaps, and holidays
docs.text:
• Winter first: the evidence holds one winter that chose nothing (2025-26, scored) and one winter whose odd months set the noise matrix and the spread (2024-25, with the even months as the replicate). No arm beats GK in winter. KEZ minus GK at D+1: winter (November to March) +0.013 (-0.041 to +0.073), 2 of 5; winter evening peaks (16:00 to 20:00) 0.000 (-0.121 to +0.070), 3 of 5; winter nights (00:00 to 06:00) -0.026 (-0.069 to +0.003), 3 of 5. Over all leads KEZ is worse in winter by 0.108 (-0.031 to +0.414). No winter interval excludes zero. The cold-snap point estimate (+0.298 at D+1, over 9 days) would trigger the winter cap of the plan at partly supported, which is moot because the verdict is already inconclusive.
  • Cold snaps: a cold-snap day is a local November to March day whose mean ERA5 temperature is below the 10th percentile of such days from 2019-09 to 2024-06 at the site (thresholds 2.08 to 3.36 degrees Celsius). The scored winter holds 2 to 14 such days per substation (D5 2, D10 11, D11 11, D14 10, D16 2, D9 14), so every comparison says too few days and has no interval. Those counts are days in the scored rows: every fifth day of the scored year is a stride day that is never scored, so the weight figures, which mark every cold-snap day of the winter, show more spans than the counts. The point estimates favour GK at D10, D11, and D14 by 0.2 to 0.6 points (figure above).
  • Cold winter nights (the operator-visible case): a cold winter night is 22:00 to 08:00 local after a cold-snap day. The scored winter holds 2 to 14 such nights per substation (D5 2, D10 11, D11 11, D14 10, D16 2, D9 14), too few for an interval. The mean quantile score of GK and KEZ on those nights at D+1 is 2.168 and 2.462 pooled over the five decision substations; by substation GK and KEZ score D5 1.593 and 1.698, D10 2.394 and 2.332, D11 2.755 and 3.674, D14 1.471 and 1.556, D16 1.821 and 1.916, so KEZ is worse at 4 of 5 and much worse at D11, where both filters under-forecast the observed night (figure below).
  • KEZ-DTs on winter nights scores -0.023 (-0.045 to -0.003) against GK at D+1 (95%, uncorrected, one of many exploratory intervals), and against KEZ it is within 0.002 on winter rows.
  • Holiday days (KEZ-DT, pre-fit clarification): KEZ-DT leaves holiday-day readings out of the filter and sets the level and anomaly corrections to 0 on holiday targets. KEZ-DT minus KEZ on the 17 holiday days of the scored year is +1.242 (+0.623 to +1.832), 0 of 5 substations better (C6), and +1.222 on the replicate months (too few days: 14). On all other days it is -0.012 (-0.025 to +0.001), within the non-inferiority margin of 0.02 (C6b). The carried level helps on holidays, so the idea that the filter carries the wrong level into holidays is not supported by this arm. An exploratory arm added after the results, KEZ-DTs (KEZ's filter with the level and anomaly corrections halved on holiday targets, a post hoc choice of 0.5 that the tuning months, with 2 to 3 holiday days, could not tune), scores +0.091 (-0.015 to +0.208) against KEZ on the same 17 holiday days and -0.000 (-0.001 to +0.000) on other days, so a halved correction is no better than the full one; against GK it is -0.058 (-0.326 to +0.178) on holiday days and +0.019 (-0.004 to +0.045) at D+1 overall.

docs.title: The known-answer gate
docs.text:
• What it tested: each draw built a synthetic stream on the real regressors of one decision substation over 2024-07 to 2025-06, injected a known path (S1: the PV weight rising by 30% over 180 days; S2: the heating weights falling by 30% over 90 days; S3: both; S0: nothing), added noise, refitted the whole noise matrix, and ran the filter. Noise came in two forms (the filter's own noise model, and a circular month-block resample of the substation's real tuning-year residuals) and the regressors came in two conditions (exact, and with weather error: the stream built from ERA5 and CAMS and the filter given the analysis proxy's regressors). A reading passes if at least 80% of 100 draws pass.
  • Result: blocking readings 1, 3, 4, and 5 failed. In the filter's own noise model, PV tracking passed (0.87 to 0.93 of draws recovered 70% of the change), heating tracking passed (0.98 to 1.00 recovered 50%, a non-blocking reading), cross-talk passed (0.96 to 1.00), and the filter beat GK on the stream in every draw; only the no-false-movement reading failed, passing in 2 to 3 of 100 draws against a bar of 80 (the wander is modest: on a clean stream the heating weight wandered by a median 0.15 and the holiday weight by 0.13, against a bar of 0.10). With resampled real residuals, PV tracking passed in 0.16 to 0.21 of draws, heating tracking in 0.44 to 0.53, no-false-movement in none, and cross-talk in 0.37 to 0.51; the forecast-skill reading passed in the PV scenarios (0.86 to 0.90 in S1 and S3) and failed in S2 (0.26 to 0.30).
  • Power check: the injected PV change was 1.5 to 14.7 posterior standard deviations (D10 1.5, D16 1.8, D5 4.5, D14 4.9, D11 14.7) and the heating change 0.9 to 3.4, so both weights are labelled "not interpretable". The doubled-amplitude rows were added as a check after the first gate run (post hoc, no bar changed): At doubled amplitude (the PV weight rising by 60% in the S1x2 scenario and the heating weights falling by 60% in S2x2, 20 draws per substation; S3x2 was not run), PV tracking passed in 0.98 to 1.00 of draws and heating tracking in 0.99 to 1.00 in the filter's own noise model, and in only 0.39 to 0.42 (PV) and 0.55 to 0.62 (heating) with resampled real residuals, still under the bar of 0.80.
  • The maintainer's process rule was that the replicate and scored forecasts run after the failed gate and that the contrasts are published as descriptive, with the verdict capped at inconclusive. The first-run gate fits are kept. Not run (reported, not blocking): the level step, the holiday step, the gate with the shared-step noise matrix, the 10% and 20% amplitude rows, and the doubled-amplitude S3x2 scenario.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• A Sonnet audit ran (re-derived C1 to C5 from the stored predictions; leakage, spread, held values, and the gate failure checked). It found no bug in the forecasts, scoring, or likelihood. Its findings on the write-up are applied above.
  • Bar calibration. Two gate readings failed on bars the filter cannot meet even when correct: the P4 zero-variance bar of 1e-7 is below the optimiser's grid (a true zero fits at 8e-7, a GREEDY_GRID value, the optimiser's grid of candidate variances), and the S0 no-false-movement bar of 0.10 is tighter than the filter's own posterior spread for the heating weights (0.09 to 0.33). The failures that stand are PV and heating tracking on resampled real residuals, and the holiday variances (fitted 1e-3 to 3e-2).
  • Median forecast minus mean forecast, per substation (all leads, scored year, points; GK / KEZ): D5 -0.117 / -0.088, D10 -0.037 / -0.041, D11 -0.043 / -0.008, D14 +0.015 / +0.019, D16 +0.002 / -0.010, D9 -0.014 / -0.005. The spread shifts no forecast by more than 0.12 points.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each contrast (D+1, scored year, KEZ-first contrast of the mean forecast's absolute error): C1 +0.012, C2 +0.250, C3 -0.238, C4 -0.030, C5 -0.006. Every sign agrees with the quantile-score contrast.
  • Triggers that fired (the seven triggers of the plan): 1, controls failed (the known-answer gate, and P4's known-q recovery for the PV and holiday weights); 2, a result contradicts its own prediction (C1 was predicted at -0.02 to -0.10; the PV weight explains part of the scored-year shortfall at three substations (D10, D11, D16) but not the replicate months, where the level noise fitted by the day-ahead likelihood is worse than GAM-K's, KEZ-Q0 minus GK +0.066; it is not settled); 4, leaving one substation out flips a sign (C1 in the replicate months turns negative without D5; C4 in the scored year turns positive without D11; C5 in the replicate months turns positive without D11; each flip is a move of about 0.01, inside an interval of plus or minus 0.05 or more, and C1 in the scored year is positive whichever substation is left out); 5, a nested arm beats the arm that contains it (GK beats KEZ by 0.015, inside the noise); 6, the replicate months' C1 interval (half-width 0.09) is about four times as wide as the sister experiment's. Triggers 3 and 7 did not fire. Triggers 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6 therefore call for an audit.
  • Tails at D+1, scored year (coverage at q01, q05, q95, q99, and pinball loss at each): GK 0.020, 0.062, 0.942, 0.982 and 0.189, 0.635, 0.656, 0.206; KEZ 0.017, 0.055, 0.945, 0.982 and 0.187, 0.646, 0.672, 0.211. KEZ is within 0.7 percentage points of GK's coverage at every tail. Threshold-weighted CRPS and curtailment cost were not computed (experiment 87 found no event that could rank forecasts).

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Caveats: the 3.5-hour telemetry delay is assumed; the hindsight switching masks apply in scoring; five decision substations and one winter of evidence that chose nothing; collinear weights can offset each other, and the posterior standard deviation is probably overconfident; the capacity vintage for D9 at the tuning cuts is hindsight (D9's vintages start in 2025-04); the in-sample ENS calibration, the pinned capacity reading hindsight weeks, ERA5 in the convex model's last training rows, and the spread fitted on the tuning months are inherited from experiment 111; the gain reported by de Vilmarest et al. is on regional load. The forecasts ran on module commit 2e356581b of PR 1407; if its review changes the module, what the change affects re-runs and these first-run results stay on this page. The scripts import the module from packages/studies.
  • What to try next: KEZ without the PV weight is the only one of the nine arms that scored below GK in the scored year, and it did not in the replicate months, so a filter that moves the profile and heating weights while fixing PV is a cheap follow-up. A day-ahead likelihood fit for GK's own level-and-anomaly filter is the fairer comparison for KEZ-Q0 (KEZ-Q0 minus GK is +0.022, +0.006 to +0.035).

docs.title: Pre-registered design
docs.text:
• Weights: 14 (level per hour band, profile scale per day type, heating per hour band, PV capacity, holiday), standardised, with an AR(1) anomaly per hour band in the arms that use it; noise matrix per substation fitted on the tuning months under a prior shared across substations; filter reads residuals at least 3.5 hours old, and no switching mask.
  • Arms: GK (experiment 111's filter, reproduced); KE (no anomaly); KE-infl (KE with the observation noise held at the square root of 27 times KE's); KEZ (the decision arm); KEZ-Q0 (only the level moves); KEZ-QI (one step variance for every weight); KEZ-drop-g (g in profile, heating, PV, holiday); KEZ-DT (holiday days treated apart, added as a clarification); KEZ-1s (the first run's KEZ, kept). The KEZ-sh arm (experiment W1's shape state) is a follow-up with no number, because W1 has not merged a tested shape state.
  • Decision rule: the verdict is C1's label (supported needs the scored-year 99% interval wholly below zero, an estimate of at least 0.05 points, at least 4 of 5 substations better in both periods, and C5 below zero), capped at inconclusive if the known-answer gate fails. The smallest gain worth porting is 0.05 points at D+1.
  • Predictions against the outcome: C1 was predicted at -0.02 to -0.10 and observed +0.015 (failed); C2 within +/-0.05, observed +0.180 (failed); C3 at -0.02 to -0.08 under 24 hours and under 0.03 in size at D+1, observed -0.134 and -0.164 (failed); C4, KEZ-Q0 within 0.02 of GK, observed +0.022 (failed narrowly); C5 at -0.01 to -0.06, observed -0.010 (held, with an interval that includes zero). The gate's readings 1 and 3 to 5 were predicted to pass and failed with real residuals; reading 2 (heating tracking), predicted likeliest to fail, passed in the filter's own noise model. The fitted steps were predicted at 0.1 to 0.4 a year for the level and holiday weights, 0.02 to 0.15 for PV, and under 0.05 for the profile scales; observed, the level steps are 1 to 70 points a year, PV 0.02 to 1.8, and profile 0.07 to 0.55. The PV weight was predicted to stay within 0.15 of 1 at 4 of 5 substations; its median over the scored year is within 0.15 of 1 at 2 (D14 0.95 and D16 0.89; D5 0.82, D10 0.74, D11 0.76).
  • Three clarifications were added before any replicate or scored forecast, each recorded in the plan commits of PR 1409: the winter breakdown and the cold-snap rule (maintainer's winter-first rule); the day-type-aware arm KEZ-DT; and the lead-matched noise likelihood, which replaced the one-step likelihood after the first tuning-month fit scored KEZ at 2.524 against 2.420 for GK at D+1 (in-sample, tuning months) with the PV and level weights at the upper bound of log q. The change also widened the bound on log q to that of studies.dp_assimilation. The first run's KEZ is the arm KEZ-1s.

docs.title: Substation cards
docs.text:
Provisional: fitted to past weather on a screening run, forecast on ENS. Each decision substation (D5, D10, D11, D14, D16, with D9 beside them) has the figures above for its own panel: its filtered weights over the scored year, with bands and the holiday and cold-snap days marked (the three weight figures), its fitted step per year for every weight (the step figure), its score on cold-snap days (the cold-snap figure), and four example weeks (below).

  • Weak identification: a heating slope is known to about 38% of its size at real noise (experiment 113), and the gate labels the PV and heating weights "not interpretable", so no weight on a card is a measurement of that substation.
  • The PV weight against the vintage: the middle 90% of the scored year's PV weights (5th to 95th percentile) run 0.68 to 1.08 at D5, 0.42 to 1.07 at D10, 0.73 to 0.79 at D11, 0.62 to 1.04 at D14, 0.55 to 1.15 at D16, and 0.42 to 1.02 at D9, so the implied PV capacity is mostly below the pinned vintage capacity. D9's vintage is hindsight at the tuning cuts, so its PV weight is the least informative. The hindsight capacity estimates of experiment 45 are not drawn beside the weights.
  • Weights worth a second look: D16's holiday weight sits at the clip of -1 from January to March (days 184 to 275 of the figure), and D11's holiday weight sits near 1.7 from late August to mid-December with a band that reaches the clip of 3. Both follow from a weight that updates only on the few holiday half-hours, so they are not measurements. D5's weekday profile weight rises from about 0.35 to 1.2 and falls to 0.55 within the year.
  • Cross-substation comparison: the step figure shows, for every weight, the fitted random-walk step at all six substations side by side; the level steps range from 1 to 70 points a year, the holiday and PV steps differ by more than 10 times between substations, and the profile steps stay under 0.6 of their effect a year.
  • Example weeks, fixed in the plan before any score was read (the weeks beginning 2025-07-14, 2025-10-13, 2026-01-12, and 2026-04-13; D+1 forecasts chained from each 09:00 UTC origin; median with 80% and 90% bands against the observed series, GK and KEZ side by side):

docs.title: Differentiable physics, ENC: a weather-patch encoder around each Primary, on ENS
docs.text:
We asked whether a small neural network that reads the weather forecast for the boxes around a Primary substation, and not only the box the substation sits in, would lower the error of our current demand forecast (GAM-K, the generalised additive demand model with a Kalman filter that was fitted in experiment 111). The weather forecast is the 51-member ensemble (ENS) of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). We trained the network on one year of GAM-K's forecasts and scored it on the other year. We then swapped the two years: direction F1 is scored on 2025-26 and direction F2 on 2024-25. We also trained copies that saw only the centre box, the box of a distant substation, or the same substation's weather from another date, to find out where any gain comes from. The network lowered the quantile score (a pinball-loss score of the 11 forecast quantiles, in points of the substations' effective capacity, where smaller is better) by 0.062 in F1 and 0.035 in F2. The copy that read another date's weather kept about two-thirds of that gain, and the copy that read only the centre box (the one ENS grid cell that holds the substation) kept nearly all of it (0.060 and 0.038 points). Most of the gain therefore does not come from the surrounding boxes, and is probably a recalibration of GAM-K's quantiles, which a later experiment has to test.

The verdict is inconclusive: the known-answer gate failed its one rerun, and the pre-registered plan, written before any scored-year prediction, caps the verdict there. The gate checks that an injected signal can be found, and that controls which cannot see the signal do not find it. On the point estimates the pre-registered label would have been supported (it would be partly supported if C3's F2 interval, which includes zero, is read as not below zero). Either label would mislead, because the centre-only control scores as well as the full patch. Experiment 119 is not for production.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
The arms. ENC-c is the network with the full 37-cell patch, correcting GAM-K's quantiles. ENC-c0 sees only the centre box, ENC-cps the patch of the farthest decision substation, and ENC-cpt the same substation's patch from another date (the placebos). ENC-r uses the full patch to replace GAM-K's temperature and irradiance (through GAM-K's own sensitivities), and ENC-r0 sees only the centre box. The five decision substations are D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16.

  • C1, the correction against GAM-K, is -0.062 [-0.090, -0.033] in F1 and -0.035 [-0.060, -0.017] in F2 (99% intervals, points of capacity), with 5 of 5 decision substations better in each year and the mean absolute error of the median moving the same way (-0.102 and -0.061). Leaving any one substation out changes C1 by at most 0.005. The pre-registered smallest gain worth porting is 0.04 points, and F2 sits below it.
  • C2, the patch against the centre box alone, is -0.002 [-0.010, +0.007] and +0.003 [-0.003, +0.010]. The surrounding boxes add nothing the centre box lacks, although the plan predicted -0.01 to -0.05.
  • C3, the right date against another date, is -0.019 [-0.036, -0.006] and -0.013 [-0.028, +0.002]. Date-aligned weather in the centre box accounts for about a third of C1. C3b, against the distant substation's patch, is -0.002 and +0.001 and is read as a leak-through warning, because the six patches share 12 to 30 of their 37 cells.
  • C4, the replacement through GAM-K's own sensitivities, is -0.037 [-0.053, -0.020] and -0.035 [-0.054, -0.019]. Its centre-only control scores the same (-0.037 and -0.036), and the gate shows ENC-r could not recover a small injection, so C4 carries no label.
  • ENC-c scores 2.739 in F1 and 2.698 in F2 against GAM-K's 2.800 and 2.733 (annual quantile score on shared rows, smaller is better). All arms, F1: GAM-K 2.800, ENC-c 2.739, ENC-c0 2.740, ENC-cps 2.740, ENC-cpt 2.758, ENC-r 2.763. F2: GAM-K 2.733, ENC-c 2.698, ENC-c0 2.696, ENC-cps 2.697, ENC-cpt 2.711, ENC-r 2.699. GAM-0 (no Kalman filter) scores 2.951 and 2.984 on the same rows.

Most of the gain survives when the network reads the wrong date's weather. ENC-cpt gains 0.043 (F1) and 0.022 (F2), 69% and 63% of C1. The centre-only ENC-c0 gains 0.060 and 0.038. The gain therefore comes from inputs that are not the weather of the right day: the lead, the hour, GAM-K's own forecast, and the centre box's values. The median shift of ENC-c against lead (cards below) follows the daily cycle. That pattern is consistent with a recalibration and does not prove one.

docs.title: Winter and the hard days
docs.text:
The gain is smaller in winter than over the year, and it is never a loss. In winter (November to March, by the run's month) C1 is -0.041 [-0.076, -0.020] in F1 and -0.027 [-0.042, -0.014] in F2. On winter evening peaks (16:00 to 20:00 UTC) C1 is -0.046 [-0.099, +0.004] and -0.049 [-0.067, -0.032]. The evidence holds two winters, one scored in each direction (2024-25 in F2 and 2025-26 in F1), so no winter row is a finding by itself. The pre-registered rule holds an arm back for a winter loss, and ENC-c has no winter loss.

On the hardest days the intervals are wide and carry no label. The coldest 5% of days (13 days in F1, 22 in F2) show C1 of -0.115 [-0.197, -0.039] and -0.057 [-0.133, +0.008], but C3 on the same days is -0.077 [-0.199, -0.015] and -0.043 [-0.124, +0.028]. The showery days (18 and 27) and the largest-error days (69 and 84, chosen on GAM-K's own outcomes) are in the figure. No subset has more than 84 days a year, and its days cluster in weather spells, so none carries a label.

The tail quantiles move towards their nominal levels, and the wrong-date copy does the same. In F1 the share of observations below the q01 quantile falls from 0.018 (GAM-K) to 0.013 (ENC-c and ENC-cpt), and in F2 from 0.015 to 0.011. The q99 share moves from 0.983 to 0.984 (F1) and from 0.987 to 0.990 (F2).

docs.title: The known-answer gate
docs.text:
The gate was redefined once after run 1 failed, and the rerun failed as well. Run 1 used the first-written gate: the controls ENC-c0 and ENC-cps recovered 140% and 136% of the injection, ENC-r recovered it at 1 of 5 substations, and the permuted-actual test of "no false gain" gave a gain of 0.56 points because GAM-K was never calibrated to its target. The redefinition (committed before the rerun) orthogonalised the injection against the non-patch inputs, sized ENC-r's injection per substation, and replaced the null target with GAM-K's median plus another run's residual.

In the rerun, ENC-c recovered the dense injection but missed the sparse one, and the controls and ENC-r failed. ENC-c recovers the dense 0.05-point injection (100%, 4 of 5 substations) and fails the sparse one (2 of 5, interval upper bound 0.000). ENC-r recovers 16% (1 of 5). The controls ENC-c0, ENC-cps, and ENC-cpt recover 59%, 89%, and 46% (the rule required under 20%, and ENC-cps is read as descriptive). On the null target ENC-c (+0.009) and ENC-r (-0.002) stay within 0.01 and the intervals include zero, and ENC-cpt misses by 0.003 (+0.013). The original clean-data test (at most 0.01 from GAM-K on the real targets) also fails for every arm (ENC-c +0.025, ENC-c0 +0.042, ENC-cps +0.026, ENC-cpt +0.026, ENC-r +0.015), because a real gain is not a false one. Reproduction (largest difference from GAM-K 0), causality (largest change 0 when later weather changes), the purge (0 violations), and the seed spread (0.008 points) pass. Run 1's readings and the redefinition are in gate_run1.json and the commit history.

docs.title: Substation cards
docs.text: Provisional: fitted to past weather, forecast on ENS, screening run. Patch weights are not identified individually (neighbouring cells share an ENS box); read the ring and east-west contrast, not one cell. No physical direction is claimed from one site. Each card shows the number of distinct ENS boxes in the patch, the learned weight of each box (the change in the median forecast per kelvin added to that box, with the five seeds' range in the tooltip), the median shift against lead, the cold-snap scores, and four example weeks fixed before any score was read (the Monday to Sunday weeks starting 2025-07-21, 2025-10-20, 2026-01-19, and 2026-04-20). The cold-snap panel uses the coldest 5% of days, and says "too few days" below 10 days.

docs.title: Plan, predictions, and what changed
docs.text:
Hypothesis and decision rule. The pre-registered plan is in the plan commit (c4430fd72). The verdict is C1's label (supported, small gain, partly supported, refuted, inconclusive), with a smallest gain worth porting of 0.04 points, a second year, 4 of 5 substations better, and C3 below zero in both years.

Predictions against outcome.

  • C1 (-0.02 to -0.08 overall, -0.03 to -0.10 day ahead, 3 to 5 of 5 substations, tail coverage within 3 and 1.5 points): held (-0.062 and -0.035; -0.062 and -0.038; 5 of 5; q01 coverage 0.013 and 0.011).
  • C2 (-0.01 to -0.05), C3 (-0.02 to -0.07), and C3b (about half of C3): failed (C2 -0.002 and +0.003; C3 -0.019 and -0.013; C3b -0.002 and +0.001).
  • C4 (-0.01 to -0.05, smaller than C1): the range held, and C4 was smaller than C1 in F1 (-0.037 against -0.062) but equal in F2 (-0.035 against -0.035).
  • C5 (coldest -0.10 to -0.40, showery -0.05 to -0.30, largest error -0.05 to -0.25 for ENC-c against ENC-cpt): failed (-0.077 and -0.043; -0.016 and -0.019; -0.036 and -0.011).

Deviations from the plan, all fixed before any scored-year prediction. The first nine runs of 2024-04 have no analysis-proxy week and experiment 111 never forecast them, so F1 trains on 447 runs, not 456. The run's half-hours reach 177 hours after initialisation, so the encoder reads 54 ENS steps, not 53. GAM-K for 2024-04 to 2024-06 was re-forecast from experiment 111's stored fits and reproduces its stored rows exactly. No decision substation is free of shared ENS cells, so the placebo ENC-cps uses the farthest decision substation. Settings: ENC-c uses c = 40 (the top of the grid) in both directions, with 11 and 4 epochs. ENC-r uses c = 0.4 with 1 epoch in F1 and c = 40 with 2 epochs in F2. Lambda is 0.5 throughout. The rows with switching events are left out of every score; the plan's "all-rows score beside" was not computed.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast, per substation (GAM-K's, the same for every arm): F1 D5 -0.117, D10 -0.037, D11 -0.043, D14 +0.015, D16 +0.002; F2 D5 -0.090, D10 -0.042, D11 -0.045, D14 +0.009, D16 +0.001. The encoder shifts the median and the mean together by construction, so it adds no spread-induced shift.
  • Mean absolute error of the median beside every quantile-score contrast: agrees in sign for C1 to C4 in both years.
  • Audit triggers that fired: trigger 1 (the gate's controls and ENC-r failed), trigger 2 (C2, C3, C3b, and C5 contradict the predictions, with an explanation recorded above and untested), and trigger 5 (ENC-c0 and ENC-cps score 0.003 and 0.001 better than ENC-c in F2, by their contrasts against GAM-K). An Opus audit is owed before the merge, and the manager runs it.
  • Triggers that did not fire: quantile score and mean absolute error disagree in sign (no), leaving one substation out flips a sign (no), a headline interval more than twice or under half a sister's (C1's 99% half-width of 0.029 against about 0.027 at 99% for the paired contrast of Part 4's experiment), and a later design depending on an unreplicated result (F2 replicates C1).

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Caveats. One frozen fit per direction, no refits. F2 reverses time, K0's 2025-26 fits saw more history than its 2024-25 fits, and ECMWF may have changed its model cycle between the years. The largest-error subset is selected on outcomes. ENC-r is first-order and applied after the filter. The encoder sees the member mean and spread, not 51 members, and the 3.5-hour delay is assumed. The inherited leaks of experiment 111 (the ENS calibration fitted on odd months, hindsight pinned capacity, ERA5 in the GAM's last training rows) apply to GAM-K and the encoder alike. The out-of-fold gain on the F1 training year (0.025 on the clean data) is smaller than the scored gain, and out-of-fold scores are optimistic.
  • What the next experiment should answer. Whether a plain recalibration of GAM-K's quantiles from lead, hour, and GAM-K's own forecast, with no weather at all, reproduces the placebo's gain of 0.043 and 0.022 points, and whether adding the centre box's dew point, pressure, precipitation, and member spread adds the remaining 0.019 and 0.013.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, SH: a convex library of shared daily shapes
docs.text:
In this experiment a library of shared daily shapes could not be shown to work: the test that checks whether the method can find a library that we plant failed, so the verdict is inconclusive. A Primary substation is the last electricity substation before the feeders that serve homes and businesses, and its daily profile is the average shape of its demand through the day, separately for weekdays, Saturdays, Sundays, and bank holidays. The library describes each substation's profile as a mix of three shared shapes plus a small substation-specific correction (the deviation). The test, called the known-answer gate, failed on 7 of its 10 lines. In the gate, with five Primaries and this noise, the fitted shapes changed with the starting point and the forecast score could not tell 2 shapes from 6.

Scores below are the quantile score (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of capacity, where 1 point is 1% of a series' capacity; lower is better), on the 12 months after a cut, and "scored year" is 2025-07 to 2026-06. In the scored year the library scored 0.001 points better than the fleet-mean model of experiment 109, which pulls every substation's profile towards one shared profile (98.33% interval −0.005 to +0.002), and 0.030 points worse than one profile per substation (interval +0.009 to +0.056). Most of the loss to the per-site profile came in winter: 0.068 points worse from November to March (interval +0.041 to +0.099). The library did not find the Economy 7 step as a shape of its own. Economy 7 is a tariff that switches night-time storage heating on at a fixed time, and the step is the jump in demand that follows at about 01:00. On cold winter nights the library's forecast reproduced between a tenth and a half of that step. Experiment 121's hand-built night-step arms are the comparison for a better route to the step.

We asked whether the Primary substations fall into a few kinds, so that each profile can be a mix of a few shared daily shapes instead of a pull towards one fleet-mean profile (the method is a non-negative matrix factorisation fitted by alternating constrained least squares, inside the convex demand model of experiment 109). We fitted 3 shapes (chosen on 2023-24 from 3 or 4) to five Primaries (D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16) on the two years before each of three cuts (2023-07-01, 2024-07-01, and 2025-07-01), and scored the 12 months after the last two. Before the scored fits, the gate asked whether the method recovers a library that we plant in synthetic substations with the real weather and noise; the gate failed. Afterwards we looked for the Economy 7 night step, which matters most to the network operator's trust in the forecast, in the shapes and in the forecasts.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. G is the per-site convex model, N the fleet-mean model (deviation penalty 3,000 rows), N-full complete pooling, SH the library (K = 3, deviation weight 1,000 rows, orthogonality weight 10 times the shape's data curvature, 5 seeds, headline seed the lowest training objective), SH-K1 one shape, SH-g0 no orthogonality penalty, SH-nodev no deviation, SH-wd weights per day type, and SH-all all years. Capacity is pinned as in experiment 109, there is no drift, and the lockdown and the 66 hand-filtered transfers are out. Rows are the 12 months after each cut, outside the hand-filtered switching masks, at the day-ahead lead. Weather is ERA5 and CAMS (estimates of past weather), so every arm is flattered alike.
  • Schedule. One frozen fit per cut and seed, no refits (the screening tier); intervals resample whole calendar months of stored predictions, paired across arms. The scored fits ran on the module version recorded as library_module_blob in work/fit_run_replicate_scored_tuning.json. The Opus module review has not yet happened, so a later change to the module is not reflected here.
  • C1, SH minus N. −0.001 points (98.33% interval −0.005 to +0.002) in the scored year, 4 of 5 substations better; −0.004 (−0.006 to −0.001) in the replicate year. The 0.05 smallest gain worth porting is far outside both intervals.
  • C2, SH minus G. +0.030 (+0.009 to +0.056) in the scored year, 1 of 5 substations better, so SH is worse than the per-site profile and the interval reaches the 0.05 margin; −0.007 (−0.039 to +0.025) in the replicate year. Leaving any one site out leaves C2 positive in the scored year (+0.013 without D16 to +0.044 without D10).
  • C3, SH minus SH-K1. +0.001 (−0.000 to +0.003) scored, −0.001 (−0.002 to +0.000) replicate: more than one shape adds nothing measurable.
  • Absolute scores, scored year, five sites (points of capacity). G 2.884, SH-K1 2.912, SH 2.914, N 2.915, SH-nodev 2.924, lagless XGBoost with solar offset 3.048, SH-all 3.063, manual heuristic 3.488, N-full 3.553, climatology 4.068. Replicate year: SH-all 3.053, SH 3.159, N 3.163, G 3.166, lagless XGBoost 3.199, manual heuristic 3.839, climatology 3.910.
  • Exploratory (95%). SH minus N-full −0.640 (−0.982 to −0.387): complete pooling is clearly worse. SH minus SH-g0 0.000 and SH-wd minus SH 0.000: the orthogonality penalty and per-day-type weights change nothing. SH minus SH-nodev −0.011 (−0.022 to +0.002). SH minus lagless XGBoost −0.135 (−0.375 to +0.082). SH-all minus SH +0.149 (−0.070 to +0.325) in the scored year and −0.106 (−0.366 to +0.110) in the replicate year.
  • Winter first. November to March, scored year: SH minus N +0.004 (−0.001 to +0.008), and +0.023 (+0.006 to +0.038) in the evening peak (16:00 to 20:00); SH minus G +0.068 (+0.041 to +0.099), and +0.077 (+0.045 to +0.124) on winter nights (23:00 to 07:00). In the replicate year the point estimates of the winter contrasts against N and G are within ±0.013 of zero (cold-snap rows excluded), with intervals of about ±0.07 against G. The scored-year winter loss to G is a reason to hold the library back whatever the annual mean does. The evidence holds 2 independent winters (2024-25 and 2025-26); the tuning winter chose the settings. A cold-snap day has a mean 6-hour-smoothed ERA5 temperature below 0 °C at the site: 20 site-days in the scored year and 25 in the replicate year, and the intervals on those rows are degenerate because the days fall in few months.
  • Tails. SH matches N at q01, q05, q95, and q99 within 0.002 coverage in every year and season. In the scored year q95 coverage was 83% (all rows) and 77% (November to March) for SH, and 73% for N-full in winter, so the upper tail is too low in winter. The residual spread of every arm comes from one earlier year of fits (the replica fit), which is a known weak point.

docs.title: The Economy 7 step and the shapes
docs.text:
• No shape of the library is a night step. The rise at 00:30 (the half-hour that ends at 01:00) is 0.061, 0.011, and −0.006 per unit length for the 3 shapes, and the fitted profiles rise there by 0.3 to 3.3 points. Each shape carries weight from 5 to 7 substations of the fit (the five and the two others in the pool); no shape belongs to a group of substations.
  • The forecast under-reproduces the step on cold winter nights and invents one on mild nights. On cold nights (below 2 °C) in the replicate year (23 to 26 nights per substation) the actual step at 01:00 was 6.9, 9.0, 3.2, 1.2, and 6.9 points at D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16, against forecast steps of 2.6, 3.1, 1.5, 0.4, and 1.5. The scored year (4 to 13 cold nights per substation, so few) gives the same picture: 5.7, 11.3, 3.8, 1.6, and 7.1 against 2.6, 3.4, 1.5, 0.1, and 1.9. On mild nights (above 10 °C) the forecast step is 1.4 to 3.3 points at D5, D10, D11, and D16 against actual steps of −0.3 to 2.3. A visible miss on cold winter nights counts against release; the card for each substation shows the median cold night.
  • The step is UTC-fixed. On cold nights (below 6 °C) the largest rise ends at 01:00 UTC in British Summer Time and in Greenwich Mean Time at 9 of 10 substation-years (the exception, D14 in the replicate year, has the smallest step), with 16 to 27 British Summer Time nights each. A local-clock step would rise an hour earlier in UTC in summer.
  • The window and the weight by winter cannot be read. The profiles fall back at 06:00 and 11:00 local time and rise at 06:30 to 08:00, which does not show a seven-hour window ending near 07:30, and the shapes of different cuts do not match (matched cosine 0.48 between the tuning and replicate fits, 0.53 between the disjoint tuning and scored fits), so a weight on the shape with the largest rise at 00:30 by winter is "cannot tell".
  • The two-clock regression is uninformative. The three windows overlap by 5 of 7 hours, and the coefficients (local window 1.8 to 4.5 points, UTC window −1.1 to +1.1) do not agree with the onset readout, so the onset readout is the readout to trust. The learned shapes are indexed by local time only, so a UTC-indexed shape family and a heating-dependent shape (a winter and a summer version of each) are not tested here.

docs.title: Stability and shape mix
docs.text:
• Across seeds, the matched shapes agree at a median cosine of 0.59 (tuning cut), 0.56 (replicate), and 0.61 (scored), minimum cosine 0.19 to 0.24. The plan calls under 0.6 unstable; the null fleet of random profiles gives 0.78, so the real shapes are less stable than shapes fitted to profiles that share nothing.
  • Across years, the replicate and scored fits agree at 0.95 (their windows share a year), and the disjoint tuning and scored fits at 0.53.
  • Shape mix. Each of the five substations puts 7% to 53% of its weight on each shape, so none sits wholly on one shape, and the deviation holds 0.7% to 2.3% of the profile's energy. The range over the 5 seeds is wide (for example 0.24 to 0.88 for D10 on shape 1), so the shares are not identified. The plan's month-block intervals on the shares were not computed, because each needs a refit per resample; the range over seeds stands in, as a labelled departure.

docs.title: Known-answer gate
docs.text:
Twenty fleets per kind (the plan's cut order: 20 instead of 40, pass at 15 instead of 30, the same 75%). Each fleet has 5 synthetic substations on the real weather and pinned capacity of the tuning cut, a 3-shape library, and block-resampled noise from the per-site model's residuals before the cut.

  • Passed: no duplicate shapes (line 3: 20 of 20, largest pairwise |cosine| 0.0002 at the tuned penalty against 0.43 without it), local optima (line 7: 20 of 20), and the module tests (line 8).
  • Failed: shapes recovered at cosine 0.9 (line 1: 0 of 20; median of the worst shape 0.77), weights (line 2: 14 of 20, below 15), a deviation absent from every shape, tested with one evening bump at one substation (line 4: 0 of 20), K chosen (line 6: 0 of 20, the tie rule gave K = 2 every time), null fleet (line 5: 2 of 20), score power (line 9: 4 of 20; at an oracle gain of 0.084 SH minus N had a median of −0.026), and the Economy 7 step (line 10: 2 of 20; time and size were found in every fleet, but the placebo step, the difference between two fits that differ only in noise, had a median of 1.4 points against a limit of 25% of the 4-point step, which is 1.0). The dense weight prior (reported, not blocking) gave a median worst cosine of 0.33.
  • What the failure means. In the gate, with five substations, 3 shapes, and this noise, the shapes were recovered only up to a rotation that does not change the score, so every number on shapes and shares in this page is descriptive. No run here used more than five substations, so the cause is a hypothesis, not a finding.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast is 0.000 points at every substation and arm, because the spread is median-centred.
  • Mean-error contrasts point the same way as the quantile-score contrasts (C1 −0.003, C2 +0.033, C3 +0.001 in the scored year).
  • Reproduction of experiment 109: G and N scored 2.884 and 2.915 (scored year) and 3.166 and 3.163 (replicate), identical to the stored sets.
  • Audit triggers fired: trigger 1 (a gate line failed; the reproduction of experiment 109's G and N, the other part of trigger 1, passed) and trigger 6 (C1's interval is 0.007 wide, under the 0.022 floor, because SH and N are nearly the same model). Triggers 2 to 5 and 7 did not fire. No Opus audit has run; the merge is held pending the maintainer's decision.

docs.title: Predictions against outcome
docs.text:
• K from 3 or 4, within 0.023 of K = 2 and 6: held (every K from 2 to 6 within 0.003 of 3.554).
  • C1 −0.01 to −0.04, 3 or 4 of 5 sites better: missed on size (−0.001), 4 of 5 better. C2 −0.02 to +0.03: at the top of the range (+0.030). C3 −0.01 to −0.04: missed (+0.001).
  • Seeds stable at 0.9 or more, disjoint years 0.7 to 0.9, null under 0.6: all three missed (0.56 to 0.61, 0.53, 0.78).
  • Most substations 70% or more on one shape, deviation under 20%: the second held (under 3%), the first missed. SH-g0 has a pair of shapes above 0.7 and SH does not: missed (0.43 without the penalty).
  • q95 and q99 coverage within 3 points of N: held.

docs.title: Caveats and post hoc labels
docs.text:
• Post hoc. Gate line 10 was missing from the first printed report (a replacement that did not match), and the module tests failed there only because they ran from the wrong folder; both were fixed before reading any line as a decision, and the bars were not changed. Three readouts were fixed after a first look because of code faults: minutes of the day overflowed an 8-bit hour (the night clock and step tables), the night-rise table averaged different nights at each half-hour, and the step slot was first set one half-hour late. No bar or contrast changed.
  • Screening tier on one year per cut, with ERA5 and CAMS weather. The late vintage at the tuning cut and the single replica year behind the spread are known weak points.
  • A library fit with K above the pool size fails (K = 6 with 5 substations gave a singular weights step in one tuning seed and in some gate fleets); those fits are reported as failed.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
• Does a library find shared shapes when many substations share them? The options are the eight Primaries that report apparent power and the wider fleet, where a night step shared by a group of substations could show up as a shape, with the same gate; the choice is the maintainer's.
  • Does a heating-dependent night-step term close the cold-night miss? The hand-built arms of experiment 121 are the benchmark. Shape arms that depend on heating and on UTC time need a module change first.

docs.title: Substation cards
docs.text: Provisional: fitted to past weather on a screening run. One card per decision substation (D5, D10, D11, D14, D16) from the 2025-07-01 headline fit: the daily profile per day type (library and deviation drawn separately), the weights on the shapes, the heating response, the holiday effects, the weight on the step shape by winter ("cannot tell" where the shapes do not match), four example weeks fixed by calendar rule before any score was read (the first Monday on or after 15 July 2025, 15 October 2025, 15 January 2026, and 15 April 2026, with 80% and 90% bands for SH and the median of N), and the median cold winter night (a night from 23:00 to 07:00 local time, November to March, mean temperature below 2 °C, 4 to 17 nights per substation under this whole-night rule, which differs from the per-row rule of the step figure) against the forecast medians of SH, N, and G. The pinned capacity is the real-time vintage, not a measurement, and weights and shapes are identified only up to the rotation the data fix. The per-site model with recent-level assimilation (GAM-K) is outside this experiment, so G stands in as the per-site reference on the cold-night panel.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, MH: multi-hinge heating curve and night step
docs.text:
Adding night-time levels indexed on the UTC clock removes most of the 01:00 jump in demand that the current forecast misses on cold winter nights, and a five-hinge heating curve adds almost nothing. We asked two questions of GAM-K, the fitted model of primary substation demand (a primary substation is a substation of the electricity distribution network that supplies local feeders) that the differentiable-physics series of experiments uses. First, does letting its heating response bend at five temperatures instead of one lower the forecast error? Second, does a night-time step term, such as the load that Economy 7 meters and storage heaters switch on at about 01:00, lower the error on winter nights? (Economy 7 is a UK off-peak electricity tariff.) We fitted each change at five substations, forecast each one day ahead for the 12 months from July 2025, and scored it on the same rows as the unchanged model, which the page calls B0-K. We tested the fitting code on synthetic substations first. The five-hinge curve lowered the error by 0.016 points against B0-K, a tie. The UTC-indexed night term lowered the error on winter nights by 0.23 points, and the gain held in the previous winter (2024-25). The synthetic tests could not show that a step this small can be detected, so every night label stays not powered and the verdict is inconclusive.

The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, so lower is better. It is measured in points, which are percent of a substation's effective capacity and not MW, after the recent-error filter (a Kalman filter that corrects each forecast with the latest metered error) unless stated. All forecasts use observed ERA5 temperature and CAMS irradiance instead of weather forecasts, so each number is a ceiling for a live forecast. One point is 0.054 to 0.117 MW depending on the substation (effective capacity 5.72 MW at D5, 5.40 at D10, 10.78 at D11, 11.71 at D14, and 9.12 at D16).

Code Meaning B0, B0-K GAM-K with one 15.5 C heating hinge; the suffix K adds the recent-error filter MH B0 plus heating hinges at 10, 12, 14, 16, and 18 C (MH-5 replaces B0's; MH-sh shrinks them) NS-L, NS-U free levels for the 20 half-hours from 22:00 to 08:00 on the local or the UTC clock NS-H, NS-HW the cold hinge times one night window (NS-H) or times each night half-hour (NS-HW) NS-UT NS-U with a level that drifts month to month C1, N1 to N4 the pre-registered contrasts: C1 is MH-K minus B0-K; N1 to N4 are NS-L-K, NS-U-K, NS-H-K, and NS-HW-K minus B0-K on winter nights not powered the synthetic test could not show that the contrast would detect the effect it targets

docs.title: Take-home message and verdict
docs.text:
• Night terms lower the winter-night score by 0.233 points. NS-U-K (free night levels on the UTC clock) minus B0-K is −0.233 points on winter nights (99.375% interval −0.276 to −0.180, drawn from only 5 resampled init-time months, so lean on the site and winter consistency), better at 5 of 5 substations, with −0.153 (95% interval −0.183 to −0.121) in the replicate winter 2024-25. The forecast of the 01:00 step on cold winter nights rises from 15 to 45% of the observed step to within 0.2 to 3.1 points of it (figure 2, table below).
  • The five-hinge heating curve ties with the single hinge. MH-K minus B0-K is −0.0155 (97.5% interval −0.035 to +0.004), −0.022 in the replicate year, better at 5 of 5 substations in both years. The label is tie. The gain sits in cold snaps (−0.140 in the scored winter, −0.077 in the replicate winter) and not in winter evening peaks (+0.005).
  • The verdict is inconclusive. The MH label is tie. Every night label is not powered because all three synthetic detection gates failed: a 4-point step is detected in 14%, 14%, and 8% of draws (80% needed, figure 5). The estimates for NS-U-K and MH-K above are results on real data and are reported in full; the pre-registered rule does not let them earn a label.
  • Production status is candidate, not adopted. NS-U and NS-HW are the arms worth an ENS confirmation plan with monthly refits, after an independent audit by a reviewing agent (triggers 1, 2, 4, 5, and 7 below).

Figure 1 shows the heating contrasts near zero and the UTC-indexed night contrasts well below it. The evolving night step (NS-UT) is worse than the fixed one.

docs.title: The forecast reproduces the 01:00 step only with a night term
docs.text:
B0-K gets 15 to 45% of the observed step; NS-U-K and NS-HW-K get most of it. The table gives, over cold winter weekday nights (22:00 to 08:00, daily mean temperature below 8 C, 55 to 59 nights per substation in the scored winter, 64 to 65 in the replicate winter), the median observed step (half-hour starting 00:30 minus the half-hour starting 00:00) in points and MW, and each forecast's median step minus it, with a 95% interval from resampling nights. This readout includes rows inside the switching masks, which every score on the page excludes; excluding them moves the gaps by at most 0.5 points.

Substation Observed step, points (MW) B0-K minus observed NS-U-K minus observed NS-HW-K minus observed D5 7.0 (0.40) −4.3 (−4.8 to −3.4) −0.5 (−1.0 to +0.4) +0.3 (−0.5 to +1.0) D10 11.3 (0.61) −7.9 (−8.3 to −7.5) −3.1 (−3.4 to −2.7) −2.6 (−3.0 to −2.0) D11 3.6 (0.38) −2.0 (−2.3 to −1.7) −0.2 (−0.5 to +0.1) +0.2 (−0.1 to +0.5) D14 1.8 (0.22) −1.6 (−2.0 to −1.5) −0.3 (−0.6 to −0.1) −0.1 (−0.5 to +0.1) D16 7.9 (0.72) −6.0 (−6.6 to −5.2) −1.9 (−2.5 to −1.2) −1.4 (−2.0 to −0.8)

Figure 2 shows the observed jump after midnight and the forecasts that follow it. The largest remaining median miss of NS-U-K is 4.6 points high at 07:00 at D10 (the morning rise), 2.5 points high at 23:00 at D5, and 2.2 to 3.2 points low between 01:00 and 03:00 at D11, D14, and D16. B0-K's largest miss is 3.6 to 5.8 points low after the step at D10, D11, D14, and D16, and 4.6 points high at 23:00 at D5. The maintainer's rule is that a visible miss on cold winter nights counts against release even when the mean score is unchanged.

docs.title: The night gain sits on winter nights and costs nothing elsewhere
docs.text: Figure 3 shows the night arms' gain on winter nights and no loss on other rows. Per substation, NS-U-K minus B0-K on winter nights is −0.299 at D5, −0.359 at D10, −0.092 at D11, −0.222 at D14, and −0.216 at D16. Pooled, NS-U-K minus B0-K is −0.233 on winter nights, −0.101 in November to March, −0.019 in April to October, −0.025 on rows other than winter nights (99.375% interval −0.048 to −0.001, so the +0.02 upper bound holds), and +0.012 on 676 cold British Summer Time (BST) night rows. NS-HW-K is −0.137 on winter nights, −0.012 on other rows (upper bound +0.001), and −0.094 on cold BST nights. MH-K's gain is −0.140 in cold snaps (the coldest 10% of days of each winter, 16 days per substation and winter; the rule uses the 6-hour trailing mean of temperature, not the daily mean of ERA5, so the cold-day subsets shift slightly under the other definition) and +0.005 on winter evening peaks, +0.019 on cold BST nights. The step was found on scored-winter rows, so only the replicate winter 2024-25 (−0.153) is a clean test; the tuning winter 2023-24 is descriptive only.

docs.title: Pooled scores of every arm
docs.text: Scored year, all rows, pooled over the 5 decision substations (points): B0 2.884, B0-K 2.255, MH-K 2.240, MH-5-K 2.240, MH-sh-K 2.238, NS-L-K 2.255, NS-U-K 2.204, NS-H-K 2.255, NS-HW-K 2.227, NS-UT-K 2.339; experiment 114's T-all-K 2.216 and H-site-K 2.243; Part 4's WK 2.267, A2 2.275, lagless XGBoost with the filter 2.496, manual heuristic 3.488, climatology 4.068. On winter nights: B0-K 2.061, MH-K 2.045, NS-U-K 1.829, NS-HW-K 1.925. On the 66,849 rows that BG2's stored predictions share (no interval; the sets do not cover every row), NS-L-K (equal to B0-K) minus BG2 is −0.265 and NS-U-K minus BG2 is −0.317.

docs.title: Heating curve results
docs.text:
Contrast (scored year, after the filter) Estimate Interval Replicate Sites better C1: MH-K − B0-K (planned, 97.5%) −0.0155 −0.035 to +0.004 −0.022 5 of 5 MH-K with B0's filter − B0-K (control) −0.0157 −0.033 to +0.001 −0.023 5 of 5 MH-5-K − B0-K −0.0155 −0.032 to +0.002 −0.022 5 of 5 MH-sh-K (multiplier 1000) − B0-K −0.0168 −0.030 to −0.005 −0.020 5 of 5 MH − B0 (unfiltered) +0.0001 −0.037 to +0.039 −0.030 2 of 5 MH-K − H-site-K (experiment 114) −0.0035 −0.009 to +0.001 −0.001 4 of 5 MH-K − T-all-K (experiment 114) +0.0233 −0.001 to +0.051 +0.016 1 of 5

The label is tie. The interval includes zero, so the rule gives tie although the replicate year's interval lies below zero (−0.042 to −0.004). Leaving D10 out gives −0.0163 (−0.030 to −0.002), a small gain, so the label depends on one substation (trigger 4). The filter-fit control agrees with the label, and the unfiltered contrast is zero, so the gain exists only after the filter. MH-sh at its tuning-year multiplier of 1000 (interior of the grid up to 100000) is the same size. The pooled-curve coverage gate returned 66%, outside 70 to 90%, so no curve summary or per-substation curve is shown.

docs.title: Synthetic tests run before any scored fit
docs.text:
• Test 1 passed at all four cuts, and B0-K reproduces experiment 114's stored scored-year B0-K exactly (difference 0).
  • Gate 2 passed. On 100 synthetic substations, MH-K minus B0-K is −0.031 (80% interval −0.036 to −0.027) under a five-hinge truth, recovering 83% of the 0.037-point oracle gain, and +0.003 under a single-hinge truth (limit +0.01). The curve-coverage check returned 66%.
  • Gate 4 as written failed, as predicted: NS-L is collinear with B0's profile (added effective degrees of freedom 0.0), and the winter-night criterion cannot be met because winter local time equals UTC.
  • Gate 4' as first written failed (NS-U beat B0 on BST nights in 74% of draws against 80% needed; NS-HW beat B0 on winter nights with a cold step in 72% against 90%). It was redefined after seeing that failure.
  • Gate 4'' (redefined with a stated effect size and power target) failed. At 5% false positives (1 to 4% verified), a 4-point step (0.2 to 0.5 MW) is detected on the label's night rows by NS-U in 14%, NS-HW in 14%, and NS-H in 8% of draws; a 7-point step in 59%, 57%, and 10%. On the step's own half-hour: 58%, 65%, and 16% for 4 points. NS-U does not detect a local-clock step (5%). Because gate 4'' failed, N2, N3, N4, and the indexing contrast are not powered, and the plan fixes the verdict at inconclusive.

docs.title: Night terms in detail
docs.text:
The clock that indexes the night step is not identified. NS-U-K minus NS-L-K on BST nights is −0.029 (95% interval −0.069 to +0.013) in the scored year and −0.077 (−0.107 to −0.040) in the replicate year, better at 5 of 5 substations in both. The indexing label is indexing not identified because gate 4'' failed. Cold BST nights (daily mean below 8 C) number 5 to 7 per substation in the replicate year and 5 to 11 in the scored year, so the clock contrast is cannot tell per substation, except at D10 and D11 in the scored year (11 nights each). As descriptive evidence only, on BST weekday nights the observed step sits at 01:30 local (00:30 UTC) at D10, D16, and D5 (about 1 point), with no step at 00:30 local. The winter gain cannot separate the clocks, because in winter local time equals UTC. Trigger 2 below gives the likely source of the winter gain.

An evolving night step (NS-UT) is worse than a fixed one. NS-UT-K minus NS-U-K is +0.286 (95% interval +0.264 to +0.302) on winter nights, and NS-UT-K is 0.084 points worse than B0-K on all rows although NS-UT before the filter is 0.098 points better than B0. Its fitted winter level (points, MW in the stored file ns_ut_step_by_winter.json) falls from 5 to 1.4 points at D5 between winters 2021-22 and 2022-23 and rises to 4.7 in 2024-25. D14 is 4.4, 0.2, 2.9, and 0.1. These are descriptive: a fit at each cut sees only the 24 months before it, and winter 2025-26 is outside every fit.

NS-H, one cold-hinge window from 00:00 to 07:00 UTC, adds nothing (+0.0005). NS-HW, which lets the cold hinge differ by half-hour, gains −0.137. NS-L is a null control: its scores equal B0's to 1e-4 points. The filter-fit control for the night arms agrees: NS-U-K with B0's filter minus B0-K on winter nights is −0.224, against −0.233.

docs.title: Consistency checks
docs.text:
• The median forecast equals the mean forecast. The median minus the mean is 0.0000 points at every substation for B0-K, MH-K, NS-U-K, and NS-HW-K, so the quantile spread does not shift the median forecast.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each score contrast: C1 −0.031 (score −0.0155), N2 −0.465 (−0.233), N4 −0.280 (−0.137); the signs agree.
  • No arm moves a tail more than 1 point from nominal. After the filter the q95 coverage is 0.941 to 0.942 and the q99 coverage 0.983 for B0-K, MH-K, NS-U-K, and NS-HW-K.
  • Four audit triggers fired. (1) The positive controls failed: gates 4, 4', and 4'' and the pooled-curve coverage check (66% against 70 to 90%). (2) The plan predicted NS-U-K and NS-L-K within 0.01 on winter nights, and they differ by 0.233. The explanation, which is post hoc: B0's profile is one year-round level per local half-hour and day type, so it cannot hold a step that is large in winter and small in summer. NS-U can, so the winter gain may come from the difference between the GMT and BST seasons and not from the UTC clock. (4) Leaving D10 out changes C1 from tie to small gain. (5, applied by analogy) NS-UT-K scores worse than B0-K, which it nests (the explanation, the held last level meeting the filter, is untested); (7, by judgement, since no label is gain) the night term is meant to enter GAM-K. An independent audit by a reviewing agent is planned before the night result is used. No trigger fired for the others: test 1, gate 2(b), and B0-K's reproduction of experiment 114 passed, and C1's interval width (±0.019) sits inside the sister contrast's ±0.023.

docs.title: Predictions against outcome
docs.text: The heating predictions held and the night predictions held only in sign. C1 fell in the predicted range (−0.016 against −0.03 to +0.01) with the predicted label, MH-K against H-site-K and T-all-K and MH-5-K matched, and gate 2(b) matched. The sign of the night gain was predicted, but its size was not: at D10 it is −0.36 (predicted −0.10 to −0.30), and at D11 (−0.09) and D14 (−0.22) it is far above the predicted "under 0.03". NS-U-K and NS-L-K were predicted within 0.01 on winter nights and differ by 0.233. The tuning-year NS-U-K gain of 0.043 was not expected to carry over and became 0.233 on winter nights. Three other predictions failed: the unfiltered MH gain was not larger than the filtered one (+0.0001 against −0.0155), gate 2 recovered 83% of the oracle gain (predicted 50 to 70%), and the MH gain did not sit in November to March (−0.0155, against a predicted more than 0.02), although cold snaps carry −0.140.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Every number is a past-weather ceiling (ERA5 temperature and CAMS irradiance), one scored year with frozen fits, hindsight masks, and one replicate winter.
  • The night step was identified on scored-year rows (experiment 111's stored residuals), so the scored winter is not a clean test for the night arms. The replicate winter confirms the sign and roughly two thirds of the size.
  • The scored year has served experiments 106, 111, 114, and this one, and MH was chosen after seeing experiment 114's scored-year contrasts.
  • Leaks, none reaching a scored row: the 2022-07-01 replica reads the 2023-08-07 capacity vintage 13 months late; the 2023-07-01 cut has the 5-week vintage leak; D9's 2024-07-01 fit reads the 2025-04-14 vintage; the replicate-year filter spread is in sample for the filter hyperparameters.
  • Gate 4'' replaces gate 4' as first written, which is kept above. The redefinition came after the first failure and before any scored fit.
  • Provisional substation cards (fitted to past weather on a screening run) are in the same folder as card_D5.svg, card_D10.svg, card_D11.svg, card_D14.svg, and card_D16.svg. D9 is short-history and has no card.
  • The experiment 114 merge commit (503ce3a3de408d1f0c2bdbada5ba88032ff238bb) is recorded in the hashed decisions.json.

docs.title: Citations
docs.text: The convex-model-plus-filter design follows Fasiolo et al. (2021), who fit additive models with quantile output, and Obst et al. (2021), who forecast with an adaptive component on top of a fitted model. Experiments 104, 106, 111, and 114 supply the base model and its filter.
