The injection harness adds steps, stuck-meter runs, and scale errors to a single substation's residual stream, not experiment 43's multi-series transfers. The edge-flow comparison was not run.
  • Gate 3 for W-basis kept the basis learned from real data, and its oracle gain overshot (0.053 points), so its "not powered" label is partly a fault of the gate.
  • S-ewma could not reach the target oracle gain at 3 of 5 substations (its columns nearly repeat T-all's smoothings), so its gate rests on 2 of 5.
  • Schedule: frozen yearly fits (monthly-refit shortcuts not used), one seed.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• E-sol on ENS weather and the earlier winters, with a row set that makes the interval narrower than 0.03 points.
  • G-skf as a load-transfer detector with its multipliers re-tuned on injected events.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, KFD: a shared day-level error state and a sparse process noise in GAM-K's filter
docs.text:
This experiment asked whether one extra number per day, shared by every time of day, lets the correction to a Primary substation's day-ahead demand forecast follow recent errors more closely. It stopped before any forecast was scored. The forecast comes from a convex model (a physical demand model fitted by least squares) driven by weather forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). A Kalman filter (a method that updates an estimate of the current forecast error each time a new reading arrives) corrects each forecast. For each of four hour bands (night, morning, midday, and evening) the filter keeps a slowly moving level and a fast anomaly. Errors and scores are in points, where one point is 1% of a substation's effective capacity. The substations D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16 are anonymised Primary substations.

We added a day-level error that all four hour bands share, and changed how the filter decides which levels may drift. The new filter is called KDS. The filter it extends is GAM-K, experiment 111's level-and-anomaly filter, called GK in the tables. KD is GK plus the shared day state only, and KS is GK with the sparse level noise only. Before scoring any forecast, we injected a known change, shaped like a rise in solar-panel capacity, into copies of the real recorded errors of the five substations. Each copy is one draw. We then checked how often each filter's midday level recovered the injected change. S1 is the size of change that experiment 118 injected, and S1x3 is three times that size. The plan said to stop if KDS tracked worse than GK when the errors follow the filter's own AR(1) error model (each reading is the previous reading's error times a constant, plus fresh noise). KDS did, so the experiment stopped.

KDS did not recover the injected change reliably, and its day state failed a control that shifts the hour bands apart. At S1x3, KDS's midday level recovered the change in 35% of the 60 draws of real errors. The plan set the bar at 0.8 times KDS's own rate on AR(1) draws (60%), which is 48%. GK recovered it in 22% of the real draws, and in 80% of the 30 AR(1) draws against KDS's 60%. The verdict is inconclusive, because the plan's decision rule needs a scored contrast to say supported or not supported, and none exists. The errors in different hour bands do move together, but a single shared state probably also absorbs errors that belong to one band. At S1, four of the five substations could not show the change clearly in the first place.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Reading 1 compares each arm's rate on real residuals (orange) with its rate on AR(1) draws (blue). At S1x3, KDS reaches 0.35 against a bar of 0.48.

Reading 2 asks whether the night level and the day state stay below a quarter of the injected change's peak. KD passes in 27% of real draws and KDS in 28% at S1 and 57% at S1x3.

On the first draw at D5 (S1x3), every arm's level stays about 6 points short of the injected change at its peak.

The shifted fits stay at 0.45 to 0.76 points against a required level below 0.1.

D11 keeps no free level at 1, 2, or 4 nats (a nat is the unit of a log-likelihood gain).

docs.title: Arms that ran at the gate
docs.text:
Arm Filter state Level noise Role GK level and AR(1) anomaly per hour band one shared variance (experiment 111's) benchmark KD GK plus one day-level state d shared by all four bands one shared variance, refitted day state alone KS GK one variance per band, sparse from zero sparse noise alone KDS GK plus d one variance per band, sparse from zero hypothesis arm

The hour bands are local time: 00:00 to 05:59, 06:00 to 10:59, 11:00 to 15:59, and 16:00 to 23:59. The state d is constant within a local day and follows an AR(1) across days, with its persistence bounded at 0.90 per day. The sparse search sets each band's level variance to exactly zero unless a likelihood gain of 2 nats justifies it. KD, KS, and KDS use the one-step likelihood, as GAM-K does, so that they differ from GK in the state and the noise search only. Four exploratory variants (KDS-1n, KDS-4n, KDS-floor, and KDS-da) were fitted and not run through the gate or scored.

The filter and the search for its noise re-implement published methods. de Vilmarest et al. (2024) put a random walk on the weights of a frozen additive regression model of regional electricity load and fitted a sparse, diagonal noise matrix by likelihood. de Vilmarest and Goude (2022) describe the greedy search that starts every noise variance at zero, and the R package viking implements it. We did not find the shared day-level state in either paper. The code builds on experiment 111, which supplies the monthly convex fits, calibration, and filter settings, and on experiment 118, which supplies the periods, rows, and known-answer gate.

docs.title: The known-answer gate on real residuals
docs.text:
The gate injects a change shaped like a rise in solar-panel capacity into streams of residuals and asks whether each arm's midday level follows it. Experiment 118's change raises the solar-panel weight from 1 to 1.30 over 180 days, so the stream gains a negative deviation that grows with the solar regressor. Each arm is refitted on every stream, GK included. The noise is either a circular month-block resample of the substation's real residuals (12 resamples per substation, 60 draws, the decision form) or the filter's own AR(1) error model (6 per substation, 30 draws). Each injected stream is paired with a stream on identical noise and no injection, and an arm's reading is the difference between the two. Four readings are scored:

  • Reading 1, tracking: the midday level recovers at least 70% of the injected change at its peak and correlates with it at 0.70 or more.
  • Reading 2, no cross-talk: neither the night level nor the day state d moves by a quarter or more of the injected change's peak after day 60.
  • Reading 3, steadiness: on streams with no injection, the median largest movement of the midday level is at most 1.25 times GK's.
  • Reading 4, error follows: the arm's day-ahead error on the stream is below GK's.

Power check. At S1 the injected change peaks at 1.0 (D10), 1.7 (D16), 1.8 (D14), 2.1 (D11), and 3.4 (D5) posterior standard deviations of the midday level, a median of 1.8. The plan requires 3, so S1 was underpowered at four of five substations and the decision amplitude became S1x3.

Readings at S1x3 (share of draws passing; 60 real-residual draws, 30 AR(1) draws):

Arm 1 tracking, real 1 tracking, AR(1) 2 no cross-talk, real 2 no cross-talk, AR(1) 4 error follows, real 4 error follows, AR(1) GK 0.22 0.80 0.70 1.00 (reference) (reference) KD 0.07 0.80 0.27 0.97 1.00 1.00 KS 0.28 0.57 0.68 1.00 0.15 1.00 KDS 0.35 0.60 0.57 1.00 1.00 1.00
  • Reading 1 failed the relative bar. KDS's real rate of 0.35 is below 0.8 times its AR(1) rate of 0.60, which is 0.48. KDS minus GK in the real tracking rate is +0.13 (95% interval -0.44 to +0.56), below the required +0.10 with an interval excluding zero.
  • Reading 2 failed the relative bar. KDS's real rate of 0.57 is below 0.8 times its AR(1) rate of 1.00, which is 0.80. KD fails it worst (0.27). The stored rates do not separate the night level from d, so the night level or the day state moved by more than a quarter of the peak.
  • Readings 3 and 4 passed. KD and KDS lowered the stream's day-ahead error below GK's in all 60 real draws. On streams with no injection, the median largest movement of the midday level after day 60, in units of the injected peak, was 0.35 for KDS against 0.78 for GK on real residuals (ratio 0.45, bar 1.25), and 0.024 against 0.085 under AR(1) noise.
  • The stop rule fired. KDS minus GK under AR(1) noise is -0.20 (95% interval -0.44 to 0.00), past the -0.10 limit.
  • Among the four arms, sparse noise alone (KS) tracked best at S1 (0.63 of real draws against GK's 0.28) but not at S1x3 (0.28), and its forecast error followed in only 17% and 15% of real draws at S1 and S1x3. KS is not part of the gate rule.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Control Result P1, nesting: KD with sigma_d 0 and KS with equal q reproduce GAM-K pass (state differences about 1e-12 to 4e-10 and log-likelihood differences up to 1.2e-9; stored quantiles equal exactly on 13,440 rows per substation) P2, causality: later readings change no state pass P-day: local-day bookkeeping across both clock changes pass P-ident: recovery of a known sigma_d of 1.5 in 150 simulated draws pass (98.7% within a factor of 2; median fit 1.57) P-ident, step test: a permanent step of 3 points for KD, 85% of the step went to the level and 9% to d; for KDS with all q_b zero, 60% went to d P-sparse: AR(1) streams with a true zero or a true 0.05 pass (a band kept at 2 nats in 7% of true-zero draws, and in 100% of true-0.05 draws) P-premise: correlation between the daily means of different hour bands' innovations 0.18 to 0.23, mean 0.20 (predicted 0.25 or more; above the stop limit of 0.10) P-premise: lag-1 autocorrelation of the mean of those four daily means 0.25 to 0.37, mean 0.32 (bar 0.3) P-shift: KD refitted with each band shifted by its own random number of days fail at five of five substations (below)

P-shift failed at all five decision substations. The median shifted-band sigma_d was 0.49 (D10), 0.60 (D11), 0.45 (D14), 0.76 (D16), and 0.54 (D5) points, against 3.45, 2.40, 1.78, 1.99, and 2.05 on the real stream. The criterion was below 0.1 at four or more of five substations, and no shifted fit reached it. The shift keeps each band's own day-to-day behaviour, so the shared state also absorbs single-band structure. The plan makes an audit the consequence of this failure, and no audit has been run.

The 2-nat rule left D11 with every level frozen. At D11, all four q_b are 0 under KDS, KDS-1n, and KDS-4n, so the sparse rule did not support the day anomaly there. A frozen level lets d take any permanent shift, which is the plan's second stop rule. KDS-floor (each q_b at least 1e-4 points squared per day) sits at that floor at D11, so its levels can move only barely. D10 keeps bands 0 and 3 only at 2 nats.

docs.title: Decision rule and stop rules
docs.text: The verdict is inconclusive. The plan's rule reads: "inconclusive: every other result, and any result that would be supported or small gain but has a failed gate [...] A failed P-shift [...] also gives inconclusive and triggers an audit." Both are met here. not supported and refuted need the interval of C1 (KDS minus GK at day D+1), which was never computed. Two stop rules fired: "If KDS tracks worse than GK by more than 0.10 in the AR(1) form [...] Stop and report before any scored forecast", and the rule to stop if all four q_b are zero at any decision substation, which happened at D11.

docs.title: Predictions and what happened
docs.text: Quantity Prediction Result Gate tracking, real form, S1x3 KDS 50% (30% to 70%); GK 40% (20% to 60%); KDS minus GK +0.10 (0.00 to +0.25) KDS 35%; GK 22%; +0.13 (-0.44 to +0.56) Gate tracking, AR(1) form KDS within 0.10 of GK, both at least 70% KDS 60%, GK 80%; -0.20 Gate, steadiness KDS at most 1.25 times GK's 0.45 times Cross-band control (P-shift) passes at four or more of five substations fails at five of five Premise (P-premise) correlation at least 0.25; lag-1 at least 0.3 0.20 mean; 0.32 mean Fitted d sigma_d above its floor at five of five; phi_d 0.4 to 0.8 sigma_d 1.78 to 3.47 at five of five; phi_d 0.62 to 0.90 (0.90 at D10, the bound) Sparse support at 2 nats at least 3 of 4 bands nonzero at four or more of five 3 bands at D5, 2 at D10, 0 at D11, 2 at D14, 2 at D16: one of five meets it

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Triggers that fired. Trigger 1 (a control failed): the known-answer gate and P-shift. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction): P-shift was predicted to pass and the gate's real rates fell short of the predicted ranges. The explanation, that d absorbs single-band structure, rests on P-shift alone and was not tested separately. Trigger 5 (a nested arm beats the arm that contains it): GK tracked in 22% of real S1x3 draws and KD, which contains GK, in 7%; KS tracked in 63% at S1 and KDS, which contains KS, in 23%. No audit has been run for these triggers.
  • Triggers 3, 4, 6, and 7 did not fire. Triggers 3 and 4 compare scored contrasts and so could not fire. Trigger 6 compares a headline interval with a sister experiment's, and none exists. Trigger 7 needs a later experiment whose design depends on this result, and none does yet.
  • The mean-forecast checks were not run, because nothing was scored. The median-forecast minus mean-forecast difference per substation, and the mean-forecast error beside each quantile-score contrast, need forecasts.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Caveats:
    • The P-shift failure is unresolved and no audit has run.
    • The gate had low power at S1 and a wide interval at S1x3: the paired interval on the tracking difference spans -0.44 to +0.56 with 60 draws over five substations, which share real streams.
    • The 2-nat threshold is calibrated only under the filter's own error model.
    • The gate reads the midday level alone, so a change that the arm carried in the day state instead counts as a failure of reading 1.
    • The injected change is shaped like the solar-panel term, and a different slow change might behave differently.
    • The hyperparameter likelihood counts the odd months only, while the warm state also saw the even months' readings, as in experiment 111.
  • What to try next, stated as options and not commitments:
    • A day-level state for each hour band plus a smaller shared part, so that single-band structure does not have to land in one shared state.
    • An explicit solar-panel term, so that the midday level need not carry a slow solar change (experiment 118 suggested fixing the weight on the panels and moving the others).
    • A known-answer gate with an injected change large enough to detect at every decision substation, for example S1x3 from the start, with the S1 results reported beside it.
    • Judging the day state by a forecast score at D+1, with the gate as a diagnostic only.

docs.title: Pre-registered but not run
docs.text: The plan pre-registered these, and none ran: the contrasts C1 to C5 (KDS, KD, and KS against GK and each other) at day D+1 over the scored year and the replicate months, with 99% month-block intervals; the exploratory arms KDS-shuf, KDS-nod, KDS-1n, KDS-4n, KDS-floor, and KDS-da as scored arms; the breakouts (winter, winter nights, winter evening peaks, cold-snap days, cold winter nights, and the holiday days); the tail coverage and pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, and q99; KDS-dow (a shrunken same-weekday correction on KDS) and its last-week reference; and the substation cards.

docs.title: Earlier advice
docs.text:
The experiment followed experiment 111's choice of the level-and-anomaly filter as the benchmark, the 3.5-hour telemetry delay on residuals, experiment 115's advice to test a new filter state with an injected change before scoring it, and experiment 118's advice to test on resampled real residuals. It departed from experiment 118's advice to fit a filter's noise by a day-ahead likelihood with a wide bound on log q, so that the arms differ in the state and the noise search only. Quantile scores follow experiment 87's 11 quantiles.

Every number on this page is printed by e00128_gate.py report and e00128_charts_gate.py numbers, and e00128_charts_gate.py figures draws the figures.

docs.title: Differentiable physics: can the embedded solar capacity behind a Primary be inferred, with an honest range?
docs.text:
Take-home message: the capacity of the unmetered solar behind five Primary substations can be read from their power, but the range around each estimate is a spread over test scenarios and not yet a calibrated 80% interval. The arm 2 estimate of AC capacity in 2025/26 is 3.3 to 4.5 MW across the five Primary substations, which is 0.4 to 2.8 MW above the 2021/22 estimate (figure 1). The range is 1.2 to 1.6 MW wide. Arm 2 and arm 4 passed every pre-registered gate, so the pre-registered rule gives supported. The verdict is partly supported because the coverage test is close to circular and the known-answer recovery was measured on farms and not on embedded panels (see "Limitations"). That downgrade is a judgement beyond the rule. No forecast gain is scored.

Terms used below. D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16 are the five decision Primary substations of experiment 103's data set. A season-year runs from July to June and is labelled by the year of the July, so 2025/26 is the label 2025. The plan below says September to August, which is not what the convex model uses. The four arms are the experiment 45 frozen capacity (arm 1, a control and not a truth), arm 2 (a capacity that steps up each season-year), arm 3 (arm 2 plus demand terms that cannot see the sun), and arm 4 (arm 2 with a penalty on the steps). Recovery is the capacity found with a known solar farm's output added to a Primary's power, minus the capacity found without it, divided by the added capacity. The divisor is the median recovery of the other real farms at the same Primary, which rescales a recovery to 1; the published estimates are already divided by it. A coverage cell is one Primary, one plant class, and one load, with the known capacity checked against the range. CAMS is the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service's satellite irradiance, ERA5 is the European Centre's reanalysis of past weather, and DESNZ is the UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero.

The fits stop at 2026-07-31 and add one month to the original cut. The maintainer approved fitting to 2026-08-31 as an exception to the hold-out, on the understanding that season-year 2025/26 would then be complete. Season-years run from July to June, so 2025/26 was already complete at 2026-06-30. The final ERA5 for August 2026 is not out, so the exception added July 2026 only, and the model fits July 2026 at the 2025/26 level because it has no 2026/27 increment. The code constants that mark where the hold-out begins, and the grid end, are moved inside this experiment's scripts only (E00129_THROUGH_JULY=1), and packages/ is unchanged.

Capacity rose at all five Primaries, and experiment 45's pinned value sits above the range at D16 in every year. The estimates at D10 and D11 step up in 2022/23, and the cause of the step was not tested. The figure starts in 2021/22. Season-year 2020/21 has no training rows at any Primary because of the lockdown exclusion, and 2019/20 has none at D14 and D16 and only winter rows at D5, D10, and D11, so the fit copies or barely identifies a capacity there and the page does not show it.

docs.title: Gates
docs.text:
Arm 2 and arm 4 passed all four gates; arm 3 failed the placebo gate. Arms 2, 3, and 4 were tested against the gates fixed before stage C. Arm 3 is descriptive and cannot win. Arm 4 uses an increment penalty of 0.1, and the plan ran arm 4 only if arm 2 failed the drift gate, which it did not in the final run. Coverage is 23 of 30 cells for arm 2 (77%), against a nominal 80%, so the range reaches the 21-cell gate but not its nominal level.

Gate Limit Arm 2 Arm 3 Arm 4 Recovery of both mismatched plants within 0.75 to 1.25 after the divisor 4 of 5 Primaries 5 5 5 Semi-synthetic coverage cells with the truth in the range 21 of 30 23 22 23 Placebo difference of fits, share of the real-sky recovery (median, max) at most 0.20 0.12, 0.13 0.21, 0.22 0.12, 0.12 Drift per 5 years, pooled mean (max Primary), data years only under 0.05 0.041 (0.047) 0.039 (0.047) 0.034 (0.038)

A first run of the drift gate counted season-years with no training rows and failed arm 2 (0.095). The Opus science review found that the convex model copies the capacity of a season-year with no rows from its neighbour. The gate was re-run on season-years with at least 12,000 training half-hours (a full season-year has 17,520), which are 2021/22 to 2025/26. The first run is kept in work/before_data_year_filter/. The recovery gate does not discriminate: divided recoveries are about 0.9 for the east-west plant and 1.1 for the south-west plant, so every arm passes at 5 of 5 Primaries, and the pre-registered prediction of 3 of 5 was wrong.

Real farms' output was recovered at about 0.8 before the divisor, at 20, 50, and 100% of the pinned capacity alike. A synthetic load that rises on overcast days, of 0.1 of the injected capacity, adds about 0.2 to the recovery at every Primary. The 0.2 is twice the assumed load, so it measures the model's sensitivity and not a bias found in real data. When that load is present, the true capacity lies inside the range for the south-west plant in only 1 of 5 cells and for real farms in 3 of 5.

Arm 4 follows a sudden rise in capacity more slowly than arm 2 does. Half of experiment 45's pinned capacity was injected as a step-up on 1 March 2024, in 2023/24. At the median Primary, arm 2 recovers -0.07 and -0.06 in the two years before (no leakage) and 0.84 and 0.87 in the two years after. Arm 4 at penalty 0.1 recovers -0.04 and 0.04 in the two years before and 0.77 and 0.85 after, and at penalty 1.0 recovers 0.19 and 0.26 before and 0.57 and 0.64 after.

docs.title: Primary power beside the estimated solar power
docs.text: The estimated solar power is not visible as a one-for-one dip in the metered power. Figure 4 shows the metered power of D5, D10, and D14 on a cloudy, a median, and a sunny day in May to July 2026. At each Primary the days are the lowest, the median, and the highest mean CAMS irradiance between 06:00 and 18:00 UTC among days with a full day of readings outside the switching events, chosen before any plot was drawn: D5 on 4 May, 15 June, and 2 July; D10 on 3 May, 1 July, and 2 July; D14 on 4 May, 1 July, and 2 July. On the sunny days the metered power falls during daylight by about 1.6 to 2.3 MW between the 06:00 UTC level and the noon level (D5 about 1.6, D10 about 1.7, D14 about 2.3), against estimated solar peaks of 3.9, 3.3, and 4.5 MW. Two explanations fit: the demand that the solar hides is not constant through the day, or the estimate is too high (see "Limitations"). The flat tops of the estimated solar power are the inverter limit in the solar shape. The estimated solar power is arm 2's capacity times that shape before temperature derating.

docs.title: Every range reaches the register totals
docs.text:
• The Feed-in Tariff (FiT) register lies below every range. The register, shared to each Primary by postcode district, lists 1.9 to 2.6 MW of declared net capacity at sites of at most 1 MW (2.0 to 2.8 MW of DC capacity) and 2.1 to 3.2 MW at sites of at most 5 MW (2.2 to 3.5 MW of DC capacity). The ranges reach these totals at all five Primaries. The register's "declared net capacity" is its name for AC capacity. A lower-bound check cannot detect an overestimate.
  • DESNZ's domestic solar by constituency, shared by area, gives 2.1 to 3.8 MW. Its capacity basis (DC or AC) is not stated.
  • Holding the 1 July 2025 estimate forward undershoots the hindsight 2025/26 estimate by 0.00 to 0.70 MW for arm 2. The as-of fit at that origin sees season-years to 2024/25, and the held value is its 2024/25 capacity. The largest gaps are at D16 (0.70) and D10 (0.30), where capacity is still growing. The as-of divisors come from known-answer fits that use data to 2026-07-01, which is future information, with a small effect because recovery varies only from 0.78 to 0.86 across the Primaries.
  • CAMS' own beam and diffuse irradiance changes the latest arm 2 estimate by 0.04 MW or less. The beam and diffuse columns were already in the downloaded files, so no new download was needed. Recovery falls by 0.02 and the divided estimate rises by at most 0.04 MW, partly because the divisor moves with the raw estimate.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The range is a spread over test scenarios. A bootstrap over resampled months spreads the 2025/26 capacity by only 3 to 7% of the estimate (reviewer's check). The rest of the width comes from dividing by 240 recovery ratios (10th to 90th percentile 0.73 to 1.08) measured on three plant shapes, with and without the overcast-day load, at the other four Primaries. A coverage cell is covered when its own recovery lies inside that pool, so 23 of 30 is close to guaranteed, and the cells that fail are the extreme scenarios. The test does not say how often the range holds on real panels.
  • The point estimate sits near the top of its range. The point divides by the Primary's own median real-farm recovery (0.78 to 0.86), and the range divides by the pooled ratios (median about 0.92).
  • The divisor may overstate embedded capacity by roughly 5 to 10%. A farm's recovery rises with the correlation of its irradiance with the Primary's (r = 0.79 over 25 farm and Primary pairs, reviewer's check). Embedded panels sit at the Primary's irradiance point, so their recovery is probably above the farms'. The unit is also the 99th-percentile output of a farm-like plant, not nameplate AC capacity. A synthetic plant driven by the Primary's own CAMS would test both.
  • The semi-synthetic target flatters every arm. It uses arm 3's demand terms, which the fit can represent exactly, and shuffles residuals across years by month, which removes demand trends and weather-correlated residuals. Coverage, drift, and the placebo were measured with no demand misspecification. Coverage was tested only for 2024/25 at 100% injection.
  • Growth is not separated from demand trends. The convex model has no drift term here, so a multi-year fall in daytime demand would load onto the capacity steps. The D10 and D11 steps in 2022/23 are unexplained. The sign of the growth survives resampling, which covers sampling error only.
  • The arm 4 penalty was not tuned. The plan tuned it on D9 from semi-synthetic drift, but D9's drift is undefined (under 3 estimable years) and every penalty from 0.001 to 1.0 gave a recovery of about 0.75. The middle value 0.1 was fixed, and arm 4 was not needed under the plan's rule.
  • The placebo limit of 0.20 is a post-pilot choice, set after seeing arm 2 at 0.10 of the injection in the pilot. It changes no verdict among arms 2 and 4.
  • The fits use mixed cuts. The known-answer, coverage, semi-synthetic, and step fits stop at 2026-07-01, and the real, as-of, and beam fits stop at 2026-08-01. The four gates rest on the first group, so they do not use the July 2026 rows. July 2026 may contain unmasked switching, because the switching labels may not cover April to July 2026.
  • Four planned comparisons were not run. They are the December-factor comparison, experiment 45's semi-synthetic constant-path re-run, and the Embedded Capacity Register and the Renewable Energy Planning Database comparisons, because experiment 45's processed files do not hold the last two.
  • The monotone-arm and sun-blind-arm fits are copied from experiment 110 and are not yet in packages/studies. Moving them there needs a separate module PR.

docs.title: What a later experiment must not take for granted
docs.text:
• That the range is a calibrated 80% interval, or that the estimate is nameplate AC capacity.
  • Any capacity for 2019/20 or 2020/21, and any year-to-year change beyond what the step test shows arm 2 can follow.
  • That hindsight capacities can be used in a forecast test. A net-demand forecast test must use an as-of fit at each forecast origin and must never use capacities fitted through July 2026 when scoring rows on or after 2026-07-01.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The next experiment should test whether explicit solar modelling lowers the net-demand forecast error on the sunniest half-hours without raising it on dark ones. Refitting each March instead of each September, or each quarter, is a further question.

docs.title: Plan (written before any fit)
docs.text:
This section is the plan as written before any fit and is kept unedited, except for two facts the finished work overturned. The convex model's season-years run from July to June, not September to August. The stage B drift figures below were measured before the data-year filter described under "Gates", so they include season-years with no training rows.

The full plan, with the Opus review's triage, is data/ml-experiments/briefs/dp_pv_design_note.md (private). Its content is repeated here in short.

  • Deliverable: a capacity-over-time estimate with an 80% range per Primary, for a substation card and for NGED. A forecast gain is not scored here. A follow-on experiment tests whether explicit solar modelling lowers the net-demand forecast error on the sunniest half-hours, without raising it on dark ones.
  • Inputs: CAMS global irradiance at the Primary (beam and diffuse, found already in the downloaded files, for one sensitivity row), ERA5 2 m temperature, cleaned Primary net power with metered generators already subtracted, the hand-labelled switching events of experiment 103 (66 events, plus and minus 24 hours), and five metered solar farms as the injection source.
  • Model: experiment 110's convex model, with a fixed south-facing tilt-35 shape (orientation is not identified at a Primary, experiment 73) and one capacity per season-year, each year the previous year plus a non-negative increment. Fits run on the GPU where possible.
  • Arms: (1) the experiment 45 frozen vintage as control; (2) monotone season-year capacity; (3) arm 2 with sun-blind demand; (4) arm 2 or 3 with a penalty on the increments, run only if arm 2's measured drift exceeds 0.05 per 5 years.
  • Known-answer test: farm output at 20, 50 and 100% of the Primary's pinned capacity, as a matched plant and two mismatched synthetic plants (east-west, tilt 15, DC:AC 1.3, clipped; south-west, tilt 25), each with and without a day-long cloud-driven load of 10% of capacity, plus a step-up injection. Recovery is the difference of two fits divided by the injected capacity; it measures bias only, because the fit is nearly linear in its target. Coverage, drift and the placebo run on a semi-synthetic target with a known capacity.
  • Stages, each ending in a one-line report: A, a beam and diffuse fetch at the five points (not needed: the columns were already downloaded); B, pilot on two Primaries; C, full grid; D, real-data tables; E, register comparison and write-up.

docs.title: Register comparison
docs.text: The write-up compares the hindsight capacity per Primary with the Embedded Capacity Register, Renewable Energy Planning Database and Feed-in Tariff figures that experiment 45 processed. The registers are lower bounds, so the check is that our range lies above the register total of sites below 1 MW (sensitivity at 5 MW).

docs.title: Stage B findings and rules fixed before stage C
docs.text:
Stage B ran on D10 and D16, on the feature cache that stops at 2026-06-30. The numbers are the pilot's and are not results.

  • Fits cost about 0.5 s, and the GPU and CPU give identical capacities, so the whole experiment takes minutes.
  • The ridge does not matter. Ridge 0.01, 0.1 and 1.0 move the recovery by 0.01 or less, so the ridge pilot is dropped and 0.1 (experiment 104's value) is kept.
  • A real farm's output is recovered at 0.73 to 0.88 without load, as experiments 39 and 63 found. A day-long cloud-driven load of 10% of capacity adds about 0.21 to arm 2's recovery and 0.20 to arm 3's.
  • Arm 3 recovers 0.02 to 0.03 more than arm 2 and does not cut the cloud-load bias. Its placebo difference of fits (0.17 to 0.18 of the injection) is larger than arm 2's (0.10).
  • On the semi-synthetic target (true capacity zero), the capacity found from noise is 1 to 4% of the injected capacity. The recovery's drift on a constant farm is +0.18 per 5 years at D10 (standard deviation 0.16 over 10 draws and 5 farms) and +0.045 at D16, against a limit of 0.05.

Rules for stage C, written before it runs.

  • Arm 3 is descriptive. It cannot win the verdict if it only matches arm 2. Its purpose is the stated claim that sun-blind demand does or does not cut the cloud-load bias, at five Primaries.
  • Arm 4 runs, because arm 2's drift exceeds 0.05 per 5 years at D10. Its increment penalty is tuned on D9, which is not a decision Primary, from the semi-synthetic drift alone.
  • Post-pilot choice: the placebo gate is "placebo difference of fits at most 20% of the real-sky recovery of the same arm and Primary". The 20% is a round number chosen after seeing arm 2 at 0.10 of the injection, so the gate is not independent of the pilot.
  • Grid: the five decision Primaries; 20, 50 and 100% of the pinned capacity; the five real farms, the east-west plant, and the south-west plant; with and without the cloud-driven load.
  • Divisor: recovery is divided by the median recovery of the other four farms (matched plants, no load, 100%) at the same Primary and arm; the two synthetic plants use the median of all five.
  • Coverage cells: 30 cells, one per Primary, plant class (matched with a rotating farm, east-west, south-west), and load, each at 100%. The interval is the stratified month-block bootstrap of the last complete season-year, divided by recovery ratios from the other Primaries and other farms.

docs.title: Experiment 130: does a better demand forecast help the detector find load transfers?
docs.text:
A better demand forecast lifts the share of moved power that the detector finds only a little, and the Kalman filter's one-step errors make the detector much worse. A load transfer is a switching operation that moves part of one Primary substation's demand onto neighbouring Primary substations for hours or days. We added synthetic transfers to real power history, and counted the share of the moved megawatts (MW) that the detector raised an alarm on. Built on the convex demand model's forecast (arm B), the detector found 0.794 of the moved MW, against 0.772 when built on the lagless XGBoost model's forecast (arm A). The difference of +0.023 (95% interval -0.001 to +0.046) is under the +0.03 that the plan set as the bar for a worthwhile gain, and its interval includes zero, so the verdict is inconclusive. On the 35 real transfers lasting over 1 day, arm B found 18 and arm A found 12, a count that flatters arm B because the convex demand model trained with those real transfers masked. Most of the remaining misses are small steps with no metered receiving substation, so a stronger signal for those transfers is the next idea to try, more than a better forecast.

The detector is experiment 82's refit-offset neighbour-count detector (RO-NC). It subtracts a forecast from a Primary substation's measured power, and raises an alarm when the 24-hour average of the difference steps by 4.0 noise units or more. One noise unit is the usual size of that step in odd-numbered months. We added synthetic transfers to the real power history of 15 Primaries, and swapped the forecast for the convex demand model of experiment 122, with and without the Kalman filter that experiment added (together called GAM-K). A Kalman filter, as in Kalman (1960), tracks a slowly moving level in the recent errors of a forecast, and its one-step error is the next reading minus the level it predicted.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. A: lagless XGBoost residual (experiment 82). B (the headline): residual of the convex model, frozen between fits, with the model fitted on the 1st and on the 16th of each month for the refit offset. C: one-step innovations of the Kalman filter on that residual, filter re-run on each injected power series. D: arm B with one model and no refit offset. Every arm is RO-NC with its own noise unit, its own logistic score, and 80 unexplained odd-month alarms.
  • Row set. The 602 fresh headline-band transfers per injection shape that start in even months and do not start at the excluded series (shapes S2, S3, and S4 pooled), and 214 long transfers (15.6 to 60 days). The draw is experiment 82's.
  • Sanity. On all 16 series the lagless arm reproduces experiment 82: RO-NC 0.770, PF14 0.656. The harness check reproduces the stored flags of experiment 70 and experiment 71 exactly.
  • MW-weighted recall (95% interval). A 0.772 (0.688 to 0.840); B 0.794 (0.719 to 0.855); C 0.488 (0.407 to 0.588); D 0.724 (0.644 to 0.770).
  • Planned contrast C1, B minus A: +0.023 (-0.001 to +0.046); the lower end is not above zero, so the rule gives inconclusive. By shape, +0.020 (S2), +0.022 (S3), +0.027 (S4).
  • Descriptive contrasts: C2, C minus A, -0.283 (-0.331 to -0.216); D minus B -0.071 (-0.120 to -0.040); B minus A on long transfers +0.034 (-0.043 to +0.086).
  • Donor step 2 to 4 noise units. With no metered receiver, A finds 147 of 550 and B 181 (C 42). With a metered receiver, A finds 109 of 151, B 126, and C 66. Such misses are 0.637 of arm A's missed transfers (445 of 699) and 0.623 of arm B's (394 of 632).
  • Real transfers over 1 day (35, descriptive). RO-NC found 12 (A), 18 (B), and 11 (C). The convex demand model trained with the hand-filtered switching events masked. Those events include these real transfers, so the count favours arms B and C.
  • Why arm C loses. Its step statistic has 0.11 to 0.29 of arm A's noise, but a constant 3-day step keeps only 0.13 to 0.29 of its size (median 0.22). We predicted arm C within -0.03 to +0.03 of arm A and it landed far below. Across the 15 series, the median 99.9th percentile of the absolute statistic over its scale is 6.0 for arm C against 5.4 for arm A, so tails do not explain the gap on medians (arm C's heaviest series reaches 17.8 against 8.4, and arm B's median is 8.0 yet it wins). The hypothesis we think most likely is that the filter's level and transient follow the step within hours and so absorb the transfer. We did not test it further.

docs.title: Pre-run deviations
docs.text:
These were found before any detector was scored. The diagnostic read only residual noise and step retention, not recall.

  • Headline moved from arm C to arm B. A plan review asked for a positive control on the filter. The control adds a constant 4-noise-unit, 3-day step to the frozen residual and re-runs the filter. The filter kept a median 0.22 of the step, and arm B's noise was 0.6 to 1.2 times arm A's (median 0.8). Arm B was therefore expected to gain, and arm C stayed as a descriptive arm.
  • 15 Primaries, not 16. One Primary has no usable history for the convex demand model, so every arm is scored on the other 15 Primaries.
  • Fitted PV capacity, not pinned. The real-time capacity vintages exist for only 8 of the 16 series, so the convex model fits its PV capacity from the training window.
  • Own filter settings. The four filter settings of each series are fitted on its odd-month frozen residual, with the prior of experiment 106, because the settings of experiment 111 cover 6 series.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast, and error beside the quantile score. Not applicable: the experiment scores detector alarms against injected transfers and makes no probabilistic forecast.
  • Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction), fired for arm C. The positive control and the tail check are the tests above. The cause stays an untested hypothesis. Arm C is descriptive and carries no verdict, so the audit was not run.
  • Trigger 4 (leaving one site out changes the verdict), fired weakly for C1. Without donor 3, 8, or 9 the lower end rises above zero (+0.002, +0.007, and +0.003), which would read as small gain. Without donor 18 C1 falls to +0.013 (-0.003 to +0.032). The sign never flips, and the point value stays between +0.013 and +0.030, so no leave-one-out result reaches the +0.03 bar for supported. The audit was not run, because the verdict is below the bar either way.
  • Triggers 1, 3, 5, 6, and 7 did not fire. The sanity arm reproduces experiment 82, and arm D is below arm B as expected. C1's 95% interval is 0.047 wide, against the 0.08 that the plan expected.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Lab conditions. The convex model uses past weather (ERA5), which arrives about 5 days late, so a live service could not build these residuals. The convex model is not-for-production (experiment 122).
  • Hindsight in training. The convex demand model leaves out the hand-filtered switching events when it trains. The injected-transfer contrast is unaffected, because the injection is added after the fit.
  • Code location. The residual builder and detector scripts live in this experiment's folder. Moving them into packages/ needs a review.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Can a signal other than a better forecast find steps of 2 to 4 noise units with no metered receiver? Arm B still finds only 181 of 550 such transfers. One untried route is a signal from the sum of the neighbouring Primaries' power, or from the electricity network's topology above them.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, NRA: edge flows with a per-node drift term
docs.text:
The drift term cuts false flow by half to three quarters at equal or higher recall, but the fit still fails the known-answer gate, so the verdict is inconclusive. At the matched setting (step constant 3, level constant 0.3) the placebo flow falls from 20.42 MW-days a year without a drift term to between 9.70 and 4.83 with one. Recall for transfers of 3 to 24 hours rises from 0.631 to about 0.75. None of the 96 settings we screened met the recall targets and the 0.05 placebo limit together. The setting the tuning year chose finds 0.575 of the injected megawatts of 24 to 72 hours in the tuning year and 0.631 in the replicate year, against a target of 0.77. The fit reports the transfers it does find at 0.64 to 0.72 of their true size.

In the replicate year the chosen setting puts 4.27 MW-days a year on one pair with no interconnection, and part of that flow sits in two unlabelled jumps. The pair is D16 and D10. D10 has two jump windows that carry no label (see the data-processing page). Of the 4.27 MW-days, 1.58 lie inside those windows. Separately, 0.41 lie within 48 hours of a hand-filtered event and 3.86 lie away from one. The other replicate placebo pair, D5 and D11, holds 0.82 MW-days, all away from events. The placebo failure therefore partly reflects real, unlabelled structure in D10's data, and partly reflects drift that the fit leaves unexplained. Only the replicate year is independent of tuning.

docs.title: Question and results
docs.text:
Question. With a per-substation drift term, can a flow fit recover injected transfers that last hours to days without putting flow on pairs of substations that are not connected? The plan below was registered before any fit and was followed, except for the departures listed under "Deviations". The normal running arrangement (NRA) is the layout of the electricity network without transfers.

Tuning found no setting that meets both targets. Of the 96 settings screened, 38 were under the 0.05 MW-days limit on the placebo pairs, and 36 of those had a drift term. Among those 38 settings, the best margin was 0.714. The margin is the smaller of recall for 3 to 24 hours over 0.5 and recall for 24 to 72 hours over 0.77, so a margin of 1 means both targets are met. The chosen setting is step constant 3, level constant 1.0, drift variance 0.0016 points squared a day. Its tuning-screen recall is 0.429 for 3 to 24 hours and 0.548 for 24 to 72 hours, with 0.0007 MW-days a year on the full-year placebo.

The gate fails three of its four readings in at least one year, and release share passes in both years. A big transfer moves at least 10% of the receiving substation's 99th-percentile demand, and the tuning year holds 182 of them and the replicate year 173. The gate recall differs from the tuning-screen recall above because the gate draws set G with a new seed. Release share is the share of found transfers whose causal flow has fallen under 20% of the moved megawatts soon after the transfer ends.

Reading Needs Tuning year Replicate year Moved-MW ratio 0.8 to 1.25 0.434 (fail) 0.560 (fail) Recall, 24 to 72 h at least 0.77 0.575 (fail) 0.631 (fail) Recall, 3 to 24 h at least 0.5 0.472 (fail) 0.590 (pass) Placebo, MW-days a year under 0.05 0.0007 (pass) 4.27 (fail) Release share at least 0.5 0.987 on 75 found (pass) 0.95 on 100 found (pass)

The benchmark without a drift term is degenerate. At its best setting (step constant 100, level constant 1.0) the fit finds almost nothing (recall 0.002) and puts no flow on the tuning-year placebo pairs. In the replicate year the benchmark still puts 7.35 MW-days on a placebo pair. The comparison that matters is therefore the matched-recall comparison above.

The level penalty shrinks the transfers that are found. The median ratio of fitted to true mean flow over found transfers is 0.644 in the tuning year (75 found) and 0.721 in the replicate year (100 found). The moved-MW reading fails because of this shrinkage, whatever the recall.

Transfers of 7 to 30 days are partly absorbed, as predicted. Recall is 0.30 in the tuning year and 0.36 in the replicate year with the drift term, and 0.36 and 0.47 without the drift term. This arm is descriptive and carries no verdict.

docs.title: Real events
docs.text: On real data the fit finds 1 of 16 big labelled transfers, and 6 of its 120 flow runs match a logged event. This comparison is descriptive and was fitted after the gate. A decision edge is an interconnection between two Primary substations that the fit may put flow on, and the decision graph is the set of those edges. The graph holds 24 labelled transfers (10 in the tuning year, 6 in the replicate year, 8 in the scored year), of which 16 are big and 4 have no known direction. The one big event found is on D3 and D8, lasts 54.5 hours, and is labelled 2.5 MW against a fitted mean flow of 1.52 MW. A flow run is an unbroken stretch of nonzero fitted flow on one edge. Of the 120 flow runs (7 in the tuning year, 55 in the replicate year, 58 in the scored year), 6 matched a labelled transfer within 24 hours, 2 in each year, so precision is 5%.

docs.title: Deviations, checks, and what follows
docs.text:
Deviation: we added 36 settings to the grid, on the tuning year, before any gate reading. No registered setting met both targets: level constant 0.3 met the recall targets but not the placebo limit, and level constant 1.0 met the placebo limit but not the recall targets. The manager approved the extra settings, and the 0.05 limit is unchanged.

Deviation: the screen reads the placebo first. It skips the recall reading whenever the placebo is at least 0.05, to save compute.

Step 6 was skipped: the comparison with experiment 130's detector. The plan allowed a list of the transfers that experiment 130's refit-offset neighbour-count detector misses, with this fit's recall on them. Experiment 130 injected a different draw of transfers on other edges. A subset comparison was therefore not cheap, and this page reports no comparison.

No forecast contrast ran, because the gate failed. The check of the median forecast against the mean forecast per site therefore does not apply.

The thresholds, seeds, and chosen settings were written before the gate was read. The module change passed its 56 tests. Every number on this page comes from report.txt.

The audit trigger "a control fails" fired. The placebo control failed in the replicate year. The manager agreed that no Opus audit is needed, because the placebo failure is the finding and the post hoc check of D10's unlabelled jumps above tests an explanation for it. The triggers that concern forecast contrasts do not apply. The prediction put the chance of all four readings passing at about one in three, so the failure does not contradict it.

Each fit window around an injected transfer is shorter than the 72-day placebo tiles. A year-long fit may behave differently from a fit on either.

What the next experiment should answer. The drift term reduces false flow but does not reach the recall targets and the placebo limit together, and the level penalty shrinks the flows that survive. A candidate next step is a topology check on candidate flows, or a smaller level penalty combined with a check for unlabelled jumps in the placebo pairs. This page does not commit the project to either.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text: The plan tests one change to experiment 116: a drift offset for each substation. This page is the plan, committed before any fit. Experiment 116 fitted flows on the interconnections between Primary substations (the normal running arrangement, NRA, is the layout without those transfers). Its flow fit found injected transfers only at settings that also put flow on pairs of substations with no interconnection. A drift audit on 116's residuals (exploratory, no fit) found that slow drift alone gives 23 and 38 MW-days a year (megawatts of flow summed over the days of a year) on the two tuning placebo pairs. The drift is mostly shared by both substations of a pair, not opposite-signed, so this experiment adds a per-substation offset, not a pair term.

docs.title: Question and method
docs.text:
Question. With a per-substation drift term, can a flow fit recover injected transfers that last hours to days without putting flow on unconnected pairs?

Model. The objective is 116's: the Huber loss (quadratic near zero, linear beyond 1.5 noise scales) on the residuals of the frozen convex model, plus a step penalty and a level penalty on each flow. This experiment adds an offset d_i(t) for each substation. The offset is a random walk. Its change over one day has variance q_d, in points of effective capacity squared (a point is 1% of the substation's effective capacity), so the variance per half-hour row is q_d divided by 48. The fit alternates between flows and offsets until both settle (studies.dp_edge_flow.fit_flows, drift term in pull request 1431). The residuals are the arm-A0 residuals of experiment 116, so the drift term is the only change. Only half-hourly flows are used.

A big event moves a substation by at least a set number of megawatts. The threshold is 10% of the receiving substation's 99th-percentile cleaned demand, taken from rows of the tuning year's cut that hold a reading and fall outside hand-filtered events. A transfer is big when its mean moved megawatts reach the threshold; every injected transfer lasts at least 3 hours. The threshold is 0.56 to 1.1 MW at the four gate receivers, is frozen at the tuning cut for every year, and is set before any gate reading (e00131_threshold.py). In set T, injected transfers of 25% and 40% of the receiving load clear the threshold in most cases, and transfers of 0.5 MW and 10% rarely do. The script also prints 5 hand-filtered events, picked by a fixed random seed, beside the threshold, and the page reports that comparison. Events below the threshold are not looked for.

Injected transfers. The code is 116's, with new seeds. Sets T (tuning) and G (gate) hold 400 transfers each, balanced over 4 sizes (0.5 MW; 10%, 25%, and 40% of the receiving load) and 2 durations. The durations are 3 to 24 hours and 24 to 72 hours, log-uniform within each band. The split into two equal-count bands departs from a single log-uniform draw over 3 to 72 hours, because the gate reads the two bands separately. Set L holds 200 transfers of 25% and 40% that last 7 to 30 days. The two gate edges are D5–D16 and D10–D11. Each transfer is fitted on a window that starts 7 days before it and ends 7 days after its 48-hour post-event rows, so the drift term has a week of context on each side. Windows are shorter than the 72-day placebo tiles below, and a year-long fit may behave differently from either; the page says so.

Placebos. The placebo pairs are 116's pairs without an interconnection (tuning D5–D10 and D16–D14, replicate D5–D11 and D16–D10). Each is fitted in 72-day tiles over the year (the last tile is shorter, and the total is scaled by rows covered to a year), with the placebo path listed first and last. The larger flow counts, because the zero placebo reading of 116 came from the path order. Placebo tiles contain whatever real events fall in them, and injected windows exclude events within 48 hours.

docs.title: Tuning (tuning year only)
docs.text:
Stage 1 screens 60 settings. The grid is step constant {3, 10, 30, 100, 300} × level constant {0.3, 1.0} × drift variance q_d in {none, 0.0001, 0.0004, 0.0016, 0.0064, 0.0256} points² per day, with a Huber threshold of 1.5 noise scales. The five positive values of q_d give a standard deviation per day of 0.01 to 0.16 points. The value "none" is the benchmark, the same grid without a drift term, and is not one of the five tuned values. A level constant of 0 is left out because the minimiser is then not unique. Each setting is scored on the big transfers of set T and on 4 evenly spaced 72-day placebo tiles, scaled to a year.

Stage 2 reads the finalists on the whole year. Settings under 0.05 MW-days a year on both placebo pairs in both path orders at stage 1 are ranked by their margin, the smaller of (recall for 3 to 24 hours ÷ 0.5) and (recall for 24 to 72 hours ÷ 0.77). Ties go to the larger step constant. The top 3 are re-read on every placebo tile of the year. Among those still under 0.05, the setting with the largest margin is chosen. The Huber threshold of the chosen setting is then compared at 1.0, 1.5, and 3.0 noise scales by the same rule. If no setting is under 0.05 at stage 1, the setting with the smallest placebo flow is chosen, the gate is read anyway, and the verdict is inconclusive. The same rule runs separately for "none", which gives the benchmark's best setting. The chosen settings are written to decisions.json before the gate is read.

docs.title: Decision rule
docs.text:
The gate passes only if all four readings pass in the tuning year and in the replicate year. It is read on the big transfers of set G, drawn in each year, with the settings frozen. Only the replicate year is independent of tuning: the tuning-year placebo reading repeats the stage-2 computation on the same tiles, and the tuning-year recall readings use a different seed on the same residuals. The scored year (2025-26) is read only for C2 and C3, once, and only if the gate passes. The thresholds 0.77, 0.5, 0.05, and 0.8 to 1.25 are experiment 116's, kept by the brief for this experiment so that the two experiments' gates are comparable.

  1. Moved-MW ratio. The median over big transfers of the fitted mean flow over the true mean flow on the transfer's edge, over the transfer's rows and signed towards the receiver, lies between 0.8 and 1.25.
  2. Recall. Recall is the sum over rows of the smaller of the fitted and true flow (positive in the true direction), over the sum of the true flow, pooled over transfers. It is at least 0.77 for transfers of 24 to 72 hours and at least 0.5 for transfers of 3 to 24 hours.
  3. Placebo. Under 0.05 MW-days a year on each placebo pair of the year, with the placebo path first and last.
  4. Release. A big transfer is found when its hindsight recall is at least 0.5. At least half of the found transfers must have a causal flow under 20% of the moved MW at the larger of 6 hours and 10% of the duration after the end. The causal flow comes from refitting, with the drift term, the trailing 30 days of residuals up to 3.5 hours before the deadline. The reading needs at least 30 found transfers; fewer counts as a fail. The count is reported.

Not read as a verdict: the 7 to 30 day arm (set L, read in the tuning and replicate years; it reports whether the drift term absorbs long transfers), the real-event comparison, the benchmark, and any variant chosen after reading a result (labelled post hoc). Flow on unconnected paths inside the injected windows is not read.

If the gate fails on any reading, the verdict is inconclusive, and the take-home says whether the drift is separable from the transfers at this residual quality. Post hoc variants may be explored, labelled as such, and play no part in the verdict. If every reading fails, the session stops and asks the maintainer before any audit.

If the gate passes, C2 and C3 run as in experiment 116, with the winter and cold-night breakdowns. C2 is non-inferior when the upper end of the 98.33% interval for the change in day-ahead quantile score outside events (training without the found flows, minus training on every row) is under 0.05 points. C3 improves when the causal flows lower the quantile score on injected rows and the 48 hours after them by at least 0.5 points. Both met: supported. One met: partly supported. Neither: not supported. No threshold changes after reading.

Descriptive, no verdict. The hindsight flows of the whole decision graph are compared with the 31 logged pairs and the hand-filtered events (recall and precision, pairs named by D-label only). If experiment 130 has reported by then, the injected transfers and real events that its detector misses are listed with this fit's recall on them. The residuals' noise scales come from rows before the cut, where the frozen model was trained, so they understate the out-of-sample scale; 116 shares this property.

docs.title: Reviews, compute, and earlier advice
docs.text: A Sonnet reviewer read this plan before any fit. A Sonnet code review covers the module change (pull request 1431) and the scripts, and a Sonnet numbers review and a Sonnet prose review cover the finished page. There is no Opus review. The fits use CPU only, at most 4 workers while the machine is busy, with memory capped at 12 GB. The plan follows the advice of experiment 116: read the placebo with the path first and last, and fit a drift term before tuning the penalties. Any new data-processing finding goes into docs/ml-experiments/data-processing.md with the write-up.

docs.title: Experiment 132: does RO-NC find the real transfers at P12 and P13 with their readings restored?
docs.text: The refit-offset neighbour-count detector (RO-NC) missed the 6 real transfers at P12 and P13 because the cleaning step had flagged and removed the readings that show them, and with those readings restored it finds 4 of the 6. A load transfer is a switching operation that moves load from one substation or transformer to another. P12 and P13 are the two transformers of one Primary substation, and the 6 transfers last more than 1 day. In 4 of the 6, one transformer reads exactly 0 MW for nearly the whole transfer, and in a fifth (E44) for 10 half-hours. The cleaning rule substation_zero flags a reading of exactly 0 at a Primary substation as a telemetry fault. We re-read the 426 flagged half-hours from the cleaned power table. We also fitted an XGBoost forecasting model to each series and took its errors (the residual, observed minus predicted power, in MW) over 2025, each error from a model that never saw the block of time it scores. Experiment 17's residuals start only in 2026, because its XGBoost model needs a year of history. We then rescored RO-NC with the alarm thresholds and logistic-regression alarm scores that experiment 82 saved. Experiment 101, which scored RO-NC against the labelled real transfers, found 12 of the 35 that last more than 1 day. With the readings restored, RO-NC finds 17 of the 35 (a fraction of 0.49; 95% Wilson interval 0.33 to 0.64). The 35 are the transfers over 1 day among the 66 labelled in experiment 41, and 6 of the 35 are at P12 and P13.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• At P12 and P13: 4 of the 6 transfers are found (E49, E50, E52, and E54), against 0 of 6 (0.67; 0.30 to 0.90). The steps of those 4 transfers are 10.4 to 17.1 noise units. A noise unit is the usual size of the detector's 24-hour step on odd-numbered months, and a step is the largest 24-hour change in the residual within 2 hours of the labelled start. The 2 transfers not found are E44, where only 10 of the 99 half-hours read 0, and E59, where P12 has no readings inside the transfer. Their steps are 0.6 and 0.9 noise units.
  • Elsewhere: 13 of the other 29 transfers are found (0.45; 0.28 to 0.62), against 12 before the restoration. The extra transfer found is E55 at P13 and P14, whose step rises from 1.9 to 11.4 noise units now that P13 has readings. No transfer found before is lost.
  • MW-weighted recall on the 35: 0.631 (0.433 to 0.787), against 0.357 (0.169 to 0.554).
  • Injected transfers: these are synthetic transfers that experiment 82 added to the real power readings. The panel without the P12 and P13 residuals reproduces experiment 82's 31,200 stored rows exactly. On the panel with them, RO-NC's MW-weighted recall on the headline band of experiment 82 is 0.772 (0.669 to 0.858), against 0.770. Injected transfers that touch P12 or P13 are found 0.196 of the time, MW-weighted 0.767 (0.645 to 0.869), over 56 transfers and 3 shapes.
  • Restored half-hours: 426, all exactly 0 MW, none invented: E44 10 at each series, E49 102 at P12, E50 103 at P13, E52 1 at P12 and 100 at P13, and E54 100 at P13. E50 at P13 has 43 half-hours absent from the cleaned power table, and none are restored.
  • The guess: the pre-registered guess of 3 to 5 found was right on the count, and the step sizes were not the guessed ones: 4 transfers have steps over 10 noise units and 2 under 1.
  • Variants: blocked fits with equal sample weights, and fits with the 6 transfer windows masked from the training rows, give the same 17 found and the same outcome on every transfer.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• No leakage: every blocked fit has 0 training rows inside its held-out block or the 7-day purge, for all 3 variants and both residuals. e00132_report.py also lists the held-out block of each transfer.
  • Noise: the noise unit at P12 is 0.431 MW, 0.143 of capacity, against a median of 0.030 over the other 14 Primary substations (4.8 times). The noise unit at P13 is 0.037 of capacity (1.2 times). The 4 transfers found have steps over 10 noise units, so the larger noise unit at P12 does not decide them.
  • Alarm rate: at the stored thresholds, the unexplained alarms (alarms matching no labelled transfer and no logged closure) on odd-numbered months rise from 80 to 95 for PF14 (the single-series detector), from 75 to 88 for X (the refit-offset detector), from 80 to 87 for LOGIT_SAME (the same-sign neighbour count), and from 80 to 87 for RO-NC. The thresholds were not re-tuned, so the comparison with experiment 101 is not at a matched alarm rate. No sweep of the threshold was run.
  • Audit triggers: none fires. The control, experiment 82's injected rows on the panel without the P12 and P13 residuals, reproduces exactly.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Six transfers, descriptive only. Five of the 6 have readings at both transformers, and the load moves between the two transformers of one Primary substation, unlike the injected transfers, which move load between Primary substations. E59 has no readings at P12 inside the transfer.
  • The expected count does not separate the two rules. The pre-registered rule, injected recall at each transfer's step band and metering, gives 0.8 expected of the 6. The injected draw holds no transfer of 10 noise units or more without a metered receiver, so the rule fell back to a cell holding 4 injected outcomes. Using the metered cell (injected recall 0.949) gives 3.8 expected of the 4 transfers with steps over 10 noise units. The 4 found match the second figure.
  • The residuals use data from after each transfer. The held-out fits are out of sample, but they train on rows from after each transfer, and have at most 17 months of history.
  • The injected draw changed. More series have power readings, so the random sample of injected transfers accepts different transfers. RO-NC's recall on the long injected transfers (shape S1, even-numbered months) is 0.449, against 0.519.

docs.title: What the next experiment could test
docs.text:
A next experiment could re-tune the thresholds on the new panel and check that the 4 found transfers survive. Whether RO-NC can find the 2 transfers with steps under 1 noise unit depends on how the detector is built, not on which readings are restored.

Code: ml-experiments/00132-ro-nc-rescored-with-p12-and-p13-residuals-in-2025/; every number above is printed by e00132_restore.py, e00132_report.py, and e00132_inj_report.py.

docs.title: Experiment 133: do learned noise settings beat the fixed ones in GAM-K's filter?
docs.text:
Choosing the filter's noise settings for each substation by next-day score did not improve the forecast on later months. The gain was 0.044 points on the months that chose the settings and 0.009 points (99% interval -0.044 to +0.030) on the scored year. A single setting shared by every substation did as well, and letting the observation variance follow recent errors did not widen the 0.95 quantile where it fell short, on cold nights. The verdict is inconclusive. The scored-year gain is too small to justify building either change, and the grid did not find a minimum, so this experiment cannot say whether a wider search would.

We asked whether the Kalman filter of the convex demand model with the filter (GAM-K, experiment 111) forecasts the next day better when its noise settings are chosen by next-day score instead of by likelihood. The filter tracks, in each of 4 bands of hours of the day, a slowly moving level and a quickly decaying transient of the convex model's error. Experiment 118 and experiment 128 found that the likelihood of such settings scatters about 10 times between fits, so we ran the filter on a grid of 1,323 settings per substation on a graphics processing unit (GPU), ranked the cells by next-day error on the odd months of 2024-07 to 2025-06, re-scored the best 20 with the full ensemble forecast, and judged the winner on the even months and on the scored year. We also tried the scalar variant of VIKING (variance-inferring Kalman filter; de Vilmarest and Wintenberger (2022)), which tracks the observation variance online, and used it to scale the spread of the forecast. The design is in Plan below.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. FIX: experiment 111's stored settings. GRID: the cell chosen per substation. POOL: one cell shared by all substations. VK0: GRID's cell with the online observation variance, mean correction only. VK1: VK0 with each row's spread scaled by the online variance. TRAIL: GRID's cell with the spread scaled by the trailing 7-day root mean square of the filter's one-step errors. Every arm reads experiment 111's stored monthly fits, calibration, and solar shrink, and refits its own spread on the odd months, so only the filter and the spread differ.
  • Row set and period. fold_a_daily_gap_v1's 292 scored runs (2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30) at D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16, with D9 scored beside them; the even months of 2024-07 to 2025-06 are the replicate; rows outside the hand-filtered switching events. The convex model refits monthly (experiment 111's stored fits), so the contrasts between filter settings do not depend on the refit schedule.
  • Absolute scores, 12 to 36 hours, scored year (mean quantile score, points of effective capacity): FIX 2.498, GRID 2.488, POOL 2.462, VK0 2.475, VK1 2.485, TRAIL 2.486. Over all leads (0.5 to 168 hours): FIX 2.800 (it reproduces experiment 111's GAM-K), GRID 2.783, POOL 2.771, VK0 2.751, VK1 2.784, TRAIL 2.793. Replicate months, 12 to 36 hours: FIX 2.393, GRID 2.398, POOL 2.352, VK0 2.403, VK1 2.410, TRAIL 2.394.
  • C1, GRID minus FIX (headline), 12 to 36 hours. Scored year -0.009 (99% interval -0.044 to +0.030; 3 of 5 substations better, 8 of 12 months negative). Replicate +0.005 (-0.031 to +0.073). Odd months -0.044 (-0.062 to -0.019; 5 of 5 substations better). The prediction was -0.02 to -0.08 with a replicate gain of at most 60% of the odd-month gain, so the prediction failed on the replicate. Verdict by the decision rule: inconclusive, because the gain lives on the months that chose the cells; only 1 of 5 substations improves in the replicate, and leaving out D5 turns the scored-year contrast positive (see Checks).
  • C2, POOL minus GRID. Scored year -0.026 (-0.078 to +0.013), replicate -0.046 (-0.096 to +0.016), odd months +0.053 (+0.0004 to +0.144; POOL is worse on the months that chose GRID, as it must be). The interval is wider than the +/-0.03 equivalence band, so by the rule the sign decides, and it favours POOL out of sample.
  • C3a, VK0 minus GRID. Scored year -0.013 (-0.045 to +0.005), replicate +0.005 (-0.003 to +0.012); not under the -0.03 bar. C3b, VK1 minus GRID. Scored year -0.004 (-0.052 to +0.027), replicate +0.012 (-0.014 to +0.037). Over all leads, C3a is -0.032 (-0.104 to -0.004) in the scored year and -0.007 (-0.014 to +0.000) in the replicate, a descriptive result, because the settings were not tuned for all-lead score. C3b over all leads is +0.001 (-0.101 to +0.051) and +0.029 (+0.012 to +0.044).
  • Cold-night coverage of the 0.95 quantile, 12 to 36 hours, scored year: FIX 0.879, GRID 0.864, POOL 0.877, VK0 0.868, VK1 0.865, TRAIL 0.867, against 0.95 and against all rows at 0.940 to 0.944. The change against GRID is +0.003 (-0.003 to +0.011) for VK0 and +0.000 (-0.013 to +0.015) for VK1, so the predicted rise of 3 to 8 points is excluded (against FIX the two arms are lower, 0.868 and 0.865 against 0.879).
  • Mechanism. The log correlation of the tail statistic at the cutoff with the next day's absolute error is 0.29 (online variance) and 0.30 (trailing innovations) over all rows, and -0.03 and +0.06 on cold nights. Recent residual size predicts error on average and not on the nights that matter.
  • Tails, 12 to 36 hours, scored year (coverage; pinball loss): the 0.01 quantile covers 0.016 to 0.020 and the 0.99 quantile 0.982 to 0.984 for every arm, and the pinball loss at the 0.95 and 0.99 quantiles is 0.633 to 0.646 and 0.195 to 0.204. POOL has the lowest pinball loss at the 0.05 quantile (0.620) and ties TRAIL at the 0.01 quantile (0.178).
  • Breakouts, descriptive, 12 to 36 hours, scored year (mean quantile score for FIX, GRID, POOL): winter 2.550, 2.539, 2.497; winter nights 2.112, 2.055, 2.025; cold nights 2.351, 2.304, 2.279; holidays and Christmas 2.889, 2.846, 2.778. POOL has the lowest score in each, though it was no better than FIX on the tuning months (PH1 +0.009).
  • Post hoc PH1, POOL minus FIX (added after the scored year was read; no verdict). 12 to 36 hours: scored year -0.036 (99% interval -0.076 to -0.0003; 4 of 5 substations better, 9 of 12 months negative); replicate -0.041 (-0.104 to +0.017; 5 of 5 substations better). All leads, scored year: -0.030 (-0.070 to +0.010).
  • Fitted values. Every GRID cell touches an edge of the grid (figure 5): five of six sit at the lowest transient standard deviation of the grid (0.61 times the observation standard deviation), four at the highest decay factor (0.98 per half-hour), D10 at the lowest (0.73), and D16 inside the range (0.95). POOL is one cell at both edges (level variance 0.37 times the observation variance per day, transient standard deviation 0.61, decay factor 0.98). FIX's values are 1.3 to 44 and 2.8 to 9.0 for the same two ratios. The grid did not find a minimum, so a wider grid could change C1.
  • Selection. The Spearman correlation between the proxy-error ranking of the 20 best cells and their ensemble quantile-score ranking was 0.70 to 0.94 across substations, so the cheap ranking does track the target score. The online variance's random-walk variance went to the edge of its grid (e^-5 per half-hour), with mean tuning scores of 2.2939, 2.2928, and 2.2928 for the three values, so the random-walk variance barely mattered.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, GRID, 12 to 36 hours (points of capacity): D5 -0.117, D9 -0.041, D11 -0.018, D14 +0.011, D16 +0.008, D10 -0.007. FIX's D5 is -0.097; no GRID or VK0 spread shifts the forecast by more than 0.12 points, but TRAIL and VK1 do at D5 (-0.162 and -0.137).
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each contrast, 12 to 36 hours, scored year (99% intervals): C1 -0.013 (-0.070 to +0.053), C2 -0.049 (-0.136 to +0.021), C3a -0.019 (-0.051 to +0.002), C3b -0.019 (-0.051 to +0.002). Each has the sign of its quantile-score contrast, so the audit trigger for a disagreement between mean and quantile scores did not fire.
  • Controls. The reproduction control passed: FIX's scored median forecast matches experiment 111's stored GAM-K rows with a maximum absolute difference of 0 at every substation. The selection control passed: on simulated streams the cell chosen on odd-month cases scored 1.0031 times the true setting's error on even-month cases for the filter's own model, and 0.9997 times for a model with a seasonal wobble added.
  • Tracking gate (not informative). The pre-registered pass rate is 100% for every arm on real residuals and on AR(1) noise at three injected sizes (half, 0.2, and 0.1 of the residual standard deviation as the peak; the last two are post hoc), because the filter is linear and the shifted and unshifted streams share one noise realisation, so every draw gives the same answer. The tracking ratio (filtered midday gain over the injected midday shift) is 0.97 for FIX, 1.13 for GRID, 1.06 for POOL, and 1.21 for VK0 on real residuals (first-order autoregressive noise, AR(1): 0.98, 1.14, 1.07, 1.24), so none of the chosen settings loses a slow change. The figures of 0.22 (real) and 0.80 (AR(1)) from experiment 128 are for a refitted filter and are not comparable. This experiment makes no claim about identifying any weight.
  • Audit triggers. Audit trigger 2 (a result against its own prediction) fired for C1, and the explanation, that choosing among the 20 best of 1,323 cells on a flat surface overfits the chosen months, is recorded but not tested here. Audit trigger 4 (one substation drives the contrast) fired: leaving D5 out turns C1 from -0.009 to +0.024, because D5's scored gain is -0.160. Audit trigger 7 (a later experiment builds on the result) may apply, because experiment 135 takes GRID's values as a baseline. No second-model audit has been run.
  • Not run. The curtailment-cost saving against the manual heuristic, because it needs a node's forecast and its generators' forecasts.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• A wider grid, and a smoothed or blocked choice of the cell, to see whether the odd-month gain of 0.044 survives when the cells are not at the grid's edge.
  • One filter setting shared by every substation, as the default for GAM-K, tested on its own with the same planned contrast against FIX (PH1 here is post hoc, and its interval barely excludes zero).
  • A spread that responds to cold weather directly (the temperature itself), because the size of recent errors did not predict cold-night error.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text: The plan, as committed before any fit and triaged after one plan review, is in the git history of this file (the commit "Experiment 133 plan"). The changes made after the review were: a grid of 1,323 settings (log q -4 to 6, not the 4,032-setting grid planned); an online-variance random-walk grid of e^-9, e^-7, and e^-5; D18 left out for lack of tuning readings; sigma_eps held at 1 for the grid arms because the correction depends only on ratios; a two-step choice of cell; VK0 and VK1 as separate arms; a trailing-innovation arm (TRAIL); decision rules for every contrast; and the gate made larger. Pre-run clarifications made before the first fit: POOL is one shared cell in ratio units (the filter is scale-free, so "scaled per substation" adds nothing) and is chosen on the step-1 error alone; the gate's injected shift peaks at half of each substation's residual standard deviation, because the stored fits do not expose the PV effect in points.

docs.title: Differentiable physics: a same-weekday error profile on top of GAM-K
docs.text: Take-home: using the same weekday's recent errors, instead of the last 14 days' errors alike, lowers the day-ahead quantile score by only about 0.011 points (0.5% of 2.44), so it is not worth adding to recipe R. Recipe R is the baseline correction: it subtracts 0.75 times the mean of the last 14 days' errors by half-hour from GAM-K's forecast. One point is 1% of a substation's capacity, and lower scores are better. The gain is below the 0.02-point threshold set in the plan before any fit, and the scored-year interval includes zero. The gain sits on Mondays and Fridays and is absent from Tuesday to Thursday. A variant that groups days into five day types did better (0.022 points against recipe R, exploratory) and is the version worth testing next, limited to day D+1. The verdict is not supported.

docs.title: What was asked, and the answer in plain terms
docs.text:
The question was whether the correction to the day-ahead forecast should look at the same weekday as the day being forecast. The forecast is the electricity demand of five Primary substations (the stations that step power down from 33 kV to 11 kV) for the day after the 09:00 UTC forecast origin, from the physics-based demand model with a Kalman filter on ECMWF ensemble weather (GAM-K, arm K0; experiment 111). Experiment 115 found that subtracting 0.75 times the mean of the last 14 days' errors by half-hour (recipe R) lowers the day-ahead score by 0.09 points. We kept R and added a shrunk same-weekday profile to it.

Answer. The shrunk weekday profile (arm RB) scored 2.424 points against 2.436 for R in the scored year. Scores are in points of effective capacity (1 point is 1% of a substation's capacity), lower is better, and rows inside the hand-filtered switching events are left out. The settings were chosen on the odd months of July 2024 to June 2025 (tuning months); the even months are the replicate months, and the scored year is 2 July 2025 to 29 June 2026 (292 runs).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. K0 (GAM-K); R (recipe R; its scores match experiment 115's); Rh (R with the holiday rule, kappa 0.75); L1 (last week's same-weekday error, kappa 0.5); RW (mean same-weekday error of the last 3 weeks, kappa 0.5); RB (kappa, the correction weight, 0.75; lambda, the weekday share, 0.25; n, the number of weeks, 3); RB-day-types (kappa 0.75, lambda 0.5, n 4 weeks). Settings are fleet-wide and were chosen by the tuning rows' D+1 mean absolute error of the median. No demand model was refitted (experiment 111's monthly refits are reused).
  • Rows and compute. 66,844 D+1 rows in the scored year and 41,126 in the replicate months at the five decision substations (D5, D10, D11, D14, D16), with D9 beside them. Fits take seconds; the tuning, gate, and frame builds took a few minutes on 3 cores.
  • Absolute scores, scored year, D+1 (all leads). K0 2.524 (2.812), R 2.436 (2.744), Rh 2.440 (2.745), L1 2.535 (2.879), RW 2.452 (2.803), RB 2.424 (2.750), RB-day-types 2.414 (2.756). D9 beside them: K0 2.194, R 2.123, RB 2.127.
