    • C4, blend minus the best single family: the table above.
  • Day by day (own history, blend minus climatology). The change is -38.7% at day 1, -30.0% at day 3, -20.3% at day 5, -13.3% at day 7, -11.0% at day 8, -10.0% at day 9, and -9.2% (-12.6 to -5.1) at day 10. The blend's margin over climatology is still shrinking at day 10 but is far from zero.
  • Per farm. The blend beats climatology and XGBoost at every farm and every day band in both settings (Figure 4). The margin over climatology at days 8 to 10 runs from -8.0% (farm E) to -13.2% (farm B) in own history.
  • Tail calibration (own history). Coverage of the 0.01 quantile (nominal 0.01) is 0.033 to 0.035 for the blend, 0.036 to 0.044 for XGBoost, and 0.038 for climatology. Coverage of the 0.05 quantile is 0.062 to 0.073 for the blend and rises with lead for XGBoost from 0.086 to 0.117. Coverage of the 0.95 quantile is 0.948 to 0.956 for the blend and 0.931 to 0.945 for XGBoost. Coverage of the 0.99 quantile is 0.990 to 0.992 for the blend. The pinball loss at the 0.99 quantile is 0.31 at day 1 and 0.35 at days 8 to 10 for the blend, against 0.54 to 0.56 for XGBoost, 0.43 for climatology, and 0.57 to 0.64 for manual_heuristic.
  • Reference floors. climatology scores 8.64 and manual_heuristic 8.69 to 8.83 at every band. Their difference is -0.6% (-5.0 to +5.2) at day 1 and -2.2% (-7.2 to +3.4) at days 8 to 10, so neither is the better floor.

docs.title: Method and schedule
docs.text:
• Lead bands. Day d takes, for each half-hour, the 00 UTC ensemble run whose lead is 12 + 24(d-1) to 36 + 24(d-1) hours. A run is usable 9 hours after its init_time, and the first half-hour scored is 12 hours after it. Bands pool days 4 and 5, days 6 and 7, and days 8 to 10. Each band has its own fit, blend weights, and scores. Day 1 reproduces experiment 300's weather exactly, and its blend scores 5.30 against 5.27 there, a difference that fits the change of refit schedule.
  • Ensemble step. The ensemble's stamps are 3-hourly to lead 144 hours and 6-hourly after. From day 6 the shortwave value is a 6-hour mean, spread over the 12 half-hours of its period by the cosine of the sun's zenith angle (the angle between the sun and the vertical), and the temperature is interpolated linearly between 6-hourly stamps. The plant's response to each of 51 members is computed per half-hour.
  • Own power. The farm's observed power enters at a lag of ceil(lead / 24) days. That power is known at run time. The weather at every lead is the ensemble run itself, which exists at forecast time.
  • Schedule. Quarterly refits (the screening schedule) on all earlier months, each refit's training rows ending one day before the quarter starts, predicting the runs of its 3 months. Weekly refits were not run, so absolute scores could shift a little. We did not test whether the contrasts between arms depend on the schedule. The MDN has three seeds, averaged. A run belongs to the month of its init_time, and the 12 scored months are the months of the runs.
  • Arms. climatology, manual_heuristic, the plant alone ("P2", binned by forecast and ensemble spread), the GAM (depth-1 boosted trees on P2's 11 quantiles as base margin), the MDN (three-component Gaussian mixture on the residual from P2), XGBoost (depth 6, same inputs, no base margin), the blend (per-level simplex weights fitted on earlier months, equal weights for the first three months), and the GAM, MDN, XGBoost, and blend without lagged power (own history only).
  • Row set. The scored-year runs (2025-09 to 2026-08) with finite quantiles in every arm, including both floors; the code checks equal row counts. Quantiles are sorted before any loss.
  • Reference floors. The manual_heuristic takes the quantiles of 13 earlier observed powers (analogues 1 to 6 weeks and 49 to 55 weeks before the half-hour). An analogue counts only when it was observed before the run, so the 1-week analogue is dropped at leads over 7 days. climatology uses the farm's powers before the scored year.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, own history (points of capacity, farms pooled). Blend +0.04 at day 1 and +0.72 at days 8 to 10, GAM +0.27 and +0.51, MDN +0.42 and +0.32, XGBoost -0.91 and -0.78, climatology -2.07 at every band. XGBoost's median sits below its mean forecast, as in experiment 300; the blend's median sits above it by under 0.8 points.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each score contrast. Blend minus XGBoost on the absolute error of the mean forecast is -4.0% at day 1 (9.92 against 10.34) and -4.5% at days 8 to 10 (15.60 against 16.34). Blend minus climatology is -42.8% at day 1 and -10.1% at days 8 to 10 (15.60 against 17.35). The error of the mean forecast and the score point the same way in every band, so trigger 3 did not fire.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 2 (a result contradicting its prediction) fired: the margin over climatology stays near 10% at days 8 to 10 against a predicted fall under 5%. We tested an explanation after the fact. We refitted P2 (own history, days 8 to 10) with each row's plant forecast and spread replaced by their average over the training rows of the same month and half-hour. That plant (P2 alone), which carries the season and the sun's path but none of the ensemble's day-specific weather, scores 8.24 against 8.63 for climatology (-4.6%). P2 alone with the real ensemble weather scores 7.91 (-8.4%), against the blend's 7.77 (-10.1%). So about 4.6 percentage points of the plant's 8.4% margin come from conditioning on season and sun geometry, which climatology's coarse cells (one year of farm history per month and half-hour) do not do, and about 3.8 points come from the ensemble's forecast weather. At day 1 the same check scores 8.41 for P2 alone with averaged weather and 5.55 with the real ensemble weather, so the weather matters most at short leads. The check is post hoc (e00310_climatological_plant.py). Other triggers. Trigger 4 (leaving one farm out flips a contrast) did not fire: the blend beats climatology and XGBoost at all six farms in every band, so dropping a farm cannot flip a sign (Figure 4). Trigger 5 did not fire: no ablated arm beats its full arm by more than its interval's half-width. Triggers 1 (a failed control), 3 (the mean-forecast error disagrees), 6 (an interval more than twice or under half as wide as a sister experiment's: day 1's interval for blend minus XGBoost is 2.3 points wide against 2.3 in experiment 300), and 7 (a later design depends on the result) did not fire. No audit was required.

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• Post hoc. The climatological-plant check and the day-by-day slices were added after the scores. The 98.75% level covers the four planned contrasts per band only.
  • Not covered. Weekly refits, leads under 12 hours or over 252 hours, the curtailment value (the farms are single series and the node metric needs a substation with its generators), and the GAM, MDN, and XGBoost without lagged power in zero history.
  • Climatology uses older history. climatology is frozen at the data before 2025-09, while the forecasts refit each quarter on all earlier months. The margins over climatology in later quarters therefore include the forecasts' use of newer history.
  • Intervals. Only the four planned contrasts per band are at the 98.75% level. The per-farm, per-day, and extra contrasts use the same interval width and are descriptive. Every arm holds the same row count in each band and setting, the _nolag arms included.
  • Ensemble fields after lead 144 hours. The shortwave value is treated as a 6-hour mean there. The eight extra ensemble fields (humidity, longwave, precipitation, pressure, wind, and 500 hPa height) come from experiment 270's extraction, and we did not check that their period meaning is the same across lead 144 hours.
  • Lower tail. Actual output falls below the 0.01 quantile 3.2 to 3.5 times too often for the blend, and up to 4.4 times too often for XGBoost, at every lead, as in experiment 300.
  • Next. Weekly refits of the MDN alone at days 1 to 10 would give the absolute scores for a first production model; a longer ensemble history would replace the farm history behind climatology's coarse cells.

docs.title: Does a mixture-density neural network for the forecast bands lower the quantile score of Primary demand research default 1, with the gain in the protected tail groups?
docs.text:
Replacing the forecast bands of Primary demand research default 1 with bands from a neural network lowers the quantile score by 0.037 points of capacity over the scored year, but the gain comes almost entirely from one Primary, D10, and the new bands are worse on sunny daylight half-hours, so we do not adopt them. A similar gain, 0.034 points, appears in the even months of 2024-25, measured against the stored bands of experiment 169 and not against the default itself. The next test should keep the current bands on sunny daylight half-hours, or train the head on the quantile score itself, because the head's gain sits in the 0.05 to 0.25 quantiles and not in the extreme tails.

A band is the range between two quantile levels of the forecast, and a forecast here is 11 quantile levels from 0.01 to 0.99 for each half-hour. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over those 11 levels, in points, meaning percentage points of the substation's effective capacity (its rated demand); lower is better. A Primary is a primary substation, D5 to D16 are anonymised Primaries, and the scored year runs from 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30. Sunny daylight half-hours are daylight half-hours that a solar-radiation threshold marks as sunny, and ordinary rows are all rows that are neither sunny daylight half-hours nor cold winter nights (days with a mean temperature below 2 °C, night hours only).

We asked whether the bands of Primary demand research default 1 (the GAM stack A+H+S of experiments 220 and 251) can be improved by a small neural network that outputs a mixture of three bell curves. The default's median stays as it is, so only the width and skew of the bands change. We trained the network on the stack's own past errors, refitted it every month on the preceding 24 months, and scored it on the same 561,207 half-hours as experiment 251. The mixture-density design follows experiment 287 and experiment 300 for metered solar farms, and the input features and monthly cuts are those of experiment 278. The quantile score of the six Primaries fell from 2.579 to 2.542 points of capacity (lower is better), in 9 of 12 months, but the condition on harm to sunny daylight half-hours failed, so the result is a candidate under the research default rule.

Verdict partly supported. Conditions 1 (gain), 3 (replication), and 5 (serving) hold. Condition 2 (no harm) fails on sunny daylight half-hours. Condition 4 (controls, with every audit trigger resolved) is resolved by a Sonnet audit that found no calculation error, but trigger 4 shows that the gain depends on D10. No arm is adopted, and the verdict is partly supported. The plan's verdict rule named no wording for this case, so partly supported is the closest of the six verdict words. Nothing is added to the log of versions.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Arms. Default: arm 1 of experiments 220 and 251 (stored; median, bands, and solar summary unchanged). Arm M: the default's median, with every other quantile set by the mixture-density head (average of three seeds). Arm MW: arm M with the default's cold-day widening applied to the head's upper offsets (multipliers 1.653, 1.363, 1.261, and 1.162 at q75, q90, q95, and q99 on rows whose ensemble-mean 24-hour temperature is below 2 C, read from experiment 169's stored arms). At most one arm may be adopted, so the gain is read at 99.5%.
  • The head. A three-component Gaussian mixture on the residual of arm D's mean forecast (arm D is the convex model with a Kalman filter of experiment 155), in units of the stored 5% to 95% width over 3.29, with the inputs of experiment 278's arm 2: arm D's mean, the Kalman filter's level and anomaly, the stored width, lead, ensemble-driver weather, calendar flags, and the Economy 7 flag. The head is trained on the negative log-likelihood, and its quantiles are shifted so that its median equals the default's median. The shift keeps the median unchanged and avoids training on the in-sample residuals of the neural median head.
  • Cadence. A refit at each month start on the rows of the preceding 24 months whose longest target lies before the refit date, with every fourth month held out for early stopping, as experiment 278 does.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Kind and tier. kind: change, family Primary demand, starting from Primary demand research default 1. The change is a tier 2 change (a new fitted head, with the feature code of experiment 278 imported), and the new-head minimum gain of 0.03 points applies. The brief for this experiment quoted 0.02 points; the rule page owns the value, and the point estimate (-0.037) clears both.
  • Absolute scores, six Primaries (quantile score; twCRPS at the 95th percentile of earlier power). Default 2.579; 0.1708. Arm M 2.542; 0.1703. Arm MW 2.543; 0.1705. BG2 2.715; 0.2024 (BG2 is the XGBoost research benchmark, not the production forecast). Manual heuristic 3.397; 0.2463. Climatology 3.665; 0.2627. The default scored 2.579 (six) and 2.617 (five decision Primaries), matching experiment 251 within 0.005, so the reproduction gate passed.
  • Arm M minus default, quantile score. -0.037 (95% interval -0.060 to -0.014; 99.5% interval -0.070 to -0.005), 9 of 12 months better. The three worse months are February, March, and April 2026 (+0.011, +0.031, +0.011). Arm MW minus default is -0.036 (99.5% interval -0.070 to -0.004). Arm M minus arm MW is -0.001 (-0.003 to +0.000), so keeping the cold-day widening changes the score by at most 0.003 points here.
  • Against BG2 and the manual heuristic. Arm M minus BG2 is -0.173 (95% interval -0.314 to -0.040), against -0.136 (-0.278 to -0.005) for the default. Arm M minus the manual heuristic is -0.855 (-1.123 to -0.613).
  • Gate on harm (one-sided 95% upper bound of arm M minus default, pooled six Primaries). Headline -0.018, passes (tolerance 0.02). Pinball loss at q01 -0.006 and at q99 +0.001, passes (0.05). Cold winter nights -0.064 (estimate -0.136), passes (0.05). twCRPS at the 95th percentile +1.3% relative, passes (2%). Sunny daylight half-hours +0.074 (estimate +0.029, 95% interval -0.017 to +0.084), fails (0.05). Arm MW gives the same pattern (sunny daylight bound +0.077; twCRPS +1.8%).
  • Replicate year (condition 3). The even months of 2024-25, 360,122 rows. Research default 1's neural median head and solar summary exist for the scored year only, so the comparison is the head against the stored bands of arm A (experiment 169) around arm A's own median. Arm M minus the arm A bands is -0.034 (95% interval -0.052 to -0.016, resampling origin days, not months, so it is narrower than a month-block interval would be); arm MW -0.034. The sign matches and the size exceeds half of 0.03.
  • P1 and P3 held, P2 failed, and P4 does not apply. P1 held (-0.037 against at least -0.02). P2 failed: the 0.01 and 0.99 levels give 9% of the gain and cold winter night rows give 5%, against 60% predicted. The prediction P2 mixed levels and row groups, so we scored it both ways before reading any score: the 0.01 and 0.99 levels give 9% of the gain, and the cold winter night rows give 5%, and both fall short of 60%. P3 held: the 0.95 coverage on ordinary rows is 0.935 against 0.945 for the default, within 2 points of 95%. P4 is not applicable. The stop rule did not fire: the first six months improved by 0.059.
  • Where the gain is. By Primary: D10 -0.157 (-0.305 to -0.049), D14 -0.024 (-0.033 to -0.013), D16 -0.017, D9 -0.011, D11 -0.005, D5 -0.001 (none of the six Primaries has a pass or fail). Leaving D10 out gives -0.012 (-0.028 to +0.005); leaving any other Primary out keeps -0.039 to -0.043. By level the gain is largest at q05 (-0.007), q10 (-0.008), and q25 (-0.006). By group: ordinary rows -0.048, Economy 7 nights -0.083, Christmas -0.068, leads 12 to 36 hours -0.025, bank holidays +0.014 (-0.013 to +0.028).
  • Tails. The table below gives coverage and pinball loss at the four tail levels. On cold winter nights the q95 coverage is 0.970 for the default, 0.941 for arm M, and 0.973 for arm MW. On sunny daylight half-hours the q05 coverage is 0.081 for the default and 0.126 for both new arms (nominal 0.05). q01 means the 0.01 quantile level, and so on.
  • Operator-visible behaviour. Figure 7 shows the winter profile at D10: the Economy 7 step at about 00:30 local time stays inside both sets of bands, and arm M's bands are narrower than the default's overnight. Figure 5 shows the narrower cold-night bands in one January week, and figure 6 shows the narrower lower band at midday in one June week, and the q05 coverage on sunny daylight half-hours rises above its nominal 5% at those midday half-hours.
  • The head makes the bands skewed upward. The mean of arm M's 11 quantiles sits 0.20 points above its median, against 0.02 for the default, so the head makes the bands skewed upward.
  • Rows and schedule. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, six Primaries D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16; scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30; leads 0.5 to 168 hours, so leads of 7 to 10 days are not scored and NGED's horizon is 1 to 10 days. Outside hand-filtered events. The head is refitted monthly on 24 rolling months, three seeds averaged, on the CPU (about 25 s per fit). The default's stored forecasts are not refitted. Weather at lag times is the ensemble weather available at forecast time. The GAM stack still trails BG2 on sunny April to June half-hours (experiment 251); this experiment did not change that.
  • Weather in the training rows. The 24-month pool of the earliest scored refits holds up to about a year of past-weather rows (origins before 2024-07), while the scored rows use ensemble weather, as in experiment 278.
  • Code reused. ml-experiments/00278-stack-retraining-cadence/ (e00278_h_data.py for the rows and inputs) and the scoring pattern of experiment 251, copied into this folder. No earlier folder was edited.
  • What to try next. (1) Train the head on the pinball loss of the 11 levels, which is the quantity the quantile score averages (twice the mean), and not on the likelihood. (2) Keep the default's bands on sunny daylight half-hours and use the head elsewhere, as a new pre-registered experiment, because the research default rule does not let a failed arm be adjusted after its result is known. (3) Find why D10 gains 0.157 points: experiment 220 also located the gap between the neural median head's own bands and the default's at D10.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus the mean forecast, per Primary (points; the mean is arm D's, and the median is the default's, which every arm shares). D10 +0.72, D11 -0.50, D14 -0.20, D16 -0.84, D5 +0.01, D9 -0.75.
  • Error of the median beside the quantile-score contrasts. The median is the default's in every arm, so the mean absolute error of the median is identical (4.510) and trigger 3 cannot fire.
  • Controls. The reproduction gate passed. The assertion that every training target precedes its refit date held in all 54 fits (18 monthly refits times 3 seeds). Arm MW equals arm M on every row at or above 2 C, and the median of arm M equals the default's on every row.
  • Triggers. Trigger 4 fired: leaving D10 out moves the interval of arm M minus default across zero (-0.012, -0.028 to +0.005). The audit was run by a fresh Sonnet agent and not by Opus, by the maintainer's standing instruction. The agent re-derived the headline contrasts from the stored arrays and found no difference above 0.002 points. Leaving D10 out gives an interval that spans zero, so the gain depends on one Primary. Trigger 5 did not fire (arm M differs from its nested arm MW by 0.001, and the interval includes zero). Triggers 1, 2, 6, and 7 did not fire.

docs.title: How good must an LSC detector be to beat the best no-detector forecast?
docs.text:
This experiment asks how accurate a load shift detector has to be to improve on a forecast that uses no detector. A load shift (LSC, load shift screen) moves demand from one Primary substation, a substation that feeds local demand, to its neighbours for hours or days. We worked on 44 copies of the real power record of six Primary substations (labelled D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16), each copy with shifts added by a simulator, 411 shifts in all (experiment 141 made the copies). The forecast, K0, is a Kalman filter (an updating estimate of the recent forecast error) that corrects a weather-driven forecast using recent power. Experiment 297 found that an XGBoost quantile regression model of K0's error (BAND_HEAD), which uses no detector, beats the RO-NC detector (the refit-offset neighbour-count detector) when RO-NC's mask sets aside readings. One arm still beat BAND_HEAD on curtailment cost, the forecast cost of cutting a generator's output (£2,000 per MWh, relative between forecasts): perfect knowledge, with the true megawatts of each shift subtracted from the readings K0 sees and added back to K0's forecast. We spoilt that arm one property at a time: recall (the share of shifts found), the delay before a shift is known, the error in the megawatts, and precision (the share of alarms that are real shifts). We report the worst level that still beats BAND_HEAD. We also tested band position, how surprising recent readings are against the error bands of the forecast with no recent-power correction (GAM_ONLY), as a detector, and as an input to BAND_HEAD with the perfect-knowledge inputs.

The arm tolerates much more than we predicted. It still beats BAND_HEAD within 7 days of a shift when it finds half the shifts, learns of each shift 3 days late, has the megawatts wrong by 50%, or raises false alarms at 1 in 2. It stops winning at 25% of shifts found. RO-NC found 33% (28 to 38) of the shifts on these worlds. As a detector at about 11 alarms per matched shift, band position finds more shifts than RO-NC on even months (37% against 25%), still below the 50% break-even. As an input it lowers BAND_HEAD's curtailment cost by under 2.5% and leaves its upper-tail score unchanged.

How to read the numbers. G5 is the rows within 7 days of a shift, and the shift rows are the rows before the alarm, during the shift, and 48 hours after it. G1 is ordinary rows, far from any shift. The upper-tail score is the continuous ranked probability score weighted towards values above the 95th percentile of earlier power (twCRPS). The scaled limit 0.5 is half the largest power the substation carried earlier. Every degraded arm is run under lab conditions: the true megawatts and the true end of each shift are used, and a Primary substation has no published limit, so cost figures compare forecasts and state no money saved. Gains are percentages of BAND_HEAD's score, and positive is better for the arm. Intervals resample whole shifts, or whole calendar months for ordinary rows, 95%.

docs.title: Break-even against BAND_HEAD
docs.text:
• Headline cell (curtailment cost, scaled limit 0.5, within 7 days of a shift): perfect knowledge gains 6.3% (4.5 to 8.1) over BAND_HEAD, the figure of experiment 297. Without D11 it gains 9.0% (6.0 to 12.2), and without D16 7.2% (4.9 to 9.6).
  • Recall: at 75% found the arm gains 4.6% (3.2 to 6.1), 50% found 3.5% (1.9 to 5.1), and 25% found 0.5% (-0.9 to 2.0). The break-even is 50%. Without D11 the 25% level wins, at 3.1% (1.0 to 5.5).
  • Delay: 6 hours gains 5.3%, 24 hours 3.7% (2.5 to 4.9), 2 days 2.1% (1.0 to 3.2), 3 days 1.4% (0.3 to 2.5), and 4 days 0.7% (-0.3 to 1.7). The break-even is 3 days, and 2 days without D16 (3 days without D16 gains 1.0%, -0.2 to 2.3). Delays of 6 to 48 half-hours act only on the rows before the alarm; the delays of 2 to 4 days also reach the rows during and after a shift.
  • Megawatt error: random errors of 25% and 50% gain 5.9% (4.1 to 7.7) and 3.7% (2.2 to 5.2), an error of 25% too high 4.7% (3.1 to 6.4), and 25% too low 6.5% (4.8 to 8.4). Every level tested wins.
  • False alarms: precision 0.75 gains 6.1% (4.2 to 7.9) and precision 0.5 gains 5.8% (4.0 to 7.7) near shifts, because the near-shift rows seldom overlap a false span (a false span avoids every shift and its 72-hour tail). On ordinary rows (G1), precision 0.75 raises the quantile score by 0.9% (0.7 to 1.1) and the cost by 0.6% (0.4 to 0.7) against the perfect arm, and precision 0.5 by 2.5% (2.1 to 3.0) and 1.6% (1.2 to 2.0). K0 plus spread alone is 2.9% (0.6 to 5.3) lower in cost than BAND_HEAD on ordinary rows.
  • All four mildly together (recall 0.5, 6-hour delay, 25% random error, precision 0.75; post hoc): 1.4% (0.1 to 2.8), and -0.4 to 2.9 without D16.
  • Upper-tail score on shift rows (before the alarm, during, and 48 hours after a shift): perfect knowledge gains 28.8% (14.3 to 41.3). The tolerances are narrower: 50% found gains 10.4% (0.4 to 20.8) and 25% found does not, a delay of 24 hours gains 13.3% (2.3 to 22.7) and 2 days does not, and a 25% random error gains 21.3% (6.6 to 33.4) and 50% does not. Within 7 days of a shift every degraded arm scores worse than, or no better than, BAND_HEAD on the upper tail (perfect knowledge -2.8%, -7.2 to +1.2), because the arms keep K0's bands.
  • RO-NC on these worlds: it found 33% (28 to 38) of the shifts, a median 48 hours after onset, with about 10 alarms per matched shift, below the recall break-even of 50%. On the even months and replicate periods of the detector comparison it found 25% (18 to 32) at 10.9 alarms per match.

docs.title: Band position and the head inputs
docs.text:
• As a detector: the thresholds were chosen on odd months to give RO-NC's rate of 12.8 alarms per match, and scored on even months. There the mean normal score found 37% (30 to 44) of shifts with a median delay of 45 hours at 11.5 alarms per match, and the mean absolute score found 28% (22 to 35) at 11.7. RO-NC found 25% (18 to 32) at 10.9 on the same months. About 90% of band position's alarms were false (912 of 987 for the mean normal score). The lower targets of 1.33, 2.0, and 2.7 alarms per match were not reached: the nearest odd-month rate was 2.9 (mean normal score) and 5.1 (mean absolute score), and on even months those thresholds gave 7.5 and 4.2 alarms per match with recall 25% and 19%. The odd-month calibration does not transfer exactly to even months.
  • As a head input (even-month origins): the upper-tail score within 7 days of a shift changes by -0.2% (-1.5 to +0.9) and the cost gains 1.6% (0.8 to 2.7). Held out (fitted on even-seed worlds only, scored on odd-seed worlds) the score changes by -1.4% (-2.9 to -0.0) and the cost gains 1.4% (0.5 to 2.3).
  • Perfect-knowledge indicators: the upper-tail score changes by +0.5% (-0.2 to +1.1) and the cost by +0.2% (-0.0 to +0.4). With the added-back megawatts as well, the score gains 2.9% (1.5 to 5.0) and the cost 1.5% (0.5 to 3.0). The 2% and 5% bars of P5 are not met, and these heads read inputs no detector has, so they are upper bounds.
  • Injector-leak controls: fitting on even-seed worlds and scoring odd-seed worlds, and fitting on shifts smaller than the median size and scoring larger ones, leave the numbers within their intervals. The injector and the real record are shared by every fit.
  • Head trained on: all 44 worlds' rows of one month parity, scored on the other, then swapped (experiment 297); ordinary rows weigh 4. The head's inputs are K0's filter level, K0's correction, lead, hour band, quarter, and the as-of ratio. Refitting reproduces experiment 297's scores exactly.

docs.title: Real record
docs.text:
• Rows: the six substations' real record with no injection, scored with the head fitted on the other month parity. These rows overlap the injected worlds' background. The 190 logged transfers touching the six series in the replicate and scored months are descriptive; the 7 transfers of the brief could not be told apart from them.
  • Ordinary rows: the head against K0 changes the quantile score by +1.1% (-1.1 to +3.7), so the head's quantile score is no worse than K0's (the interval includes zero). Readings fall below q01 in 0.9% of rows and above q99 in 0.9%, against 1.8% and 1.1% for K0.
  • After a transfer (48 hours): the head gains 4.7% (-2.7 to +13.1) over K0, and readings fall below q01 in 1.3% of rows and above q99 in 1.1% (K0: 2.4% and 1.0%). The no-correction forecast leaves 3.7% of readings above q99.
  • Experiments 264 and 209: experiment 264's rows are at D8, outside these six substations, and experiment 209's heads belong to arm D, so no placement is possible. Experiment 297's as-of widening arm is the nearest comparison, and BAND_HEAD beat it there.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
A prediction holds only if every clause of it holds, and each clause is scored separately.

  • P1 held. 50% found beats BAND_HEAD on cost and 25% found does not.
  • P2 failed. A 25% random error and a 6-hour delay beat BAND_HEAD, but so does a 24-hour delay (3.7%, 2.5 to 4.9), against the prediction that it would not.
  • P3 failed. Precision 0.75 wins, and ordinary-row cost stays within 3%, but precision 0.5 also beats BAND_HEAD near shifts.
  • P4 passed. At about 11 alarms per match band position found 28% to 37% of even-month shifts against RO-NC's 25%, with a median delay of 45 hours. Both recalls sit below the 50% break-even, and about 90% of the alarms were false.
  • P5 failed. Band position changes the upper-tail score by -0.2% (worse; the bar was a 2% improvement), and the indicators by +0.5% (better; the bar was 5%).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reproduction: the degraded arm at full quality reproduces experiment 297's PERFECT_ADD, and the refitted base head reproduces BAND_HEAD, both exactly (largest score difference 0.0 over 6,879,769 rows).
  • Median minus mean forecast, per site: for the head the median forecast's absolute error is 0.29 points lower than the mean forecast's at D16 and 0.11 lower at D11, by design. For K0 and the added-back arm it lies within 0.02 points at every site.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the contrasts: printed for every arm in the report.
  • Audit triggers that fired: a result contradicting its prediction (P2 and P3: the false-alarm cell cannot see false spans, which is the tested explanation, and the delay arm uses the true end), and leave-one-site-out (D11 and D16 move the break-even levels but not the sign of the headline contrast). A fresh Sonnet reviewer re-derived the headline contrasts; no Opus audit ran, because the brief limits the work to Sonnet.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Lab conditions. The arm uses the true megawatts and the true end of each shift. A real detector's timing, size, and recall errors are not independent of each other.
  • False alarms are drawn at random. A false span avoids shifts, carries a constant size drawn from true shifts, and is known at its onset. The cost cell near shifts cannot show the harm of false alarms; the ordinary-row figures do.
  • Band position's quantile table is in sample on odd months. The table is fitted on the odd months' rows that the heads also score, so the head-input figures for odd-month origins are optimistic; the even-month figures are the clean ones. The head folds follow the target month for ordinary rows and the onset month for shift rows, so rows within a week of a month boundary can sit on both sides of a split.
  • The indicators use the true end of each shift, so the heads fed them are upper bounds.
  • The shifts are 25% of load or more and last over a day, and the real record's own transfers inside the stream count as false alarms in the detector test.
  • Not done. BAND_HEAD with the added-back centre, a retrained LR_b20 on the injected worlds, and a head built on the added-back forecast.

docs.title: Arms and rows
docs.text:
• Arms: BAND_HEAD, K0, and PERFECT_ADD from experiment 297; 17 degraded versions of PERFECT_ADD (recall 0.25, 0.5, 0.75; delays of 3, 6, 12, 24 hours and 2, 3, 4 days; random megawatt error of 25% and 50%, always 25% too high or too low; precision 0.75 and 0.5; all four mildly); the head with band position, with the three indicators, with both, and with the indicators and the added-back megawatts, each fitted three ways (all worlds, held out, small shifts only).
  • Code reused: experiment 297's harness, scores, and head, and experiment 309's band-position method.
  • Rows and weather: experiment 297's 6,879,769 rows (411 shifts, ensemble-weather member forecasts), no retraining.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Build a detector that finds at least half the shifts, and test it by degrading nothing: run LR_b20 on the injected worlds and read its recall against the break-even of 50%.
  • Put the added-back centre under the head, so the recalibrated bands and the megawatt correction come together.

docs.title: Do an XGBoost model and a mixture-density neural network that see only weather and the calendar match the forecasts built on a physical plant model, for metered solar and wind farms?
docs.text:
A mixture-density network that sees only weather and the calendar forecasts almost as well as the plant-based forecasts, for the six metered solar farms and the three metered wind farms. The plant adds between 0% and 3.4% to the solar quantile score, and adds nothing we can measure in zero history. These results do not rule out a single weather-only model for the first production update.

In this page, "the plant" is a physical power model of one farm, "points of capacity" are percentages of the farm's capacity, and ERA5 is the ECMWF reanalysis of past weather, which arrives about 5 days late.

We asked whether predictors built from weather and calendar inputs only, with no plant model anywhere in the pipeline, match forecasts built on a plant model (a physical power model of the farm: the solar plant of experiments 218 and 287, or the wind physics core of experiment 230). We fitted XGBoost (Chen and Guestrin, 2016) and a three-component Gaussian mixture-density network (MDN, as in experiment 300) on the same rows as experiments 310 (solar, leads of 1 to 10 days) and 285 (wind). Scores are quantile scores in points of capacity (lower is better), and intervals resample the 12 scored months at 98.75%. "Own history" trains on the farm's earlier months and "zero history" on the other farms only.

The verdict is partly supported. The plan made four predictions (full text and bounds in the front matter). P1: the pure MDN scores within 2% of the plant plus MDN head in own history and at least 3% worse in zero history (solar, 12 to 36 hours). P2: the pure XGBoost is no better than the pure MDN at the 0.99 pinball loss (solar). P3: for wind, the pure MDN is within 2% of the pure XGBoost. P4: at days 8 to 10 the pure XGBoost is no better than climatology and the pure MDN is at least 5% worse than the plant-based blend (solar). P2 and P3 held, and P1 and P4 held in part. We read each bound on the point estimate and report the 98.75% interval beside it, so a bound can hold on the point estimate while its interval crosses the bound.

docs.title: Weather-only models against plant-based models, solar (own history / zero history)
docs.text:
| Day band | Pure XGBoost | Pure MDN | Plant plus MDN head | Plant plus XGBoost | Plant-based blend | climatology | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 5.60 / 5.65 | 5.34 / 5.45 | 5.36 / 5.53 | 5.50 / 5.58 | 5.30 / 5.45 | 8.64 | | 3 | 6.39 / 6.41 | 6.07 / 6.16 | 6.08 / 6.23 | 6.33 / 6.35 | 6.05 / 6.18 | 8.64 | | 6 to 7 | 8.06 / 7.93 | 7.48 / 7.53 | 7.35 / 7.48 | 7.99 / 7.87 | 7.35 / 7.45 | 8.64 | | 8 to 10 | 8.67 / 8.52 | 8.03 / 8.01 | 7.76 / 7.91 | 8.62 / 8.46 | 7.77 / 7.89 | 8.64 |

The pure blend (equal weights of the pure XGBoost and the pure MDN) scores 5.38 / 5.48 at day 1 and 8.19 / 8.13 at days 8 to 10, which is worse than the pure MDN alone, so the pure families are best used singly. The "plant plus" columns are experiment 310's stored arms: the MDN head sees seven inputs (the plant forecast, its spread, the lagged-power ratio, lagged power, a flag for missing lagged power, the clear-sky index, and lead), and the plant plus XGBoost sees the weather columns the pure XGBoost sees, plus the plant's response and lagged power. manual_heuristic scores 8.69 at day 1 and 8.83 at days 8 to 10.

docs.title: Solar results
docs.text:
• Pre-registered predictions (98.75% intervals).
    • P1 partly failed. Pure MDN minus plant plus MDN head, own history: -0.5% (-2.4 to +1.0) at day 1, within the 2% bound. Zero history: -1.4% (-3.0 to +0.4) at day 1, so the pure MDN is not 3% worse, and the bound fails.
    • P2 held. The pure XGBoost scores 0.54 at the 0.99 pinball loss against 0.31 for the pure MDN (-42.8%, -50.1 to -35.5, own history day 1), and the gap stays between -37% and -43% to days 8 to 10.
    • P4 partly failed. The pure XGBoost against climatology at days 8 to 10 is +0.4% (-6.2 to +8.0) in own history and -1.4% (-7.7 to +5.9) in zero history, so it shows no skill (the intervals straddle zero, so this is not a strict hold). The pure MDN against the plant-based blend is +3.4% (-0.6 to +8.9) in own history and +1.5% (-1.6 to +6.1) in zero history, short of the predicted 5%.
  • The plant's value, like for like. Pure XGBoost minus plant plus XGBoost: +1.8% (0.7 to 3.1) at day 1, +0.9% (0.3 to 1.6) at days 6 to 7, and +0.5% (-0.0 to +1.1) at days 8 to 10 in own history. Zero history: +1.3% (0.6 to 2.0), +0.7% (0.2 to 1.4), +0.6% (0.1 to 1.2).
  • The plant's value against the best blend. Pure MDN minus plant-based blend, own history: +0.7% (-0.6 to +1.8) at day 1, +1.8% (-1.0 to +4.7) at days 6 to 7, and +3.4% at days 8 to 10. Every interval includes zero.
  • The pure MDN keeps skill to day 10. Against climatology it is -38.2% at day 1 and -7.0% at days 8 to 10 in own history, and -36.9% and -7.2% in zero history. Against manual_heuristic it is -38.6% (-41.6 to -35.6) at day 1 and -9.1% (-15.3 to +0.2) at days 8 to 10.
  • Tails (own history, day 1 / days 8 to 10). 0.99 pinball loss: pure MDN 0.31 / 0.33, pure XGBoost 0.54 / 0.56, plant plus MDN head 0.30 / 0.34, climatology 0.43. Coverage of the 0.01 quantile: pure MDN 0.037 / 0.036, pure XGBoost 0.035 / 0.044. Coverage of the 0.99 quantile: pure MDN 0.985 / 0.987, pure XGBoost 0.990 / 0.989.
  • Lead range. The solar rows cover leads of 12 hours to 10 days, which is NGED's horizon.

docs.title: Wind results (W1 to W3 pooled, kept rows, 53 Tuesday runs)
docs.text:
Arm ERA5 weather, own ERA5, zero history Ensemble, own Ensemble, zero history Physics core 6.17 XGBoost on a binned power curve 5.86 Core with neural adapter 5.72 Pure XGBoost 5.76 7.11 11.58 11.99 Pure MDN 5.69 7.16 11.53 11.99
  • P3 held. Pure MDN minus pure XGBoost: -1.2% (-0.15 to +0.04 points) with ERA5 own history, -0.4% (-0.13 to +0.01) on ensemble weather own history, and +0.8% (-0.05 to +0.15) with ERA5 in zero history. All three point estimates are within the 2% bound. The intervals of the two ERA5 rows reach about -2.6% to +2.1% and cross the bound.
  • Against the physics core and the adapter (ERA5, own history). The pure MDN is 0.48 points (-0.71 to -0.27) below the physics core, matches the core with the neural adapter (-0.03, -0.18 to +0.05), and the pure XGBoost is 0.41 below the core (-0.60 to -0.23). Experiment 276's XGBoost with a binned-curve margin scores 5.86, 0.10 above the pure XGBoost's 5.76 (pure XGBoost minus binned-curve XGBoost: -0.10, -0.28 to +0.07).
  • Tails. 0.99 pinball loss with ERA5, own history: pure MDN 0.34, pure XGBoost 0.50, physics core 0.36, adapter 0.35. The pure MDN's 0.99 loss is 32.5% below the pure XGBoost's (-0.20 to -0.13 points).
  • Zero history is 1.4 points worse for wind (7.11 to 7.16 against 5.69 to 5.76) when the models train on the other two metered farms. Experiment 288's public wind farms were not used.
  • Ensemble weather. Experiment 285's physics core on raw members scored 11.82 and its XGBoost 11.70 on these rows, but those models trained to 2024-04-01 and these to 2025-06-17, so the comparison is not like for like and no contrast is stated.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast (points of capacity, own history, solar day 1). Pure MDN +0.56, pure XGBoost -0.95, plant plus MDN head +0.42, plant plus XGBoost -0.91. Wind with ensemble weather: -5.1 for the pure MDN and -5.3 for the pure XGBoost, the right skew of the member mixture that experiment 285 also found.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each score contrast. Pure MDN minus plant plus MDN head, own history day 1: error of the mean forecast -0.5%, score -0.5%. Pure MDN minus pure XGBoost: -5.5% against -4.7%. The directions agree, so trigger 3 did not fire.
  • Audit triggers. The triggers are the seven conditions in the ml-experiment skill's "Audit before merge" section. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its own prediction or an earlier experiment's finding) fired: P1's zero-history bound failed and contradicts experiment 300's finding that the plant helps a farm without history. We tested part of an explanation. The plant plus MDN head of experiment 310 sees seven inputs and no raw weather, while the pure MDN sees 20 weather columns, so the contrast mixes the plant with the input list. The like-for-like contrast (pure XGBoost against plant plus XGBoost, same weather columns) shows the plant adds 0.6% to 1.3% in zero history. We did not run a pure-weather MDN with the plant forecast added. A fresh Sonnet agent (not Opus, by instruction) then ran the audit: it re-derived the headline contrasts from the raw stored predictions with its own code and matched every point estimate to within 0.01 points or 0.05 percentage points. Its interval endpoints differ by up to 0.3 percentage points (own history day 1, -2.7 against -2.4), because its resampling used different draws, and no verdict changes. It confirmed that the P1 zero-history bound failed, and it found that the pure XGBoost against climatology intervals straddle zero, so that part of P4 is "no skill shown" and not a strict hold. It also confirmed that no pure column carries the plant or the farm's past power. The csi column divides the ensemble irradiance by the clear-sky irradiance of the farm's location, which is no plant output. Triggers 1, 4, 5, 6, and 7 did not fire.

docs.title: Method and caveats
docs.text:
• Inputs. Solar pure inputs are 20 columns: irradiance means and spread, 2 m temperature, sun elevation and azimuth, humidity, longwave, precipitation, pressure, 10 m and 100 m wind, 500 hPa height, the clear-sky index, lead, hour, and day of year. Lagged power and every plant-derived column are absent. Experiment 300's XGBoost used the plant forecast, its spread, and the plant's unit response, so it is not a pure comparator. Wind pure inputs are experiment 276's six wind columns plus the 2 m temperature, hour, and day of year.
  • Schedule. Solar copies experiment 310's three-monthly refits (not weekly) on its day bands, with five MDN seeds and one XGBoost fit. Wind trains once on ERA5 to 2025-06-17 as in experiment 285, applies the models to ERA5 (a ceiling, because ERA5 arrives about 5 days late) and to the 51 ensemble members, and mixes the members with equal weights and experiment 285's spread factor.
  • Calendar inputs. The hour and day of year are inputs, and no control without them was run, so some of the pure models' skill may be calendar memorisation. Experiment 310 found that dropping lagged power changed scores by under 0.6%.
  • Wind intervals resample the 12 months of the run with farms pooled, and the comparators (physics core, adapter, binned-curve XGBoost) are stored from experiments 276 and 285.
  • Seed averaging favours the pure MDN slightly. The pure MDN is scored on the average of five seeds' quantiles, while mdn_ens averages three seeds' quantiles and the wind comparators and the pure XGBoost average per-seed scores over three seeds. Averaging quantiles usually scores a little better, so the pure MDN's margins over the plant-based arms are, if anything, slightly flattered.
  • Idle rows in wind. The pure wind models train on all rows with no idle-band layer, and the physics core and adapter drop idle-band rows in training; the scores use kept rows only.
  • Not covered. Weekly refits, a pure MDN with the plant added, the public wind farms, and the curtailment-cost metric.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Run a pure-weather MDN with the plant forecast as one more input, which separates the plant's value from the input list, and test whether the plant helps more at the 0.99 tail.
  • Rerun the best weather-only models with weekly refits and without hour and day of year, which tests the schedule and calendar-memorisation caveats.

docs.title: Does a gated or pinball-trained band head pass the no-harm test that experiment 311's band head failed?
docs.text:
Caveat: only forecasts up to 7 days ahead (leads 0.5 to 168 hours) are scored, but NGED needs 1 to 10 days ahead, so days 8 to 10 are not covered. A neural network that sets the forecast bands (the 11 quantiles of demand around the median), with the current bands kept on sunny daylight half-hours, scores 0.041 points of capacity better than Primary demand research default 1 over the scored year and cannot be worse on sunny daylight half-hours (it returns the current bands there), but the gain is still almost entirely one substation, D10, so we do not adopt it.** Without D10 the gain is 0.015 points, and its 99% interval runs from -0.029 to +0.001. Training the network on the quantile score directly, instead of on a likelihood, did not help.

Experiment 311 found a mixture-density band head that lowered the quantile score by 0.037 points but harmed sunny daylight half-hours and leaned on D10. We tested two repairs on the same rows, the same monthly refits, and the same inputs. Arm G keeps the default's bands on sunny daylight half-hours and uses the head's bands everywhere else. Arm P replaces the mixture by a neural network that outputs the 11 quantiles directly (the median, then positive gaps outwards, so the quantiles never cross) and trains it on the mean pinball loss of the 11 levels. Arm GP is arm P with the same gate. The median of every arm is the default's median, so only the bands change. A quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in points (percentage points of the substation's effective capacity); lower is better. Sunny daylight half-hours are the group experiment 311 protected: daylight half-hours that the stored solar-radiation flag marks as sunny (90,143 of 561,207 rows).

Verdict partly supported. Condition 4 requires the gain to stay at or below -0.02 points when any one Primary is left out. Arm G meets condition 1 (gain), condition 2 (no harm), and condition 5 (serving). Condition 3 (replication) can only be read on the ungated heads, because the 2024-25 rows carry no sunny flag. Condition 4 (controls) fails, because leaving out D10 takes the estimate to -0.015, short of the -0.02 the condition requires. At most one arm is adopted, so nothing is added to the log of versions.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Kind and tier. kind: change, family Primary demand, default plus x against Primary demand research default 1. Tier 2 (a new fitted head, with experiment 278's feature code imported); the new-head minimum gain of 0.03 points applies.
  • Predictions. P1 held: arm G keeps 113% of experiment 311's gain. P2 held, but by construction, because arm G equals the default on every sunny daylight half-hour. P3 failed: without D10, arm G gains 0.015 points (99% interval -0.029 to +0.001) against at least 0.020 predicted. P4 held on the estimate: arm P minus experiment 311's head is +0.007 (95% interval -0.004 to +0.016), so the interval cannot rule out a 0.016 difference. The stop rule did not fire because arms G and GP pass the sunny-daylight test. Arm S (a sun-elevation-by-cloudiness input) was not run.
  • Absolute scores, six Primaries (quantile score). Default 2.579, experiment 311 head (M) 2.542, G 2.537, P 2.549, GP 2.544, BG2 2.715, manual heuristic 3.397, climatology 3.665. BG2 is the XGBoost research benchmark and not the production forecast. The default reproduces experiment 251's 2.579 (six Primaries) and 2.617 (five), so the reproduction gate passed.
  • Contrasts against the default (99.67% intervals, k = 3). G -0.041 (-0.081 to -0.012), 11 of 12 months better. P -0.030 (-0.062 to +0.006), 10 of 12. GP -0.035 (-0.066 to -0.003), 11 of 12. Against BG2: G -0.178, P -0.167, GP -0.171.
  • No-harm bounds (one-sided 95% upper bound, arm minus default). G: headline -0.023, q01 pinball -0.012, q99 pinball +0.002, cold winter nights -0.064, sunny daylight 0.000, twCRPS +1.4% relative; all pass. GP passes the same tests (headline -0.017, sunny daylight 0.000, twCRPS +1.3%). Arm P fails on sunny daylight, as experiment 311's head did (estimate +0.027, bound +0.073 against 0.05).
  • Leave-one-Primary-out, quantile score minus the default. Estimates with nothing left out and with each Primary left out, in the order none, D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16: G -0.041, -0.043, -0.050, -0.015, -0.050, -0.045, -0.045. P -0.030, -0.037, -0.038, -0.007, -0.037, -0.031, -0.031. GP -0.035, -0.037, -0.046, -0.008, -0.044, -0.036, -0.036. Each Primary alone (arm G): D10 -0.168, D5 -0.031, D14 -0.022, D16 -0.021, D9 -0.002, D11 -0.001.
  • Replicate year (even months of 2024-25, 360,122 rows). Rows carry no sunny flag, so only the ungated heads are scored, against experiment 169's stored arm A bands: M -0.034 (95% interval -0.051 to -0.016), P -0.054 (-0.069 to -0.038), resampling origin days. Both ungated heads match the sign of the main estimate and exceed 0.015. The pinball head gains more than the mixture head in this year.
  • Where the gain is (arm G). By quantile level the gain is largest at q10 (-0.013), q25 (-0.011), and q05 (-0.009). By group: cold winter nights -0.136, Economy 7 nights -0.083, Christmas -0.062, ordinary rows -0.048, leads 12 to 36 hours -0.027, bank holidays +0.013.
  • Tails, six Primaries. On sunny daylight half-hours, coverage at q05 is 0.081 for the default and for G and GP, 0.126 for M, and 0.134 for P (nominal 0.05). On cold winter nights, coverage at q95 is 0.970 for the default, 0.941 for M and G, and 0.929 for P and GP, and at q05 it is 0.110 for the default, 0.095 for G, and 0.098 for P (the figures give all four levels).
  • Rows and schedule. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, Primaries D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, leads 0.5 to 168 hours. Monthly refits on 24 rolling months, three seeds averaged, on the CPU (about 20 s per fit); the contrast could depend on this schedule because the heads were not refitted weekly. Weather at lag times is the ensemble weather available at forecast time.
  • Code reused. ml-experiments/00311-primary-demand-mixture-density-band-head/ (scoring machinery, arms, stored mixture-head forecasts and arrays) and ml-experiments/00278-stack-retraining-cadence/ (inputs). No earlier folder was edited.
  • What to try next. (1) Find what D10 has that the other five Primaries lack (experiment 220 also found a D10-specific gap), since each of the four heads gains 0.14 to 0.17 points there and about 0.015 elsewhere. (2) Add a sun-elevation-by-cloudiness input (arm S), so a head can learn the sunny regime without a gate. (3) A neural head that also reads D10's Economy 7 profile is one candidate; it would fail if D10's gain stays below 0.10 points.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus the mean forecast, per Primary (points; the mean is arm D's, and the median is the default's, which every arm shares). D10 +0.72, D11 -0.50, D14 -0.20, D16 -0.84, D5 +0.01, D9 -0.75. The mean of the 11 quantiles sits above the median by 0.02 points for the default, 0.20 for M, and 0.15 for P.
  • Error of the median beside the quantile-score contrasts. The median is the default's in every arm (asserted), so the mean absolute error of the median is identical across arms and trigger 3 cannot fire.
  • Controls. The reproduction gate passed. Arm G equals the default on every sunny daylight half-hour and equals arm M elsewhere. Arm GP equals arm P elsewhere. Every training target precedes its refit date in all 54 fits (18 refits times 3 seeds).
  • Triggers. Trigger 4 fired: leaving out D10 moves the 99% interval of arm G minus the default to -0.029 to +0.001 and fails condition 4. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the pooled contrasts, the leave-one-Primary-out contrasts, and the sunny-daylight contrast from the stored arrays with its own code and found no difference above 0.002 points; its code review found no leakage. Triggers 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, and 7 did not fire.
  • Caveats from the audit. (1) The gate was chosen because experiment 311 found harm on those rows, so "no harm on sunny daylight" holds by construction; a random 16% hold-back of rows would give about -0.031, so the gate adds about 0.010 points over a random hold-back. (2) The sunny flag comes from experiment 178's per-Primary two-thirds quantile of the PV unit shape over the whole period; whether that flag is available at forecast time was not traced, so condition 5 is not confirmed for the gated arms. (3) The replicate-year intervals resample origin days, not months, so they are narrower than month-block intervals. (4) Whether arm D's mean and scale inputs are out-of-fold was inherited from experiment 311 and not re-checked.

docs.title: Do neighbouring substations' residuals cut the false alarms of an LSC detector?
docs.text: Checking whether neighbouring substations contradict an alarm removes about a third of the 24-hour residual detector's false alarms and loses none of the real load shifts it found. A found shift is a logged real load shift that the detector flagged. Alarms per found shift fall by about a quarter, but the target was a fall of at least 25% with the whole 95% interval below it, and the interval's upper end is still 0.94 of the plain detector's rate. The two Primary substations that raise 17% to 20% of the residual's false alarms (anonymised as D8 and D9) keep the same number of false alarms. For NGED's event labels the filter is a usable improvement that needs no fitted parameter and no labels. For the forecast it does not matter, because experiment 312 showed that the forecast that adds the shifted megawatts back stays more accurate than the forecast that ignores shifts, even when half of its alarms are false. Verdict: small gain.

docs.title: Question and answer
docs.text:
We asked whether a real load shift, which moves load between two neighbouring substations, can be told from weather and forecast error by the sign of the neighbours' residuals. The detectors flag a substation (an alarm) when the mean of its last 24 hours of residual exceeds a set number of robust scales. The residual is measured power minus the forecast of GAM_ONLY, the generalised additive model without lagged power. We kept a flagged origin unless two or more interconnected, metered neighbours had a residual of the same sign and at least 25% of its size, and no neighbour had the opposite sign at that size. We scored the 35 labelled real load shifts of over 1 day on 15 Primary substations. Two of the 15 (D8 and D9) raise 17% (6 of 35) and 20% (24 of 119) of the residual's false alarms at the two alarm rates.

The filter removed 13 of 35 false alarms at the learned score's alarm rate and 36 of 119 at RO-NC's (the refit-offset neighbour-count detector), and it kept all 20 and 24 found shifts. The filter therefore cut false alarms by 30% to 37% and alarms per found shift by about 25%. The same filter on the band-position signal of experiment 309, which raised 2.3 times as many held-out false alarms as the residual, cut the band-position signal's false alarms by 43% and 37%, brought the band-position signal below the plain residual's alarms per found shift at the same threshold, and lost one found shift.

docs.title: Ceiling count (step 0)
docs.text:
• The neighbour list is experiment 37's interconnection list, limited to the 15 Primaries with a stored residual series, fixed in neighbours.json before any alarm was scored.
  • Of the 35 shifts, all have an interconnected metered neighbour and 22 have both Primaries of their logged pair metered: 15 of the 19 in the long-and-deep stratum, 7 of the other 16. The stop rule did not fire.
  • The hierarchy files were not used, because the grid-flow series above the Primaries have no stored residual series.

docs.title: Headline numbers (95% intervals resample whole shifts and whole calendar months, 20,000 draws)
docs.text:
• At the learned score's alarm rate (24-hour residual, k = 3.5 robust scales): found shifts 20 and 20; false alarms 35 and 22; megawatt-weighted share found 0.78 both; alarms per found shift in the long-and-deep stratum with a metered counterpart (9 of 15 found) 6.1 and 4.7, ratio 0.76 (0.56 to 0.94); pooled ratio 0.76 (0.57 to 0.94).
  • At RO-NC's alarm rate (k = 2.6): found shifts 24 and 24; false alarms 119 and 83; found in that stratum 10 and 10; alarms per found shift 14.3 and 10.7, ratio 0.75 (0.64 to 0.86); pooled ratio 0.75 (0.64 to 0.86).
  • Learned score and RO-NC as stored (unfiltered, pooled over all shifts): the learned score found 10 shifts at 4.0 alarms per found shift, and RO-NC found 20 at 7.3.
  • Alarms per found shift at fixed recall, read from each curve (pooled): at 18 or more found (recall 0.5), plain 2.4 and filtered 1.9 for the residual, 2.4 and 1.8 for the band position; at 12 or more found (recall 0.33), plain 2.2 and filtered 1.9 for the residual, 2.2 and 1.9 for the band position.
  • Band-position arm at the same thresholds (k = 2.8 and 2.4): false alarms 54 to 31 and 141 to 89, found shifts 22 to 21 and 26 to 25, ratio in the stratum 0.68 (0.55 to 0.84) and 0.68 (0.51 to 0.91). At recall of 0.5 its filtered alarms per found shift (1.8) are below the plain residual's (2.4); at the same thresholds the filtered band position has 2.5 and 4.6 alarms per found shift against the plain residual's 2.8 and 6.0.
  • Where the filter acts (residual, k = 2.6): of 2,485 flagged origins, 949 were confirmed by an opposite-sign neighbour, 675 were contradicted by two or more and dropped, and 861 were neither and kept. No flagged origin lacked a finite neighbour residual.
  • D8 and D9: their false alarms in the residual arm are unchanged by the filter (D8 17 and 17, D9 7 and 7 at k = 2.6; 3 and 3 each at k = 3.5). Alarms on probable unlogged events (D8's multi-day drops and the 17 block days) are counted separately and were unchanged (4 at k = 3.5, 12 at k = 2.6).
  • Not tabulated here: the split of matches between the long-and-deep stratum and the rest (printed_report.txt has it), and alarms per found shift without a metered counterpart (for example 6.0 against 3.2 with one at k = 3.5).

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
• Prediction (alarms per found shift in the stratum with a metered counterpart fall by at least 25% at equal recall, interval wholly below 0.75): not met. The ratios are 0.76 and 0.75, and the upper ends of the intervals are 0.94 and 0.86. The direction is established, so the verdict is small gain.
  • Sensitivity (not the result): a neighbour-size threshold of 10% of the alarm's size gives 21 false alarms instead of 22 at k = 3.5, and 50% gives 28 false alarms. Dropping an alarm when one neighbour contradicts it, instead of two, gives 20 false alarms at k = 3.5 but finds 18 shifts instead of 20.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, and the error of the mean forecast beside a quantile-score contrast: not applicable, because no forecast is scored.
  • Audit triggers: none fired. The result agrees in direction with its prediction and with experiment 308's neighbour check, whose different rule (a 30% size and a summed-cancellation test on a per-origin flag) found fewer shifts (17 of 35 against 20) and raised the even-month false alarm rate (2.25 against 0.91).
  • Plan review (Sonnet) and its triage are in the next section.

docs.title: Deviations and caveats
docs.text:
• Plan review, triaged. The plan review found, and I accepted, that comparing the filtered arm at the largest grid threshold that matches the plain arm's found shifts is tuned on the scored shifts, and a plain detector at a stricter threshold also cuts alarms. The headline therefore compares both arms at the same threshold, and reads the curves at fixed recall. The equal-recall read-out at RO-NC's rate (ratio 0.47, 0.34 to 0.61, run as first planned) is an artefact of that tuning and is not used. The filter rule keeps a flagged origin when any neighbour confirms, and is applied before alarms merge into episodes; That rule differs slightly from the brief's wording. I rejected using the existing neighbour check of experiment 308, whose rule differs and has a summed-cancellation test.
  • Alarms per found shift is (false alarms in ordinary rows over all months plus found shifts) divided by found shifts in the group, so false alarms are pooled over all 15 Primaries and not attributed to a group. The group ratios therefore move with the pooled false-alarm cut.
  • Odd months set the plain thresholds, and the alarm counts here span all months, so the plain arm is flattered in sample; the filter adds no fitted parameter.
  • Residuals are lab residuals. They come from the past-weather generalised additive model (GAM) of experiment 130 (ERA5 and CAMS), so a live detector with ensemble weather would see larger residuals.
  • Lead range. The detector reads recent observed power, so no forecast lead range applies.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Explain D8's and D9's false alarms, which the neighbour filter cannot touch.
  • Feed the filtered 24-hour residual to the event-label work (aim 3) as the cheap first pass.

Reuses the code of experiments 308 and 309 (folder 00309-lsc-two-forecast-gap-choosing-without-truth for the harness; experiment 308 for the 24-hour mean residual and experiment 227's stored alarms for the learned score and RO-NC).

docs.title: Is the band heads' gain at one Primary substation a night-time level error, and which single-input term of the best-guess demand model is behind its April-to-June gap to BG2?
docs.text:
Take-home: the band heads help at D10, an anonymised Primary substation, mainly by narrowing its night-time forecast bands, and not by correcting a level error. The forecast of Primary demand research default 1 sits above the actual demand at D10 at every hour, by 0.2 to 2.0 points. Adding a night-time level correction to that forecast, with no head, reproduces only 14% of the heads' gain (95% interval -16% to 99%). The heads narrow D10's night-time 5% to 95% band by 7.5 points on average, and applying only that narrowing scores 63% of the gain (42% to 116%). The second question, which family of single-input terms of the best-guess forecast trails BG2 in April to June, has a post hoc ranking that is not reliable: the sunshine response recovers 0.36 of the gap on the worst half-hours (0.30 to 0.44), but only 0.19 at one of the two Primaries, and an audit refit of the surrogate put sunshine near zero. The verdict is inconclusive, and stage 2 was not run.

Terms. The default is the stack of additive terms and neural-network layers that forecasts Primary substation demand. A band head is an extra neural-network layer that reshapes the default's forecast quantiles, and experiments 311 (mixture head, arm M) and 314 (pinball head, arm P) trained two of them. Their gain is nearly all at D10. BG2 is the production-style XGBoost forecast of experiment 87, and arm D is the best-guess stack of experiment 251. D5, D9, and D10 are anonymised Primary substations. The forecasts look 0.5 to 168 hours (7 days) ahead, short of the 1 to 10 days that the electricity distribution network operator NGED needs.

What we did. Stage 0 split D10's gain by hour and by what the head changes, and scored an as-of night offset: the median residual of the previous 28 nights, added to all 11 quantiles of D10's night half-hours (21:00 to 07:30 UTC) with no head. Stage 1 asked which family of arm D's single-input terms (sunshine, recent power, calendar, temperature, other weather) accounts for the April-to-June advantage that a depth-1 XGBoost refit (experiment 305) has over arm D. Arm D's own term contributions are not stored, so a depth-1 XGBoost surrogate of arm D's median stands in for them. A graft of family k shifts all 11 of arm D's quantiles by the refit's family-k contribution minus the surrogate's. S is the share of the refit's advantage that a graft recovers: (quantile score of arm D minus that of the graft) divided by (quantile score of arm D minus that of the refit).

Scores. Quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in percentage points of effective capacity (output relative to the substation's rated capacity); smaller is better. Gain is the default's score minus the arm's, so positive is better. Stage 0 uses the 561,207 rows (half-hours of forecast) of experiment 251 across six Primaries, 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, outside hand-filtered events, with month-block intervals (12 blocks). Stage 1 uses experiment 305's April-to-June rows with ISO-week blocks (14 weeks), because three month blocks are too few.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Stage 0: the gain is at night. Of the pinball head's D10 gain, 88% is on night half-hours (95% interval 78% to 132%), and the mixture head gives 85% (74% to 126%). The mean gain per half-hour is 0.278 points at night (0.130 to 0.456) and 0.031 by day (-0.031 to 0.098); night is 46% of D10's half-hours.
  • Stage 0: the night offset reproduces little. The offset (mean -1.13 points at night) scores 3.148 at D10 against the default's 3.169 and the pinball head's 3.024. A share of 14% of the head's gain (-16% to 99%) is under the 30% line below which the head is judged to act through another mechanism, but the interval is wide and also spans the 70% line.
  • Stage 0: the head narrows the bands. The head's median equals the default's. At night the 5% to 95% band narrows by 7.5 points on average and its centre moves up by 0.22 points. By day the band narrows by 3.5 points and the centre moves up by 0.55. Applying only the width change scores 3.077 (63% of the gain). Adding only the centre shift to all 11 quantiles, which also moves the median, scores 3.293, worse than the default (-86% of the gain, -237% to -30%). That arm is not the head's centre shift, because the head leaves the median fixed.
  • Stage 0: by level. At night the largest gains are at the 0.10, 0.25, and 0.40 quantiles (0.044, 0.057, and 0.040 points of quantile score each).
  • Stage 0: the other five Primaries together gain 0.007 points (-0.014 to 0.026) under the pinball head and 0.012 (-0.005 to 0.028) under the mixture head.
  • Stage 0: absolute D10 scores are 3.169 for the default, 3.024 for the pinball head, 3.011 for the mixture head, and 3.148 for the offset. The default's six-Primary score, 2.579, matches experiment 314's gate.
  • Stage 1, as pre-registered: the gate failed. The surrogate reproduces arm D's median with R-squared 0.82 to 0.93 (mean root-mean-square error 4.6 points). The graft added only the families' contributions and dropped each model's constant term, which differs by 12.3 points on average, so the graft of all five families moved arm D's quantiles by about -10 points. It scored S = 0.018 (-0.265 to 0.335) on the worst quarter at D5 and D9, against the 0.50 the plan required, and S = -8.3 on all daylight half-hours. The grafts of solar, lags, and calendar together scored -0.168.
  • Stage 1, post hoc level-matched graft. After a reviewer pointed out the level error, each family's contribution was averaged to zero over its site and month before grafting. On the worst quarter of April-to-June daylight half-hours at D5 and D9 (6,755 half-hours), the graft of all five families recovers S = 0.59 (0.51 to 0.66), which passes the 0.50 gate. Per family: sunshine 0.36 (0.30 to 0.44), temperature 0.15, other weather 0.14, calendar 0.01, recent power -0.06 (-0.12 to 0.00); solar, lags, and calendar together 0.38. Sunshine meets the plan's 0.30 line but not its 0.50 prediction, and lags and calendar each stay under the 0.25 prediction.
  • Stage 1: it differs by Primary and row set. The sunshine graft recovers 0.48 at D5 (0.41 to 0.56) and 0.19 at D9 (0.07 to 0.36), and 0.14 at the placebo D10 (0.05 to 0.22). On all daylight half-hours at D5 and D9 the intervals are very wide (sunshine 0.63, 0.35 to 2.56; all five 0.50, -0.72 to 0.80; recent power -1.13), so that row set cannot name a family.
  • Stage 1: the curves. Figure 4 shows the refit's recent-power response is steeper than the surrogate's (about -13 to +12 points against -3 to +8). Arm D carries recent power through its own filter, which the surrogate cannot see.
  • Stage 2 was not run. The pre-registered analysis failed its gate, and the post hoc ranking rests on one surrogate fit and one Primary. A stage 2 correction head would first need the lead replicated.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site (default, points): D5 0.01, D9 -0.75, D10 0.72, D11 -0.50, D14 -0.20, D16 -0.84.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the contrast. At D10 the mean absolute error of the median is 5.362 for both the default and the head, because the head keeps the median. The mean absolute error of the mean of the 11 quantiles is 5.680 for the default and 5.526 for the head, in the same direction as the quantile score.
  • Refit contributions. The refit's contributions sum to its raw median to within 0.0001 at some site-months and by up to 9 points at others (D5 May 2026), probably because the stored quantiles were sorted where the raw outputs cross. This was not examined.
  • Triggers that fired: a control failed (the stage 1 gate), a result contradicted its prediction (the night offset), and later experiments depend on the result (the ranked list's night-level and pooled-solar-term experiments).
  • Audit (one fresh Sonnet agent, no Opus). It re-derived the headline numbers from the stored files with its own code. The night share (0.883), the offset share (0.143), the pre-registered all-five S (0.018), the post hoc all-five S (0.592), and the sunshine S (0.363) all matched to within 0.003; interval ends differed by up to 0.045 (resampling noise). It found no leakage in the offset. It also refitted the surrogate as one pooled depth-1 model over D5 and D9 and, with its own averaging, got sunshine near 0.00 and only temperature and other weather positive, so the family ranking depends on the surrogate. This is why the ranking is labelled post hoc and unreliable above. The audit's input-column mapping was a guess and its surrogate differs from the experiment's (one model per site and month).

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• The offset's interval is wide (12 months, one substation).
  • The offset used the shortest-lead residuals of the default. A lead-matched or temperature-smooth offset was not tried.
  • The level-matched graft was chosen after seeing the failed one, so it is post hoc. It is an emulation, and the true graft needs arm D's own term contributions.
  • Stage 2 was not run because the brief's gate was not met: the pre-registered graft recovered under 0.30 for every family, and the post hoc ranking did not survive the audit refit.
  • The narrowing of D10's bands is the measured change. No coverage of the default's night bands is reported, so "too wide" is not established.
  • Candidate follow-ups: a band-width correction for D10's night half-hours without a neural head; replicating the sunshine lead at D9 and over more weeks; refitting the XGBoost with one family removed at a time.

docs.title: How far past 7 days does the Primary demand research default still beat the manual heuristic and climatology?
Take-home message
docs.text: The research-default forecast keeps real skill to 10 days, but only against climatology. Primary demand research default 1 is the demand forecast we use for research. Its convex model (an additive model with a Kalman filter on recent errors) has a 11.1% to 13.4% lower quantile score than climatology (a table of typical demand by month, time of day, and day type) at 168 to 240 hours, because the ensemble temperature forecast still carries information at 9 to 10 days. Against NGED's manual heuristic (an average of demand at the same time on earlier weeks) the gain is 5.3% to 8.5%, and its 95% interval includes zero. The gain sits in winter and at two substations, D11 and D14. On sunny daylight half-hours the convex model scores worse than both benchmarks. Verdict: partly supported. The gain over the heuristic is clearly above zero only to 168 hours.

docs.title: Question and answer
docs.text:
We asked how far past 7 days the convex model of Primary demand research default 1 still beats the two benchmarks. The demand experiments we ran earlier (136, 155, 160, 164, and 251) all stop at 168 hours. We rebuilt the convex chain of experiments 136, 155, 160, and 164 with a 240-hour forecast window and one new spread-table lead band per day. Below 168 hours the rebuilt chain reproduces the stored forecasts to within 0.00002 points. The research default beats climatology across NGED's 1 to 10 day horizon. Against the manual heuristic, the 95% interval includes zero from 168 hours.

Terms used below: the quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of effective capacity (percentage of a substation's capacity), and smaller is better. The gain is one minus the convex chain's quantile score divided by the benchmark's. Every interval is a 95% interval from resampling the 12 months of forecast date. A is the convex chain, H is the neural-network median correction of experiment 201, S is the two-number solar summary of experiment 202, and BG2 is the XGBoost best-guess forecast of experiment 87. D5 to D16 are anonymised labels of six Primary substations.

docs.title: Forecasts compared and rows scored
docs.text:
• Arm 1, default extended. Below 168 hours the stored A+H+S (the convex chain A plus the neural network's median correction H and the two-number solar summary S) scores 2.579 on six Primaries and 2.617 on five, reproducing experiment 251. Beyond 168 hours only A exists, because H was trained at day-ahead leads and S below 168 hours and neither was refitted; the plan states this. Over 0 to 168 hours H and S lower the score by 0.09 to 0.14 points in every band, so the A+H+S gain at 168 to 240 hours would probably be about 0.1 points larger. That estimate is an extrapolation, not a measurement.
  • Arms 2 and 3. The manual heuristic and climatology are experiment 87's stored forecasts, which hold leads to 351 hours on the same runs. BG2 was not extended.
  • Rows. Six Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16), runs from 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-29 at 09:00 UTC (291 origins per site; every fifth run is held out of the scored set), rows with a reading outside the hand-filtered events: 798,116 rows, 561,207 at 168 hours or less (the same rows as experiment 251) and 236,909 beyond. Rows per 24-hour band fall by 2.5% from 0 to 24 hours to 216 to 240 hours because late origins have no reading yet.
  • Weather calibration. The weather calibration has four lead bands. Its last band, 144 to 168 hours, is used for every longer lead, so days 8 to 10 use the 144 to 168 hour calibration.
  • Ensemble steps. The stored ensemble is 3-hourly to 144 hours and 6-hourly after, linearly interpolated to half-hours: 83% of half-hours to 120 hours lie on a straight line between ensemble steps, and 92% from 144 hours.
  • Retraining and lab conditions. Monthly refits of the convex model on a 24-month window, as in experiments 136 to 164. Weather is the Dynamical.org ECMWF ensemble mean, available at forecast time. No lab shortcut beyond the stored fits of earlier experiments.

docs.title: Headline numbers
docs.text:
Quantile score (points of effective capacity; smaller is better), six Primaries, with the 95% interval of the gain from resampling the 12 months of forecast date.

  • P1 (gain of at least 5% over both benchmarks in the bands to 216 hours, and a tie with climatology at 216 to 240 hours). The first half holds as a point estimate: 8.5% (168 to 192 hours) and 7.1% (192 to 216 hours) over the heuristic, and 12.1% to 13.4% over climatology.
